News.title: Sicko ‘strangles woman, 24, to death on hiking trail before killing co-worker with crossbow’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HORROR ‘KILLING SPREE’ Sicko ‘strangles woman, 24, to death on hiking trail before killing co-worker with crossbow’







Next

A MAN allegedly strangled a random woman on a hiking trail before killing his co-worker with a crossbow just days later.

Jared Schurr, 36, is charged with the murder of Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, and the murder of Woodrow Scott in a horrific “killing spree”.



Lizeht was walking her dog along Northlake Nature Center when Schurr attacked her, according to St. Tammany Parish Sheriff’s Office.

Schurr allegedly confessed to grabbing Lizeht, strangling her and dragging her body into the woodland, according to police.



Police said Lizeht, who was unknown to Schurr, was later found when a stranger stumbled upon her body “lying in the leaves.”

Schurr is also alleged to have shot his co-worker Woodrow Scott in the back with a crossbow near the Covington Country Club, according to the sheriff’s office.



Following the shooting, investigators linked Lizeht’s murder to Schurr.

According to cops, the Louisiana native was caught following a police chase across state lines into Mississippi.



He was arrested on November 13 with second-degree murder charges.

Detectives are awaiting further DNA analysis to help connect Schurr with Lizeht’s murder.

A motive for the alleged murder spree is currently unclear.

Sheriff Bret Ibert said that license plate detection cameras were crucial to tracking Schurr’s movements.

He said: “This technology was instrumental in connecting the dots between two seemingly unrelated homicides and getting a dangerous individual off our streets.”



“From the moment Lizeht’s body was found, our detectives have worked around the clock to find the person responsible for taking her life,” he said.

He added: “I am extremely proud of the dedication and determination our detectives have shown throughout this investigation.

“This case is a perfect example of how technology, good police work and partnerships with other law enforcement agencies can come together to solve a crime,” he said.

Schurr remains in custody in Mississippi and is pending extradition.

News.title: Shocking moment thug callously kicks cat into path of oncoming car as he walks down street
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a heartless thug kicks a wandering cat across the road and into the path of an oncoming car.

The horrifying attack was caught on camera on Monday morning in Halesowen.



Ring doorbell footage showed the fluffy feline strolling along Summer Hill just moments before the unprovoked assault.

An unknown couple can be seen walking up the pavement as the cat turns to lick itself.



Moments later, as the cat turns to move out of the path of the couple, the cruel man kicks the cat into the road.

The forceful boot sends the pet flying into the path of an oncoming car before the thug continues walking.

The footage was uploaded online by a concerned resident who wanted to find the man.

They reassured viewers the cat was okay and was back with its owner.



Speaking to Birmingham Live they said: “All I want is for the man to be caught.

“I have cats myself and couldn’t imagine this happening to one of them.

“The cat is harmless he’s been here for years and never bothers anyone, such a lovely cat.”

West Midlands Police have been contacted for comment.

This comes not long after an overwhelmed owner showed up to a rescue charity with more than 70 cats crammed in his boot.



The man pleaded to Hector’s House Cat Rescue “I can’t do this anymore” as the charity took the pets into their safe care.

Pictures show the fluffy faces piled up loose in the back of the car.

A total of 76 cats were relinquished to the animal rescue.

After learning there were more cats at the man’s home they organised a collection – bringing the total to 112.

Most of the felines have now been adopted out into loving homes.

News.title: Man, 42, ‘sexually assaults wife, 57, with phone after she recorded him during row’
News.content:
PHONE ‘ATTACK’ Man, 42, ‘sexually assaults wife, 57, with phone after she recorded him during row’







Next

A MAN has been arrested on suspicion of sexually assaulting his wife after she recorded him during a bitter row.

Peter Walkuski, 42, was cuffed at his lavish Florida home following an alleged incident where he forcibly assaulted her with a phone.

Walkuski launched an attack on his wife, 57, after becoming “agitated” when she pulled her phone out to record their heated argument, cops allege.

According to the criminal complaint, the suspect admitted to the alleged assault in a clip provided by the victim.





The complaint does not detail what injuries the woman suffered as a result of the altercation.

He was booked into a Pinellas County jail on Thursday in connection with the alleged incident on November 19.

Walkuski and his wife reportedly share a £1.4million luxury home on the waterfront in St. Petersburg the Tampa Bay area.

The defendant boasts a lengthy criminal past including a strangulation conviction where he was sentenced to 60 days in jail, according to the complaint.



In a separate incident in 2010, he was convicted of choking his girlfriend and sentenced to 14 months in prison.

His criminal record also includes other convictions for criminal mischief, marijuana possession and manufacturing, probation violation, and evidence tampering.

In another tragic incident in Florida, a husband gunned down his wife alongside her three children – before turning the firearm on himself.

Isaac Luechtefeld executed his wife and their three kids – aged just one, three and five – in a bloody triple murder last Thursday.



Emergency dispatchers heard one youngster screaming, “daddy, please don’t kill me,” just before a loud gunshot rang out.

Minutes later, cops raced to the home in Plant City, Florida, where they conducted a perimeter search and spotted a lifeless child lying on the floor.

Inside, deputies made the harrowing discovery of a man, a woman and three young children dead from apparent gunshot wounds.

Days before the sickening massacre, Raquel celebrated her husband online after he was praised in a magazine for his work as a mechanic.

She wrote: “So proud of my hubby! He was one of the master techs featured in the Kenworth Diesel magazine release!”



Luechtefeld was described by colleagues as “someone that just about everyone in our shop looks to for guidance and assistance with their repairs and diagnostics” in the article.

The Sunshine State recorded 71,125 domestic violence related offences in 2024, according to Florida’s health agency.

News.title: ‘World’s most wanted’ OnlyFans model Vera Dijkmans deported from America after ‘mistreatment’ in ICE custody
News.content:
BOOTED OUT ‘World’s most wanted’ OnlyFans model Vera Dijkmans deported from America after ‘mistreatment’ in ICE custody







Next

AN OnlyFans star has been deported after spending days locked up in an ICE detention centre.

Vera Dijkmans, 29, claims she endured unimaginable “mistreatment” during her 11-day stay inside a New Jersey immigration facility.



The Dutch model was deported back to the Netherlands on Sunday after she was cuffed on a flight from Miami on November 11.

The star who labelled herself the “world’s most wanted girlfriend”, claims she was bundles into a blacked-out van with no explanation after landing in Newark ahead of a major UFC event.



While locked-up, she was reportedly subjected to insufficient food, unsanitary conditions and days without exposure to sunlight while detained, according to her mother.

On Monday, the model said: “I’ve seen and experienced things I never imagined I would have to face.



“The mistreatment I endured behind prison walls was beyond anything I could have ever imagined.

“Some things are difficult for me to put into words and will stay with me forever.



“Grateful to finally be home int he Netherlands, grateful for all the people who stood by me, and above all grateful to have my freedom back.”

Homeland Security officials alleged Vera was a serial offender who repeatedly violated immigration policy and evaded officials for years.

Meanwhile, she flaunted her unauthorised travel around the US to her nearly six million Instagram followers and 875,000 OnlyFans subscribers.



The model was staying in the US on a tourist visa, which does not permit visitors to work, according to her mother.

According to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Vera entered the US “lawfully” in 2024 but remained in the country past her visa expiration.

She also missed a May court date following the 2025 launch of removal proceedings, according to DHS.

In 2019, she was deported after trying all illegally enter the US through a Dallas airport, officials said.

A DHS spokesperson said: “She chose to overstay her welcome in defiance of our nation’s laws.”



US Immigration and Customs Enforcement did not immediately respond to a request from the NYPost for comment on the models’ “mistreatment” allegations.

The model is “severely weakened” from the ordeal and will reportedly need time to recover “physically and mentally”, according to her mother as reported in Dutch media.

Prior to her arrest, the star was heading to New York City to attend UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden, where she planned to create content with fighters, her family said.

Dijkmans previously made headlines after claiming that 5,000 men had applied to become her boyfriend.

The social media star later revealed that she had strict expectations for men hoping to take her out.



“If they don’t suggest an impressive first date, I won’t bother going,” she told the Daily Mail in January 2025.

“And he should bring you a gift, too.”

“I’ve received things like expensive clothing – including from Louis Vuitton and Hermès – but it’s mostly about the gesture. A bouquet with flowers would also be OK.”

However, despite the thousands of applications, the outlet reported that no romance had developed.

News.title: Cops probe link between ‘tear gas released in crowd’ & jewellery robberies during Manchester Don Toliver gig
News.content:
Next

COPS are probing a link between the suspected release of tear gas and a spate of jewellery robberies at a Don Toliver gig.

A woman was rushed to hospital and 88 others were treated after the substance was released into a crowd during the show on Sunday evening.



Thousands of fans were evacuated from Manchester‘s Co-op Live arena amid chaotic scenes after the incident sparked a major emergency response.

Cops are now exploring the possibility the incident could be linked to a “small number of robbery offences” at the venue that evening.



Greater Manchester Police said the force had received nine reports of jewellery being stolen at the same concert.

They added “similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist”.



No arrests have been made at this time.

Following scenes of carnage, cops later revealed that a total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure.



One woman was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment and treatment.

The remaining 88 underwent dry decontamination at the scene before being moved into the Etihad Stadium while the incident was dealt with.

Footage captured by revellers shows fans streaming out of the venue, covering their mouths and coughing.

Videos circulating online also show police cars and vans surrounding the arena as emergency crews and officers rushed to the scene.

Other pictures from the aftermath show hundreds of concertgoers gathered in huddles on the venue floor.



US rapper Don Toliver – who was forced to postpone a gig at the London’s O2 – spoke out following the terrifying scenes.

In a post on Instagram, he said: “I’m very sad to sit here and say I have to reschedule The O2 London show to December 15 due to the unfortunate incident last night in Manchester.

“I just want to make sure everyone is safe and the next show goes on properly.



“My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night at Co-op Live.

“The only thing I love more than creating music is performing to my fans. “See you soon London, love you guys.”

Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said tonight: “We know that what happened on Sunday night and the imagery seen on social media will bring back painful memories of 2017.

“Thankfully, we are not dealing with an incident of such a devastating nature or motive and we maintain our belief that, based on the information available to us now, there is no wider ongoing risk to the public.

“We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending.



“We’ll also continue to work closely with the venue and local authority partners over the coming weeks as events begin to return to the Co-Op Live arena.

“I’d like to thank everyone who attended the concert on Sunday evening for their patience and cooperation while emergency services responded.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He urged anyone who attended the concert and has since developed symptoms or become unwell should attend their local hospital.

Co-op Live, which officially opened in 2024, has a capacity of 23,500, making it the UK’s largest indoor arena.

News.title: Massive search underway as man goes overboard off Royal Caribbean cruise ship while on vacation in Bahamas
News.content:
Next

A MASSIVE search has been launched after a man went overboard from a Royal Caribbean ship just one day into a cruise.

The passenger was sailing on a Thanksgiving voyage on the Allure of the Seas when he went overboard on Monday.



The incident happened near San Salvador Island in the eastern Bahamas the day after the cruise left Miami for an eight-day trip to the islands.

It was the cruise’s first full day at sea after departing from Miami on Sunday.



Kat Geary, who was aboard the eight-day Caribbean cruise, told The U.S. Sun that the first announcement about the missing man was made on Monday afternoon.

Geary said the message was repeated several times over the ship’s loudspeakers throughout the day.



“Towards the late afternoon/evening, staff came door to door knocking and asking if we’d seen the man in the photo,” she said.

“We did not recognize him. There are thousands of people on board and it was only the first day.”

The lack of information initially frightened one of her daughters, who feared something sinister had happened on the ship.

However, Geary said her family felt safe and praised the crew for keeping passengers informed.



“The boat feels very safe. The cruise has done a good job of keeping us up-to-date as the story evolved,” she said.

The captain subsequently informed guests that the ship was searching for the missing man.

Tracking data showed the cruise ship reversing course and repeatedly circling an area north of the island.

The US Coast Guard said it was notified of the emergency at around 11:30 pm on Monday.

The Royal Bahamas Defence Force is leading the rescue operation with assistance from the Coast Guard.



A maritime emergency alert identified the missing passenger as a 40-year-old man who was last seen wearing a gray T-shirt and blue shorts, according to Cruise Fever.

Other vessels in the area have been asked to watch for the man and report any sightings.

Royal Caribbean confirmed it was working with local authorities to locate the passenger.

The man’s name has not been released, and it remains unclear how he went overboard.

The Allure of the Seas was heading to Philipsburg, St. Maarten, when the emergency forced the crew to change course.



The ship was also scheduled to visit St. Thomas in the US Virgin Islands and Puerto Plata in the Dominican Republic.

It was originally due to return to Miami on Sunday, November 29.

The rescue operation has disrupted the ship’s itinerary, and passengers have been informed of changes to their scheduled stops.

It comes two years after another passenger went overboard from the same cruise ship.

Dulcie White disappeared during a Taylor Swift-themed cruise in October 2024 after falling from her balcony.



Her family subsequently sued Royal Caribbean, alleging that its unlimited drinks package encouraged excessive alcohol consumption and that employees overlooked warning signs before she went overboard.

White’s body was never found, and the lawsuit remains ongoing.

News.title: Sobbing Brit gran, 43, blasts ‘there’s NO help from UK!’ as she’s held by Turkish cops for 4 months after hotel bust-up
News.content:
Next

A SOBBING Brit gran battling to get home to the grandson she has raised since he was born has blasted British authorities, claiming the UK “refused to help” her.

Ann Beattie, 43, has been trapped in Turkey for four months since being slapped with a travel ban while on holiday after a hotel bust-up.



She is still stuck in legal limbo after a fight between her and another holidaymaker in the summer led to her arrest.

The gran claimed she was attacked when looking for her nine-year-old grandson at Orka World Hotel, Fethiye.





She is desperate to be reunited with him in time for Christmas, saying the little boy is “really suffering the most in all of this”.

Ann, of Stratford, East London, is the legal guardian for her grandson because of how young her daughter was when she had him.

Speaking on The Sun’s From the Newsroom, the gran claimed UK authorities did not help when she explained her situation, saying: “I contacted the British government, they refused to help me.

“They’re saying that there’s nothing they can do about it, even though we’re well aware they can do something to help in this situation.”



Ann wants the British government to “put a little bit of pressure on to onto the prosecutor to make a decision”, not to “interfere in the case”.

The ordeal began after her grandson had briefly gone missing after playing football with new friends.

Ann said she had “started worrying” and was frantically searching for the child, “calling out his name” when a woman began to yell at her and her daughter.



She explained: “Some lady started yelling over the balcony, telling my daughter to shut up.”

They kept looking for the boy, Ann said, when all of a sudden “the woman’s come running out to try and attack me and my daughter”.

The gran said the woman kicked her, and, defending herself, she punched the woman “once”.

She said the altercation “wasn’t a big scrap or anything, it was just one hit and she fell to the floor” and “hurt herself”.

“I felt like I just had to defend myself, I didn’t know what to do,” Ann said.



She eventually found her grandson, but when cops were called she was hauled in and arrested.

The woman, a Slovakian national, was treated in hospital for a broken nose.

But she has since vanished, the gran said, with Turkish authorities unable to find any evidence of her arriving or leaving the country.



Ann has been banned from leaving Turkey while prosecutors begin an investigation ahead of a potential criminal case.

Speaking through tears, Ann said she was left in a “difficult situation” with her family “severely affected” because she is the main breadwinner.

She revealed she has never had a mum and has recently lost her dad, but is most worried about her grandson because “it’s affecting his school”.

The gran said: “The most important thing is getting home to my family more than anything.

“Nobody’s helped me. Not the British government, not anybody.



“We’re doing this our own selves with our own money.”

Ann said facing Christmas without her grandson “breaks her heart”.

“Surely the court can have some compassion and let me go back to spend time with him,” she said.

She has no idea when she could be allowed back to the UK, or when any trial will take place.

Ann faces a minimum four years’ jail if convicted.



Her lawyer Çağlar Akdeniz said: “This case requires particular sensitivity because she is responsible for the care and legal guardianship of her grandchild.

“That is the biggest issue. Because she cannot return, the child is experiencing difficulties.”

Despite that, the court has still not allowed Ann home to be with her grandson, who is being looked after by her partner.

The family has spent £20,000 flying out to see her regularly on weekends.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

An FCDO spokesperson said: “We are supporting a British national in Turkey and are in contact with the local authorities.”

News.title: Pregnant Iranian teen ‘murdered by her parents as she’s forced to swallow dozens of pills before being beaten to death’
News.content:
VILE ‘HONOUR KILLING’ Pregnant Iranian teen ‘murdered by her parents as she’s forced to swallow dozens of pills before being beaten to death’







Next

A PREGNANT Iranian teen was allegedly murdered by her own parents who forced her to swallow dozens of pills before beating and suffocating her.

Helia Fattahi, 19, had told her family just days earlier that she was two months pregnant following a relationship with a young man.



Her parents, Voria Fattahi and Leila Veisi, reportedly went to court on Saturday to lodge a complaint against their daughter.

But what allegedly unfolded when they returned to their family home in the western Iranian city of Sanandaj was horrific.



The couple forced Helia to swallow around 30 anticonvulsant pills before subjecting her to a savage beating, according to the Hengaw Organisation for Human Rights.

When they realised their daughter was still alive, they allegedly smothered her with a pillow.

Both parents reportedly confessed to killing the teenager when emergency medics arrived at the house.

Police arrested the pair later that day.

Shahram Abdi, head of criminal police in Kordestan province, confirmed on Tuesday that both parents had confessed during questioning.

Cops cited “family disputes” as the motive behind the killing.



But human rights groups Hengaw and Hana have branded the teenager’s death a so-called “honour” killing.

Police and Hengaw identified Helia as 19, while Hana reported she was just 16.

Authorities have not commented on her pregnancy or the manner in which she was killed.

Hana also accused Iranian news outlet Rokna of digitally adding a hijab to a photograph of the slain teenager before publishing it without credit.



Helia’s death is the third killing of a young woman or girl to spark nationwide attention in Iran in little over a week.

On November 18, Sadaf Haghbin, 23, was shot dead at her own birthday party in the northern province of Gilan.

Her former boyfriend was reportedly behind the killing after she refused to marry him, according to Iranian news outlet Khabaronline.

Just days earlier, the body of 16-year-old schoolgirl Sogand Sayyadi was discovered in the courtyard of her apartment block in Kermanshah.



The youngster had desperately warned school staff that her father would hurt or even kill her if she was sent home with him.

Her dad, Kioumars Sayyadi, had allegedly been summoned to the school after staff discovered she was in contact with a prospective suitor he disapproved of.

He allegedly battered his daughter in front of horrified classmates and teachers.

The vicious assault reportedly continued outside the school, where he repeatedly slammed her head against a wall.

Hengaw claims the father murdered his daughter the following day by hurling her from the fifth floor of their apartment block.



A coroner confirmed the schoolgirl died from injuries sustained in the fall, with the circumstances still under investigation.

Her father was detained on suspicion of assault and murder, while the school’s principal was arrested on suspicion of negligence.

The principal has denied that Sayyadi’s father was summoned over her choice of partner.

Education officials instead claimed he had arrived to collect her academic records and arrange her transfer to another school.

Sayyadi had lived with her father and stepmother since her parents separated several years earlier.



Her dad had allegedly barred her from having any contact with her mother.

In another chilling case, 16-year-old Nesa Alizadeh was allegedly strangled to death by her father on October 29.

The schoolgirl had fled her home after her family opposed her plans to marry a man of her choosing.

Relatives reportedly dragged her back home before her father killed her over the perceived “dishonour” she had brought upon the family.

He then allegedly attempted to rush through her burial.



But suspicious cops ordered a forensic examination, which exposed strangulation as the cause of her death.

Her father later confessed to the killing during questioning following a complaint from her mother.

The spate of killings has laid bare the alarming scale of violence against women and girls across Iran.

At least 84 were killed between March 21 and October 13 this year, according to figures compiled by Iran International.

In 75 cases, the perpetrators were known to their victims.



Twelve of those killed were under 18, with eight murdered by fathers, brothers or other blood relatives.

Hengaw recorded at least 207 femicides across Iran in 2025, including 31 suspected so-called “honour” killings.

At least 13 women were killed after rejecting marriage proposals, while ten were murdered after seeking a divorce.

Another ten were victims of child marriage who were killed by their husbands.

Yet a glaring loophole in Iran’s Islamic Penal Code allows some fathers who murder their own children to escape the punishment handed down to other killers.



Under Article 301, fathers and paternal grandfathers are exempt from qisas – or retaliatory execution – for killing their children.

The exemption does not extend to mothers.

Some estimates suggest at least 450 so-called “honour” killings take place across Iran every year.

But the true scale of the bloodshed remains unknown, with countless cases feared to go unreported or be wrongly recorded.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The killings have reignited desperate calls for legislation to protect Iranian women and girls from violence.



A bill designed to offer such protection has been passed between government bodies for more than 15 years without becoming law.

News.title: Tragedy as popular wolf Lup whose howl was adored dies at Port Lympne Safari Park
News.content:
Tragedy as popular wolf Lup whose howl was adored dies at Port Lympne Safari Park

Lup, who moved to Port Lympne Safari Park near Hythe, Kent in 2015, had a tumour in his spleen, which had spread to his liver, keepers at the attraction said

View 2 Images Lup (pictured on the right) arrived at Port Lympne Safari Park in 2015 (Image: Port Lympne Safari Park/Cover Images)

Emotional tributes have been paid to a much-loved wolf who has died at a safari park.

‌



‌



Keepers say Lup, aged 11, will be greatly missed after his sudden passing, following a large tumour in his spleen, which had spread to his liver. The wolf arrived at Port Lympne Safari Park, near Hythe, Kent, from the Netherlands in 2015, where he was reunited with two fellow European grey wolves, his brothers Lobo and Vuk.

‌



The trio were adored by guests and keepers at the safari park, which attracts more than 400,000 visitors each year. Lup's distinctive howl was often heard echoing from the Wolf Lodge enclosure across different parts of the park, management said.

‌

News.title: Publisher HarperCollins accused of 'covering up' David Walliams allegations of inappropriate behaviour
News.content:
Publisher HarperCollins accused of 'covering up' David Walliams allegations of inappropriate behaviour

David Walliams, who denies the claims, worked HarperCollins on a number of best-selling books

View 2 Images David Walliams has been hit with a number of allegations of inappropriate behaviour, which he denies. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Book publisher HarperCollins has been accused of attempting to "cover up" allegations of inappropriate behaviour by David Walliams, despite years of complaints from women to the company's management.

‌



‌



The latest claims, published by the Guardian and ITV News, allege the company used a leading legal firm and a non-disclosure agreement to keep the accusations secret.

‌



One author, who is currently represented by the publisher, told the news organisations: "I certainly believe that there has been a cover-up. They tried to shut women up and keep their story under wraps."

‌



View 2 Images David Walliams at the the 2023 Mediterrane Film Festival. (Image: Getty Images)

She added there were "so many red flags" about his behaviour, and that she was aware other authors had raised concerns.

"We knew that he [Walliams] was being protected because he was a valuable asset," she said.

‌



Walliams has been accused of using his celebrity status to "groom" and prey on young women and teenagers as young as 15 for sex.

The Metropolitan Police is now investigating the TV star after the force received allegations of serious sexual offences - separate to those made in ITV News and the Guardian's reporting.

‌



The force said it has received a number of non-recent allegations against the former Britain's Got Talent (BGT) judge.

Walliams previously denied all allegations against him, including any criminality.

‌



Former staff told ITV and the Guardian that senior management were repeatedly told of concerns about Walliams' behaviour, but that nothing was done.

The concerns raised included that Walliams had an "inappropriate" sexual relationship with a woman who was an intern when he first met her, had inappropriate interactions with at least three other women connected to the company including asking two for dates, and approached a girl who appeared to be in her teens at a book signing event.

‌



Charlie Redmayne was the CEO of HarperCollins, between 2013 and 2025.

In 2023, the company brought in the City law firm Allen & Overy to investigate the allegations.

‌



Several former employees told ITV and the Guardian they believed the inquiry was a means to shut down complaints, while one said: "It was not an inquiry, it was a cover-up."

Walliams has not yet responded to the reporting published by The Guardian or ITV News.

‌



In a letter understood to have been sent several months ago to journalists working on the investigations, the television personality denied being a "sexual predator".

He said he recognised he "behaved thoughtlessly" at times, and regretted not taking people's feelings "properly into account", but insisted he had not broken the law.

‌



The publication of allegations against Walliams comes after his unsuccessful attempts to seek an injunction to prevent the media revealing his identity - with his lawyers arguing there was a risk he would take his own life after two previous suicide attempts.

HarperCollins dropped Walliams last year. The company has been contacted for comment.

‌



A statement from the publisher released last week after the first allegations against Walliams emerged said: "HarperCollins UK previously terminated its publishing relationship with David Walliams.

"We take the safety of our people incredibly seriously and to respect the privacy of individuals we do not comment on employee matters."

Article continues below

The previous allegations led to Walliams being dropped by his literary agency, Independent Talent Group, while the BBC started to remove his programmes, including Little Britain, from iPlayer, and his Labour Party membership was suspended.
