News.title: Todd Blanche erupts over questions about investigations into Jensen Huang: ‘What does that mean? For what?’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Attorney General Todd Blanche refused to say whether Nvidia’s newly reinstalled CEO Jensen Huang was under federal investigation or posed any risk to national security before Donald Trump pressured the company’s board to bring him back to the artificial intelligence giant.

Blanche told reporters Tuesday that the president “talked to a lot of people going into the decision” and was “exactly right.”

“To the extent that the Department of Justice had information he was committing crimes, or something like this, that’s something I would’ve certainly told the president, if it were true,” Blanche said.

The DOJ head then erupted over what he called “hypothetical questions” about investigations into the embattled CEO.

“What does that mean? Had Huang been investigated? For what? I don’t understand the question,” Blanche said.

Huang resigned earlier this month following news of his affair with an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is allegedly tied to Chinese intelligence agencies.

open image in gallery Attorney General Todd Blanche repeatedly rebuffed questions about Nvidia and Jensen Huang after Donald Trump claimed the embattled CEO has been ‘exonerated’ over investigations into whether the AI giant violated export controls or if Huang posed a risk to national security ( AFP/Getty )

Last week, the Department of Justice and Commerce Department issued a joint public statement indicating they were investigating Megaspeed for possibly diverting advanced Nvidia semiconductor chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls.

But on his Truth Social account Monday, Trump claimed that the “Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”

During an hourlong interview with CNBC that morning, as he celebrated his intervention with Nvidia’s leadership, Trump was asked what Blanche told him about Jensen Huang’s potential exposure to criminal liability .

“They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated,” Trump told the network.

Blanche said the Justice Department is handling “hundreds, if not more” export investigations and insisted that he had no idea what reporters meant when they questioned him about the Justice Department’s previous statements about Nvidia.

“I don’t know if there’s going to be an investigation that starts tomorrow that will lead to different results,” he said. “I can’t talk about a particular investigation, for one, and there are many investigations ongoing.”

open image in gallery Trump claimed his government ‘did a pretty good investigation’ into Huang despite warnings about his potential exposure to criminal liability for export controls and national security risks following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy ( Getty )

Blanche said reports that the president had assured Nvidia that the Justice Department would not be prosecuting anyone at the company in an effort to return Huang as CEO is based on the “public reporting of leaks.”

“I don’t deal in leaks,” he said. “We have to deal in facts. … I do think there’s a lot of baked-in assumptions about the situation that are baked in from reporting, from leaks … That certainly makes it more challenging for folks to understand what really happened.”

Asked whether he is satisfied with Nvidia’s response to federal law enforcement, Blanche called Nvidia a “good corporate citizen” but refused to acknowledge widely published reports about potential threats to national security and whether the company played a role violating export restrictions.

“I don’t know what folks are asking about specifically,” he said. “You’re mocking me … but what are you asking about? … You guys are asking me to comment about investigations to the extent that they exist … The president is free to talk about what he wants to talk about.”

Trump called into a meeting of Nvidia’s board of directors to “convince” them to reinstate Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO, the president admitted Monday.

“I spoke to them and I convinced them,” he told CNBC during a nearly hour-long on-air call Monday morning. “And it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week ago.”

The president said he believes his unprecedented intervention was “very important” in the wake of the scandal, which will now be the subject of several congressional investigations.

“We gave him assurance, at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” Trump told CNBC. “People say, ‘is it a threat to have him?’ No, it’s a threat to lose him.”

News.title: ‘Unknown substance’ released at US rapper’s Manchester gig could be linked to robberies, police say
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An "unknown substance" that sparked a mass evacuation at a US rapper’s concert in Manchester could be linked to robberies and reports of jewellery being stolen, police say.

The Co-op Live Arena was evacuated during Rapper Don Toliver’s show and a major incident declared on Sunday night, with concertgoers describing a “horrible smell”, which police initially believed to be tear gas.

According to Greater Manchester Police (GMP), 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure.

One woman was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment and treatment.

The major incident was declared in the early hours of Monday and police said on Tuesday that the scene had been lifted.

GMP said that, as part of progressing enquiries, detectives are exploring the possibility that release of the substance could be linked to reports of a small number of robbery offences at the arena on Sunday evening.

It comes after the force received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the same concert. No arrests have been made at this time.

Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said: "We know that what happened on Sunday night and the imagery seen on social media will bring back painful memories of 2017.

"Thankfully, we are not dealing with an incident of such a devastating nature or motive and we maintain our belief that, based on the information available to us now, there is no wider ongoing risk to the public.

"We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending.

"We'll also continue to work closely with the venue and local authority partners over the coming weeks as events begin to return to the Co-Op Live arena.

"I'd like to thank everyone who attended the concert on Sunday evening for their patience and cooperation while emergency services responded.

"We're continuing to advise anyone who has developed symptoms or become unwell since attending the event to seek advice from their GP, NHS 111, or to attend their local hospital if necessary."

News.title: Anthropic falls below stock market listing price
News.content:
Anthropic’s shares dropped below their initial public offering price for the first time, sealing a dramatic reversal of fortunes for the AI giant following its blockbuster stock market debut last week.

The Claude chatbot maker saw its shares fall more than 8pc from their $83 offer price to stand at around $76 as investors appeared to grow sceptical of its valuation.

The slide on the Nasdaq exchange was set to wipe over $200bn from the company’s market value.

Anthropic raised more than $81bn in the biggest IPO on record, with its valuation surging to $2tn as the shares peaked at around $115.

But the company bucked Monday’s huge rally following Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia with the shares slipping from Friday’s close.

Wall Street resumed its slide on Tuesday as underlying fears over the AI trade appear to have outweighed the impact of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as chief executive.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 was down as much as 3pc, with the benchmark S&P 500 around 1.2 pc lower.

In London, the FTSE 100 closed slightly lower, down 0.1pc, unable to sustain gains made in global markets on Monday.

The ability of AI companies to generate sufficient returns on their massive investment has proved more important than Nvidia’s boardroom drama, according to Goldman Sachs analysts.

Sharon Bell told Bloomberg: “The AI trade really depends on whether companies can make a return on the capex they spend.

“If the answer is yes, then the tech sector should do well over time and if the answer is no, it won’t do so well.”

Ms Bell argued that the management changes at Nvidia would not “make a huge difference either way”.

Glenn Yin at online trading platform ACCM told the Reuters Global Markets Forum: “By the end of ​the day, these businesses need to make enough money to justify investors’ expectations.

“‌My point is: Jensen’s return does not solve this. So, the sentiment is more emotional than sensible, in my opinion.”

Major chipmakers saw their stocks sink on Tuesday as general AI-related optimism faded.

Nvidia, the world’s largest chipmaker, saw its stock fall more than 7pc, while the Philadelphia semiconductor index, which tracks the major US manufacturers of chips, fell 8pc.

Microchip maker AMD’s share price was down as much as 10pc, while shares in Broadcom were down around 3pc.

The dollar eased back from its highest level in almost two years after Jensen ​Huang’s return to Nvidia revived the AI rally and fuelled expectations of more interest rate rises.

The President’s intervention, however, is a “slippery slope”, according to a top Republican senator.

Dave McCormick, the former boss of hedge fund Bridgewater, told Bloomberg: “I am worried about the precedent of the executive branch getting involved in real ownership deals with companies but also in board governance and making these decisions.

“This is a precedent that I don’t think we want to replicate or reinforce.”

Mr McCormick will be one of the politicians grilling the Nvidia boss next week when he testifies before the Senate Banking Committee.

Todd Blanche, the US Attorney General, has labelled Nvidia “a good corporate citizen” despite questions over whether Jensen Huang’s alleged affair could have threatened national security.

Mr Blanche added that if Nvidia was the target of a criminal investigation, “that wouldn’t be the message”.

News.title: Meningitis outbreak triggers epidemic alert in Gaza
News.content:
Cases of meningitis have risen dramatically in Gaza and have triggered an epidemic alert, the territory’s health ministry has said.

At least 272 cases were recorded across the enclave in October, more than eight times the usual monthly rate of 30 to 50 cases, Dr Nidal Ghoneim, a senior health ministry official, told a press conference on Tuesday.

Children under one year old account for 71 per cent of cases, with newborns alone accounting for 13 per cent, World Health Organization (WHO) spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said in a separate briefing.

Dr Ghoneim added that 15 Palestinians had died of meningitis since the start of the year, and that the spread of the disease through the strip threatened the lives of thousands of people, mostly children.

It is thought that most cases are being driven by enterovirus – the leading cause of viral meningitis – which is shed through faeces and can spread rapidly between people in unsanitary environments.

All six wastewater treatment plants in Gaza are currently out of operation, meaning an estimated 150,000 cubic metres of untreated sewage flows into the environment every day, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

News.title: Trapped Ebola health workers rescued after three days of fighting in Congo
News.content:
Ebola health workers have been rescued after being trapped by fighting for more than three days, in clashes further hampering efforts to curb the virus in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, head of the World Health Organization, said staff had been evacuated from a hospital in Akwe, Ituri province, “under very challenging circumstances”.

The health chief had earlier pleaded for peace, and warned staff had “been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward of the facility for over 24 hours”.

Staff were caught in a crossfire between the Congolese army, and the People’s Revolutionary Convention (CRP) group led by former International Criminal Court (ICC) convict, Thomas Lubanga, French RFI radio reported.

Local media reported heavy clashes between the army and the CRP in Ituri in recent days. At least 10 people were killed and a stream of refugees fled to the provincial capital, Bunia.

As security worsened, the WHO said it had relocated health teams from Mongbwalu.

News.title: Welsh slogger blasts England to crushing win over Australia
News.content:
It will take more than a few lusty blows to become the cricketing Don in these parts, but an extraordinary display of six-hitting from Aneurin Donald, ably supported by Phil Salt, helped England and Wales to a stunning eight-wicket victory over Australia.

Donald and Salt, the Welsh-born opening pair, put on 151 to help chase down Australia’s 184 with 41 balls to spare. David Gower famously flew a pre-war Tiger Moth between the floodlights, about 200 feet above the ground, on England’s only previous visit to this ground in 1991. It was a good thing he was doing no such thing tonight, with balls flying everywhere off Donald’s blade. He hit nine sixes, one shy of Salt’s England T20 record, in his 85 from 32 balls, before being caught on the fence with the game as good as won.

Donald, who turns 30 next month, has taken the slow road to the big stage. As a teenager, he smashed 234 off 136 balls for Glamorgan against Derbyshire in the County Championship at Colwyn Bay, but at 21 left for Hampshire. Two serious ACL injuries derailed his career, and he moved to Derbyshire in 2023, where he has turned into a formidable T20 opener.

“I am pretty decent at slogging and not too good at batting, so I will keep swinging as hard as I can,” he reflected afterwards. “Luckily there might be a career in it now, not a few years ago.”

News.title: Just 1pc of research funding spent on maternal death prevention, analysis suggests
News.content:
Only one per cent of research funding is spent on preventing leading causes of maternal deaths, analysis suggests.

Just $306 million (£233 million) was spent between 2023 and 2025 on tackling the four leading causes of maternal and child mortality in low-and-middle-income countries, according to a joint report by the non-profits Program for Appropriate Technology in Health (Path) and Impact Global Health.

The four causes are: postpartum haemorrhage, the loss of more than 500 ml of blood within 24 hours after birth; pre-eclampsia, new-onset high blood pressure and organ stress during pregnancy; maternal anaemia, when a women doesn’t have enough red blood cells to carry oxygen around her body and to her baby; and pre-term birth.

The greatest need is in sub-Saharan Africa, which accounts for around 70 per cent of maternal deaths globally. Some 182,000 women in the region died of pregnancy complications in 2023, according to the World Health Organization.

Funding for maternal health research and development (R&D) is notoriously fragile. Between 2023-25, the US National Institutes of Health and the Gates Foundation provided three quarters of funding to tackle the four leading maternal mortality conditions. Industry contributed just one per cent.

“A single shift in one funder’s priorities could reshape the whole field,” said Sabastine Wakdok, director of research at Impact Global Health.

“The women carrying the greatest risk deserve a far broader and more stable base of investment,” he said.

News.title: Wall Street stocks soar as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
News.content:
Follow the latest on Jensen Huang’s Nvidia return

US tech stocks staged a dramatic recovery on Monday after Nvidia’s shock decision to reinstate Jensen Huang.

The value of the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained nearly $2 trillion as investors rushed back into AI-linked companies following a bruising sell-off last week.

The index closed up 6.9pc late Monday after rising as much as 7.7pc, regaining its losses during last week’s rout.

Nvidia shares surged as much as 34pc, their biggest one-day gain in 25 years, after the company reinstated Mr Huang following pressure from President Trump. They closed up 31pc.

Markets had been poised to gain ground as investors took stock following a bruising sell-off driven by darkening sentiment about AI.

But the recovery was boosted by a statement from Nvidia shortly before markets opened confirming the return of its founder.

Trading in Nasdaq futures was briefly halted before markets opened because of the huge volatility.

Mr Huang had stepped down from the chip giant earlier this month in the wake of revelations of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and another with a colleague.

Nvidia said it made its decision with “input from senior levels of the United States government”.

Mr Trump on Monday said he had “convinced” Nvidia to reinstate Mr Huang.

The rebound in stocks will help to ease concerns about the AI bubble bursting as investors begin to question whether AI companies will be able to recoup the vast sums of money being pumped into the industry.

The benchmark S&P 500 closed up 4.7pc, while the Dow Jones gained around 3pc.

Mr Huang later attended Nvidia’s headquarters, telling staff he would be a “better CEO the second time around”.

News.title: Dengue more widespread than previously thought
News.content:
Dengue is much more widespread than previously thought, researchers have warned, raising concerns that the threat has been underestimated and resources misallocated.

An analysis of global data from 1990 to 2024 found that there were 73.9 million cases of the mosquito-borne disease – 10.6 million more than previously captured.

“Collectively these data show that dengue is expanding faster, more consistently and more intensely than previously thought,” the authors from institutions in the UK, the US, South Africa and Singapore wrote.

Dengue, nicknamed breakbone fever, is spread by the Aedes mosquito and it can cause intense muscle, joint and bone aches. The severe form of the disease can be fatal, and it poses a significant burden on low and middle-income countries.

The research, presented at the annual meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in Maryland, comes as countries including Bangladesh, Malaysia and Cuba are being hit hard by outbreaks of the disease.

The paper, not yet published in a journal, found that global incidence rose 34-fold between 1990 and 2024, an average annual jump of 9.1 per cent. Cases rose most rapidly in regions where the virus has recently emerged – Africa, the Middle East and South Asia – and more slowly in Southeast Asia, where it’s been established for decades.

Researchers found the missing cases by combing through uncounted sources, like ministry of health PDFs and graphics that never made it into global datasets. They then combined this with modelling, to pull together a single database that tracks 35 years of cases by month, allowing scientists to test new hypotheses.

Sports.title: Why is Ethan Nwaneri allowed to play for Borussia Dortmund against parent club Arsenal in Champions League?
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL will host Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates tonight and Hale End’s Ethan Nwaneri is set to be involved for the visitors.

The home side sit third in the competition’s league phase, only dropping points away to Bayern Munich.



Dortmund have won three in the Champions League like Arsenal, however, they suffered a narrow loss away to Bodo/Glimt in October.

Arsenal opted to loan Nwaneri to Dortmund for this season, in a bid to develop and secure more game time.



The German club have a history of developing young English talents, including Jude Bellingham, Jamie Gittens and Jadon Sancho.

Domestically, Dortmund are in fine form as they sit top of the Bundesliga, ahead of the champions Bayern Munich.

Since the beginning of the season, Dortmund have only lost twice in all competitions.

Why is Nwaneri allowed to play for Borussia Dortmund against parent club Arsenal?

Despite clauses in the Premier League preventing loan players from facing their parent club, European competitions differ.

Due to regulations in the Champions League, Nwaneri will be eligible to face his parent club when they meet in North London this evening.

Arsenal and Dortmund faced off in a summer pre-season friendly where the Germans were victorious as they beat the Gunners 3-2, with Nwaneri scoring for his parent club.



The youngster has been struggling for minutes while out on loan, Mikel Arteta commented on Nwaneri’s situation prior to their upcoming match.

He said: “He needs to earn the right to play. He’s playing at the top of the Bundesliga and the players have huge talent and quality and they are showing that and that’s the reality of football,” Arteta said.

“Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that but it takes some time.”

Arteta added: “You go there and because you come from Arsenal, it doesn’t give you any advantage, so you need to earn it.”

While the 19-year-old is not guaranteed to start the game, you would expect that he would love to get some minutes off the bench and share the pitch with his mates from London.

Sports.title: Why is David Raya not playing for Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund in Champions League?
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates in a blockbuster Champions League clash.

The Gunners are looking to continue their unbeaten start in Europe against Germany’s league leaders.



But defeating Dortmund will be a challenge as BVB are unbeaten in the Bundesliga and could leapfrog Arsenal in the Champions League table with a win tonight.

Mikel Arteta has a headache between the sticks with first-choice goalkeeper David Raya ruled out with injury.



Why is David Raya not playing for Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund in Champions League?

On Saturday night, Raya picked up a shoulder injury during Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle.

The Spaniard was forced off in the 68th minute with former Chelsea keeper Kepa Arrizabalaga replacing him.



Arsenal were defending a corner and Raya collided with Newcastle striker William Osula and could not continue.

Arteta spoke about Raya’s injury before the clash with Dortmund, he said: “He’s not fit for [Dortmund] unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious.

“We need some more tests tomorrow but it’s quite encouraging with the pain he was showing. Immediately after the action, we were quite worried but it’s not as bad as we expected.

“We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had.



“The first tests we have done showed something much more encouraging. [On Tuesday] we need to ratify that to give you more specifics.

“There was no need for surgery. That was the main fear, because that would have ruled him out for months. Let’s see.”

When asked about whether he will return for the game against Manchester City on Sunday, Arteta said: “Tomorrow we will have more tests. Then you will know.”

Who will start in goal for Arsenal against Borussia Dortmund?

The more probable choice to replace him is Kepa, who came on for Raya on the weekend and seems to be cemented as the Gunners’ back-up goalkeeper.

However, with Kepa’s underwhelming performances, including being involved in the shock loss to Fleetwood earlier this season, it could make way for Illan Meslier to start.



Both goalkeepers will want to prove their worth to Arteta and stake a claim for the No1 spot.

Sports.title: Newcastle leaning towards building £1.3billion ‘oval-shaped’ stadium with St James’ Park DEMOLISHED as plans revealed
Sports.content:
Next

NEWCASTLE are ready to BULLDOZE St James’ Park to build a brand new £1.3BILLION stadium.

The iconic stadium has been The Magpies’ home since 1892.



But, according to The Telegraph, the Toon are now ready to knock it down and move to a new “oval-shaped” stadium in Leazes Park.

Newcastle have yet to make a final decision but know they need a bigger ground to bring in extra revenue.



One option being considered is to add an extra tier onto the famous Gallowgate End.

But the Toon’s preferred route is a new stadium built directly adjacent to the current Leazes End, with an increased capacity of up to 72,000.



It has emerged now, however, that that plan would include knocking down 52,000-seat St James’ Park.

Under the plans, a new leisure, office, retail and accommodation space would be built on the east of the current plot with the remainder of the land turning into green space.

Newcastle are planning a design that would see the stadium being shaped in an oval style with a “wave effect”.

That means there would be two slightly smaller stands along the sides of the pitch rising upwards and flanked by larger tiers behind both goals.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It has also been reported the designs include black-and-white illuminated cladding — similar to Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena — although the club deny this is what the exterior will look like.

The club’s owners, led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, will not finance the project on their own and instead will seek a loan to be repaid.

SunSport recently revealed Newcastle chiefs met representatives from US bank Goldman Sachs this month to discuss funding plans.

Chief executive David Hopkinson says the team “need” a new stadium for the revenue it will unlock.

A final decision is expected to be made in 2027 and if they choose to build a new stadium then construction will begin in 2029, after St James’ Park hosts its scheduled Euro 2028 games, and could take at least four years.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino orders Man Utd stars to report early for training after scrapping major Michael Carrick benefit
Sports.content:

MAURICIO POCHETTINO ordered Manchester United players to report earlier than usual for training on Monday.

Pochettino immediately scrapped United players’ day off the day after a match, a benefit reintroduced by Michael Carrick.



United were walloped 4-0 by Liverpool on Sunday and all of the players reported for training at their Carrington complex by 9.30am on Monday morning.

Although United sources say the arrival time has been brought forward by 15 minutes, players tended to arrive by 10.30am on Carrick’s watch.



Pochettino insisted on recovery sessions for the United players the day after his first fixture in charge, a practice that former managers Ruben Amorim, Erik ten Hag, Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal favoured.

Ten Hag initially ordered United players to arrive for training at 9am in summer 2022, a time Sir Alex Ferguson used to favour.

Carrick hardly ever incorporated recovery sessions into his training schedule other than between some Premier League and Champions League matches. Carrick managed United four times in the Champions League this season.

Pochettino acknowledged at his maiden press conference on Friday that United had to improve their dismal running stats. He has been joined in Manchester by his son, Sebastiano, who is a fitness coach.

Physical trainer Sylvia Tura, who worked with Pochettino in the United States, was in the same vehicle as Pochettino when they arrived at Carrington last Wednesday but United are yet to decide on whether to add her to his backroom staff.

United have hired Sam Wilson, who was previously the lead performance coach at Arsenal. United’s physio, Jordan Reece, came from Arsenal.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Work-rate has been an issue for almost every United manager since Ferguson retired in 2013 and Pochettino had six fitness coaches during his Tottenham tenure.

United fitness coach Charlie Owen was not among the recent exodus following Carrick’s sacking. Owen was promoted to the role by Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in July 2019.

Sports.title: Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman ‘split’ as reason behind sports power couple calling it quits revealed
Sports.content:
Next

BEN Shelton and Trinity Rodman have reportedly called it quits.

The American sports power couple are no more after nearly two years together.



According to the Daily Mail, Rodman and Shelton have decided to end their relationship due to a number of factors.

While they were extremely supportive of each other, showing up to cheer one anther on at their respective events, their schedules got too full.



“It is really difficult,’ Shelton told US Weekly in September.

“I think what a lot of people don’t see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we’re so exhausted that it’s tough to do anything.

“It is tough to make time.”

Rodman was at almost all of Shelton’s matches during the US Open this year.

And Shelton was there to support Rodman when her squad lost the NWSL Championship last November.

He notably was not there when she once again lost the championship game on Saturday against the Kansas City Current.



Rodman and Shelton began dating around March of 2025, but the constant travel involved in their relationship made things too hard to sustain.

Rodman and Shelton were almost exclusively in a long-distance relationship while he played on the ATP Tour.

And while Rodman’s Washington Spirit season is now over, the issues would have returned the moment the 2027 NWSL season began.



The former couple are reportedly on good terms despite splitting up.

Sports.title: Full list of 14 major UK stadiums as four nations win bid to host World Cup 2035 tournament
Sports.content:
Next

WOMEN’S World Cup matches will be hosted at 14 major stadiums in the UK as the four nations win bid to host the 2035 tournament.

Fifa officially confirmed that England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Irelandwould host the tournament, bringing the World Cup home for the first time since 1966.

The four home nations were the only bidders to host the coveted football competition, which will see 48 nations battle it out for the World Cup.



104 matches in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will take place throughout the 39 days of the tournament.



In the ambitious “All Together” bid for the World Cup, 19 stadiums were proposed, including 14 venues in England.

Included in England’s stadium bids are locations up and down the country, from Newcastle United‘s St James’ Park to Arsenal‘s Emirates Stadium.

The AMEX Stadium, City Ground, Elland Road, Etihad Stadium, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Selhurst Park, the Stadium of Light, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Villa Park are also proposed to host.

London’s iconic Wembley Stadium, with a capacity of over 90,000 has been proposed as the venue for the Women’s World Cup final, as well as the home of Bristol City, Ashton Gate.

Manchester United‘s Old Trafford stadium is included in its current form, with a planned new stadium set to be considered.

Meanwhile, Chelsea‘s potential new stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped ground and Birmingham’s new 62,000-capacity Powerhouse Stadium could also be included.



Full list of 14 MAJOR UK stadiums set to host the 2035 Women's World Cup Wembley Stadium – London

Ashton Gate – Bristol City

Amex Stadium – Brighton & Hove Albion

City Ground – Nottingham Forest

Elland Road – Leeds United

Outside of England, matches could take place in Wales’ Principality Stadium, Cardiff City Stadium, Windsor Park in Northern Ireland, Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow.

England’s winning bid marks the first time the nation has ever hosted the Women’s World Cup in the tournament’s 35-year history.

The nation previously failed to win the chance to host the men’s tournament in both 2006 and 2018, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for 2030 was ultimately scrapped.

England hosted the World Cup for the first and only time back in 1966, where the nation celebrated its historic victory.

Sports.title: Leny Yoro’s Man Utd ban OVERTURNED after appeal – even though Howard Webb says red card against Liverpool was correct
Sports.content:
Next

REFS boss Howard Webb says Leny Yoro was RIGHTLY sent off in Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United debut – despite his one game ban being OVERTURNED by the FA.

Wembley beaks confirmed United’s appeal against the one match suspension had been waived after “a successful claim of wrongful dismissal”.



But speaking on the latest edition of the “Mic’d Up” review show, ProRef chief Webb backed ref Sam Barrott and his VAR John Brooks for sending Yoro off just eight minutes into the game.

Poch was furious at the call, arguing that Alexander Isak’s poor touch meant he would not have got to the ball before United keeper Senne Lammens had he not been barged over from behind by the French defender.



Webb, though, said: “It’s a really decisive decision by the referee.

“Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession and knocks the ball past Yoro.



“He’s moving at pace at that moment and a foul comes in and knocks him down.

“There’s a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would’ve got onto that ball before Lammens.

“In the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

“That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t, that if there was any doubt, it was doubt, not something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed the decision to stand.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“By and large, most people would see that as a correct decision. It’s a little bit debatable, I guess, but certainly not clearly wrong.”

It is the second time this season that the FA has overturned bans for red cards ProRef and its Key Match Incident penal believes to have been correct, with the first involving Brighton’s Pascal Struijk at Sunderland last month.

Webb, though, disagreed with the panel which voted that Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty in their pre-break defeat to Arsenal when Isak’s shirt was grabbed by Jurrien Timber.

The former World Cup Final ref said: “The referee (Chris Kavanagh) sees what he describes as a small hold and doesn’t think there’s an impact.



“We would never want to encourage players to dive or throw themselves down and we saw situations like that in the game.

“On TV it was played out at 25 per cent of real speed and looks more impactful.

“The freeze frame replay is distorting reality but the VAR understandably check completed the referee’s call, which was brief hold, no impact.”

Webb confirmed Arsenal should have had a penalty in their win over Hull, when referee Farai Hallam wrongly decided Kai Havertz was offside when his shirt was pulled before he was close to the ball.

Sports.title: Ref chief Webb backs process around Yoro sending off despite successful appeal
Sports.content:
Referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the process of the officials who sent off Manchester United defender Leny Yoro at Liverpool - despite the red card being overturned on appeal.

Yoro, sent off after eight minutes of Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield, was due to face a one-match ban for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity when he brought down Alexander Isak outside the box and he was in on goal.

However, United have had the suspension lifted after a successful claim of wrongful dismissal, the FA said on Tuesday. The independent commission will publish the written reasons in "due course".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Liverpool and Manchester United.

In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb, chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, described the on-field decision from referee Samuel Barrott as "decisive" and said the point of contention was around whether Isak would beat United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to the ball.

Audio from the officials reveals that the VAR John Brooks, who backed Barrott's decision, determined Isak was "likely" to get on the end of the ball before Lammens. His assistant VAR, Paul Howard, agreed.

Webb was non-committal in his verdict but backed the process of the officials by saying "most people would see that as a correct decision".

"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens," said Webb. "Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. That was the referee's call made on the field.

"The VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect and formed the opinion that it wasn't. If there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. And I think by and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."

What the officials said...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ref Watch panel debate whether Leny Yoro should have been sent off against Liverpool on Sunday.

Assistant Referee 2: He's in.

REF - Sam Barrott: DOGSO (Denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity), DOGSO.

AR2: Contact.

REF: Outside.

AR2: I think outside.

REF: Outside and it's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside, red card for DOGSO.

VAR - John Brooks: Checking the on-field decision of DOGSO. Longer loop, please.

Replay Operator: Happy with this as the point of contact?

VAR: Yeah, point of contact. Go 18 [yard] now, go 18. Clearly outside. First contact, clearly outside.

Assistant VAR - Paul Howard: Yeah.

VAR: So, Isak is the right side, defender is the wrong side. Defender bundles into him, into the back. Gets too tight. I think it's a foul. Go back to 18-yard. Let's roll it through, firstly to see whether the attacker is going to get on the end of the ball. Just roll it through, real speed.

VAR: So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and likely gets on the end of it. Certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn't. So I think the DOGSO is confirmed. We'll just check APP (Attacking Possession Phase).

AVAR: I agree.

VAR: Sam [referee], the DOGSO location and sanction is confirmed. Just checking the rest of the APP.

RO: From here?

VAR: Yeah: Frame two, clearly onside. We've seen it all. Doesn't control the ball with the arm or anything, yes. Sam, confirming the on-field decision of a free-kick to Liverpool just outside the box and a denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

REF: Thank you.

Webb's verdict in full

Head of Pro Ref Howard Webb on Mic'D Up:

"Firstly, I think this was a really decisive decision by the referee Sam Barrott. We know it is clearly a foul and we also know it is outside the penalty area.

"We're thinking about the sanction. Is it a denial of an obvious goal scoring opportunity? There's actually four considerations officials have to think about.

Image: Denying a clear goalscoring opportunity - considerations for officials

"Direction of play: he is definitely going towards the goal. It's not going out wide. Proximity from goal: it's just outside the penalty area.

"The location of other defenders: there's only Yoro there. The keeper is moving back towards his own goal. He has to put the brakes on and possibly come back out.

"The reason we're talking about it is the fourth consideration. That's control or likelihood of keeping on or gaining control of the ball. Isak's got control of the ball. He's got possession. He's got the touch. He knocks it past Yoro. He's moving at pace at that moment. And a foul comes in and knocks him down.

"And there's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. That was the referee's call made on the field.

"The VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect and formed the opinion that it wasn't. If there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. And I think by and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."

What was the Ref Watch verdict?

Former Premier League official Dermot Gallagher said it was the right call to show Yoro a red card on the latest edition of Ref Watch.

He said: "If you look at it from the referee's angle. Is it a foul? That's the first step. Yeah. Is he in possession of the ball? From that angle, yes. I think most people would've expected a red card. It would've been a surprise during the game if a red card hadn't been given.

"I don't know [if he would've gotten to the ball before Lammens]. You watch it play out. That happens. Do you think it's a red card? Gary Neville's immediate reaction was red card."

Sports.title: How 'quick check' and unseen angle saw Timber's Isak shirt-pull go unpunished
Sports.content:
Referees’ chief Howard Webb admitted it was a “quick check” by VAR for Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber’s unpunished shirt-pull on Liverpool striker Alexander Isak in the Gunners’ win at Anfield.

Webb also said Isak's lack of a "natural reaction" to Timber's shirt pull on him was a factor in the decision not to award a penalty after the striker did not go down or protest the decision.

Earlier this month, the Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel ruled Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty for Timber's shirt tug on Isak inside the box at a cross.

Upon a review of the incident on Match Officials Mic'd Up, it was revealed that VAR Stuart Attwell spotted the shirt-pull offence but decided it was "all fine" 11 seconds later.

After declaring it was "all fine", referee Andy Madley and the assistant referee asked for clarification, which Attwell immediately responded to with "all fine", meaning the total check took only 18 seconds.

It was also revealed that VAR did not look at the reverse angle, which gave a clearer view of Timber's shirt pull.

Questioned on the speed of the call, Webb replied: "It was a quick check. You heard what the referee said on the field, and he thought at full speed, 'That's what I'm seeing as well'.

"This slow-motion freeze frame is distorting reality, and therefore we always have to view these things in reality and primarily at full speed, with some slow-motion for some of the detail.

"But in this situation, to get this sort of impact you're getting here, you're freeze-framing it, and that's what we're trying not to do because it's distorting reality."

Should Isak have gone down?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Andoni Iraola suggested that Isak would have been awarded a penalty if he'd gone to ground

Isak stayed on his feet during the incident, and Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said afterwards he would tell the striker to go down next time as the Reds were beaten 1-0 by Mikel Arteta's side.

The KMI panel voted 4:1 that referee Madley should have awarded Liverpool a spot-kick, while the panel also voted 3:2 that Attwell should have intervened and sent Madley to the pitchside monitor on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error.

One KMI panellist believed "the short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress", while two panellists argued, "the subjectivity in assessing impact meant this did not meet the high threshold for VAR intervention".

Webb said: "Certainly most of the feedback we've had is that a penalty should've been given.

"But I want to talk about why that didn't happen and why in the stadium the officials took the decision.

"Simply shirt-pulling or holding somebody on a football field isn't in itself always punishable. We see a lot of grappling and holding, and we don't see that being penalised.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Liverpool and Arsenal

"It's all about the impact you have on the opponent you hold. In this situation, the referee sees what he describes as a 'small hold that doesn't have an impact'. He does reference the fact that Isak doesn't ask him a question.

"I think it's reasonable if a player is held and is impacted for there to be some form of natural reaction from being impacted in that sort of way, and we certainly don't see that here.

"We never wanted to encourage players to dive or to throw themselves down, so you're not going to get the decision you want just by throwing yourself to the floor.

"When you look at this brief hold at full speed, it looks a lot worse when it's played out in slow motion. It lasts four times as long and therefore looks much more impactful.

"Most people think that this sort of reach out on a player in front of goal should be penalised, but I absolutely understand why when looking at impact from a brief hold to no natural reaction that only becomes clear in slow-motion is not penalised on-field, and the VAR understandably check completed the referee's call which was brief hold, no impact."

What the pundits said...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright discuss Liverpool's penalty shout

Jamie Carragher: "One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR, do your job."

Ian Wright: "He shouldn't have to make more of it. We can see it... Unless I'm pulled back, I'm going to head it as much as I can. When he pulled him, it was just about enough as he would need to go down.

"VAR is wrong in this instance. If they gave that penalty, I wouldn't sit here and say 'I can't believe they gave that'."

Gary Neville: "It's actually unnatural not to make more of it. When you get pulled and you're just about to score, you ordinarily complain like crazy. It's a very odd reaction from Isak."

Daniel Sturridge: "Unfortunately, he (Isak) has not fallen over. You're supposed to fall over, put your arms in the air and show the referee you're mad about it... to me, his reaction is almost like 'VAR, do your job'.

"But they've not done their job. He shouldn't have to make more of it - clearly, he shouldn't. Everyone can see that his arm is stretched; he [Timber] is holding him with a stretched-out arm."

Ref Watch's verdict...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ref Watch panel discuss whether Liverpool should have been awarded for Timber's shirt pull on Isak

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher: "It depends which angle you watch it from. The first angle, you see nothing. That is the referee's angle.

"The second angle, which is what VAR looks at, and it is a lot more damning.

"VAR looks at it in slow motion, which is another thing against him. In normal speed, he grabs and grabs him quickly but let's go. Does he do enough [for a penalty]?

"What is Timber's intention? He is on the wrong side of him. Does he do enough to stop him? He [Isak] will say yes, as he is close to the ball.

"VAR would be accused of re-refereeing if it is a penalty. It is a case of damned if they do and damned if they don't.

"It has to be the case of on-field. The more I watch it, the more I think he [Timber] has taken a big chance and has got lucky."

What happens if Isak goes down? "Once a player hits the ground, there are more questions to ask.

"There is asking what has knocked him down. Has he gone down by his own momentum, has he slipped or has he been pulled or pushed?

"Once you factor that in, obviously you have a different decision. He [referee] has to deal with the situation he has seen. He has seen a little pull of the jersey and thought no penalty."

Jay Bothroyd: "Where was the referee? Every angle, I can see it is a penalty.

"He has pulled his shirt. How can none of them [referee and VAR] see that and say it is a penalty? I can't comprehend that. I don't get it.

"That is one of the most obvious penalties [I have seen]. He is running forward! He has stifled his momentum going forward, to stop him heading the ball.

"Every angle I look at, even normal time, I said it could be a penalty. I look at it now, the more I see it, the more I ask myself how they have missed it! How do they lose focus and not get that."

Sports.title: Paul Scholes says ‘rabbit in the headlights’ £52m Man United man is not Premier League level
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes says ‘rabbit in the headlights’ £52m Man United man is not Premier League level

Paul Scholes has claimed the Premier League looks too much for Leny Yoro after Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off less than eight minutes into United's embarrassing loss at Anfield as the Mauricio Pochettino era got off to a nightmare start.



3 Yoro has come in for added scrutiny after his sending off against Liverpool Credit: AFP

The Frenchman clumsily ran into the back of Alexander Isak as the Reds striker ran in on goal and cut across his path.

Yoro was controversially shown a straight red card, as Liverpool went on to run riot against the ten-man Red Devils after Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the subsequent free-kick.

While the defender was set to serve a one-match suspension for his dismissal, this has since been overturned after an appeal.



The FA confirmed on Tuesday that the ban had been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

However, the circumstances surrounding Yoro's red gave him little defence in the eyes of Man United great Paul Scholes, who has criticised him in the aftermath of the Liverpool defeat.



Scholes raises questions

Since arriving at Old Trafford as a highly-rated 18-year-old in a deal worth £60million in 2024, Yoro has endured a rollercoaster ride in his 78 United appearances so far.

His most difficult period yet has come this term, forming part of leaky Red Devils defence that has conceded 23 goals in 11 Premier League matches – with only Crystal Palace conceding more.



And while none of United's defenders earned praise for Sunday's display, club icon Scholes took aim at Yoro on Monday.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football, he said: "The Premier League at this minute just looks a little bit too much for him.

"You know what, he’s come in to a really bad set-up defensively now. I think they also made the point yesterday if he went in next to [Virgil] Van Dijk he might look a little bit better.

3 Yoro tripped up Alexander Isak and was sent off against Liverpool, which immediately left his side facing an uphill battle Credit: Getty



"But he doesn’t look Premier League level. He looks like a rabbit in the headlights."

Scholes was joined by former United teammate Nicky Butt, who agreed that Yoro's level of performance would have seen him sent out on loan during their days together under Sir Alex Ferguson between 1994 and 2004.

Butt added: "If that’s Man United in our day, he’s on loan like a Jonny Evans or a John O’Shea.

"He’s a great talent that will come good."

However, Scholes was sceptical of Yoro's label as a future star, which has seen him eyed up by European champions Paris Saint-Germain.



The Premier League great replied: "I’m not sure how much of a great talent he is.

3 Yoro is yet to convince everyone in his two years at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

"I think he has shown a little bit of a sign in the France squad but every time I’ve seen him he doesn’t look at the races.

"Everything’s happening around him and he’s just a bit, 'Oh, what do I do?'"



Yoro has struggled to make one of the centre-back starting roles his own since signing for the Red Devils in the summer of 2024.

He had to wait until October 10 for his first Premier League start of this season, playing just under an hour in the 1-1 draw with Tottenham.

Since then, he has been a mainstay in United's back line amid a poor run of form which leaves them a lowly 19th in the Premier League.

Yoro has also started three of his side's four Champions League games this term, missing the 4-1 thrashing by Como after he was shown a red card in a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Sports.title: EFL club announce upcoming match is moved to following day in fixture chaos
Sports.content:
EFL club announce upcoming match is moved to following day in fixture chaos

Fleetwood Town have announced that their Jersey Mike's Trophy fixture against Leeds United's Under-21s has been postponed.

The League Two side were scheduled to host the Premier League outfit's youth team on Tuesday night at Highbury Stadium.



1 Fleetwood's Jersey Mike's Trophy clash against Leeds U21s has been pushed back a day due to heavy rain in the local area Credit: Getty

However, due to adverse weather conditions, the game has had to be moved back one day to Wednesday, November 25 instead.

Heavy rain along the Fylde Coast, where Fleetwood play their home football, has led to the date being switched.

There is no rain forecast for Wednesday in the local area.

Fleetwood vs Leeds U21s postponed

Announcing the day's delay to the clash, Fleetwood wrote in a statement: "Town’s Jersey Mike’s Trophy Northern Group G fixture against Leeds United Under-21s has been postponed due to heavy rainfall across the Fylde Coast.



"Tonight’s game at Highbury Stadium will now be played tomorrow, Wednesday 25 November, with kick-off at 7pm.

"All tickets purchased for tonight’s fixture remain valid for the rearranged game.



"We apologise for any inconvenience caused and thank supporters for their understanding."

Leeds also shared a similar statement to their fans.

The Premier League side's youth team and Fleetwood have been competing in Northern Group G in the Jersey Mike's Trophy.



Fleetwood, who beat Arsenal in the FA Cup in October, are sitting second in the group after winning one and losing one of their first two games.

As for Leeds' U21s, they're bottom of the group on goal difference, having lost and won a game too.

They are sitting on -1 goal difference, along with Barnsley, while Fleetwood have +2 after two games.

But as they are all on the same points, it means it's all or nothing for both sides in their rearranged meeting.



The top two in each group in the Jersey Mike's Trophy reach the knockout stages, with Oldham already claiming one spot and Barnsley already eliminated.

So, a win for Leeds or Fleetwood will send them through, while a draw will see penalties decide who progresses, as the winner of the shootout claims an extra point.

Sports.title: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro red card overturned against wishes of referees chief Howard Webb
Sports.content:
Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's one-match suspension picked up after a red card against Liverpool has been overturned.

Yoro was sent off inside the first ten minutes of Man United's embarrassing 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

3 Yoro was sent off after eight minutes in United's 4-0 loss to Liverpool, but his red card has now been removed Credit: Getty

He clumsily ran into the back of Alexander Isak as the Reds striker raced through on goal and cut across his path.

The Frenchman was shown a straight red card for the incident and Liverpool went on to take the lead from the free-kick.

Then, in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge, United struggled to the full-time whistle, being thrashed 4-0 in the end.

And Pochettino wasn't happy when discussing his centre-back's red, complaining that his actions weren't intentional.

He also felt that Isak had taken a heavy touch before going down under contact from Yoro, which would have seen goalkeeper Senne Lammens collect the ball before the forward got to it.

The Argentine manager spoke to the officials at half-time too, revealing after the game: "I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel. That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card."

United then appealed the red card post-match and the FA have now confirmed that the decision has been overturned, meaning he will be available to play against Brentford on Saturday.

Yoro's red card overturned

“Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," the FA wrote.

"The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

"The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course."

3 United appealed Yoro's red card after being left angry at the decision that ended up leading to their heavy defeat at Anfield Credit: Getty

ProRef: Yoro red card was correct decision

The announcement is a welcome one at Old Trafford but not at Stockley Park.

ProRef chief Howard Webb has backed Sam Barrott, the referee for the Anfield clash, for the decision he made on the field and added that the incident was not clear and obvious enough for VAR intervention.

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," Webb said on the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong."

What else has been said on Yoro's red being rescinded?

Following the news of Yoro's suspension being overturned, talkSPORT's Kevin Hatchard said: "The feeling in the moment was that it was clumsy and I can understand why a red was shown.

"But I just think on a more general point that we've got ourselves into such a mess now with when should VAR get involved, when should the referee go to the screen.

3 If Webb had it his way, Yoro would've been forced to serve his suspension Credit: Sky Sports

"It's changing how referees are refereeing the game. Get rid of it."

On the lack of use of the VAR monitor, he added: "I feel the monitor is underused. If the whole point is to let the referee have another look, I do find it odd that they don't do it more often.

"Ultimately, it should be down to the referee, so if they get have a second chance to look at it then great.

"Where's the threshhold? How often do we want them to get involved. I just think it's an unneccesary mess with VAR in general."

Sports.title: Arsenal should sell Viktor Gyokeres as perfect Mikel Arteta signing identified
Sports.content:
Arsenal have been tipped to sell Vikor Gyokeres in the January transfer window.

Gyokeres is very clearly second choice striker behind Kai Havertz for the Gunners, starting just one Premier League game.



4 Gyokeres has struggled for minutes so far this season and has only scored twice in 15 appearances in all competitions Credit: Getty

In all competitions, he has started in six of his 15 appearances, scoring twice and providing three assists across those matches, making the missed deal for Julian Alvarez all the more difficult to swallow.

At least for one fan it does, as broadcaster Jacob Hawley told talkSPORT.

Could Gyokeres leave Arsenal in January?

talkSPORT host Jacob Hawley said on Hawksbee and Jacobs show: "I think he could leave...I think if Arsenal want to get someone in, they're going to have shift someone.



"Ultimately, Arsenal have just got too many players.

"We talk about this big squad and it's great, but if everyone was fit, you'd have players like Mikel Merino, Max Dowman, Piero Hincapie not even making squads.

"So if we do want to sell someone in January, I think he will go."

Hawley then went on to state that Gyokeres would be well-suited to Spanish football, bringing up the Alvarez swap in the summer.



Arsenal were linked to a swap deal with Atletico Madrid for ex-Man City man Alvarez, but in the end, nothing materialised.

"I think if Mikel Arteta was honest, he'd have loved to have swapped him for Julian Alvarez in the summer," he said.



"They chased Alvarez all summer, there were reports that they would have sent Gyokeres the other way.

4 Hawley thinks Gyokeres could be let go if Arsenal want to sign some players, as they boast a very deep squad Credit: Getty

4 Arsenal were linked with a swap deal involving Gyokeres and Alvarez in the summer - could those talks resume if the Gunners look to sell their striker? Credit: Getty

"It would have worked for everyone. He would do great in Spain.

"I think he could well go in January."

Gyokeres has been a 'daft signing'

His lack of form is growing increasingly concerning for Arsenal, who signed the Sweden international for an initial £55million in 2025.



But without regular minutes, Gyokeres is going to struggle to find his previous level.

Gyokeres scored 97 goals in 102 games for Sporting before making the switch to the Premier League last year.

But he has been far away from that remarkable record for Arsenal.

On a more positive note, though, the 28-year-old helped his side to lift a top-flight title last term, scoring 14 league goals.

Hawley believes Gyokeres has actually contributed enough so far, but that his profile just doesn't fit Arteta's style.



"Gyokeres isn't my favourite player...he scored loads of goals in Portugal, but we've seen these players come and it's a completely different game.

"Even if you look good in the Champions League, as he did against Arsenal, it's just a completely different game in the Premier League.

"It's clear now that he's second to Kai Havertz. He got 13 goals in the league last season, which isn't bad...gone are the days that strikers just bang in 25, 30 goals a season - Erling Haaland aside."

Hawley then added: "It sounds mad, but he only cost £55million.

4 The Sweden international joined Arsenal in a deal worth an initial £55m and Hawley thinks that was a good deal, even if he has struggled to replicate his best Credit: Getty



"That's not a lot of money, relative to what other forwards cost. What did Darwin Nunez cost Liverpool? What did Richarlison cost Spurs? Is Gyokeres a worse player than Richarlison?

"People have been waiting for that big striker to come in at Arsenal for years...we spent £55m on a player who was always going to be second choice, he's still second choice.

"It's two goals in 15 (this season), but those 15, most of them are sub appearances. There's been a couple of games, he's looked like he was fed up and I can understand that.

"But he doesn't play the way an Arsenal striker plays. Under Arteta, he's liked Gabriel Jesus, Havertz, played Merino there sometimes. He likes them as almost midfielders, really. It's not Gyokeres.



"And it's probably a bit of a daft signing when you bare that in mind."

Sports.title: Manchester United player open to January move after snub from Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
Manchester United player open to January move after snub from Mauricio Pochettino

Ayden Heaven is open to leaving Manchester United on a permanent or loan deal in January, talkSPORT understands.

Heaven has made just two Premier League starts and played 470 minutes across all competitions for the Red Devils this season.



4 Heaven faces an uncertain future at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

And the 20-year-old, who joined United from Arsenal in 2025, could be set leave the club when the transfer window opens.

Heaven questioning United future

With new boss Mauricio Pochettino leaving him on the bench in Sunday's 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, Heaven is concerned over how the managerial change could impact his development.

Now on his third manager in 21 months at Old Trafford, the young defender has accepted Pochettino may prefer more experienced options as United bid to avoid a shock relegation.



This comes amid rumours linking United with Fulham's Calvin Bassey, although the defender has confirmed he is in negotiations over extending his contract at Craven Cottage.

Heaven has made 32 senior appearances for Man United, 26 of which have come in the Premier League.



The England Under-20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.

Having made 13 league starts overall in his United career, he would surely benefit from more game time.



Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have previously expressed an interest in Heaven.

Both tried to sign the youngster when he decided to leave Arsenal, with his eventual move to Old Trafford seen as a major coup.

However, Heaven has largely been used as a back-up option at United, despite enjoying a run in the side under Ruben Amorim.

4 Mauricio Pochettino opted for a starting centre-back pairing of Matthijs De Ligt and Lisandro Martinez against Liverpool Credit: Getty



4 Heaven has started twice in the Champions League for Man United this season Credit: Getty

This came to an end following Michael Carrick's arrival as interim boss in January, and he returned to the starting line-up only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.

Heaven is under contract at Old Trafford until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year.

While centre-back is his preferred position, the young defender is also capable of playing in midfield and at left-back, having deputised in the latter role in United's Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in October.



However, with United sitting a shock 19th in the Premier League standings, Heaven does not expect to be a regular starter as they club look to battle back against their current circumstances.

Against Liverpool on Sunday, Pochettino opted for a centre-back pairing of Matthijs De Ligt and Lisandro Martinez.

Then, after Leny Yoro was shown a red card in the opening 10 minutes, the Argentine brought on experienced defender Harry Maguire ahead of Heaven as he looked to shore things up.

4 A 10-man United defence was unable to keep Liverpool at bay on Sunday Credit: Getty



This move failed to achieve the desired result though, as Liverpool ran riot with goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz to claim a comfortable win.

Sports.title: Euro 2028 qualifying draw date, start time, format and confirmed pots
Sports.content:
The countdown to Euro 2028 will get underway in earnest with the qualifying draw next weekend.

The next European Championship is being held in England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales from June 9 to July 9, 2028.



3 Tuchel's preparations for Euro 2028 will begin with the qualification draw Credit: Getty

Spain will be the defending champions after beating England in the 2024 final but now, the Three Lions will be eyeing glory on home turf.

Thomas Tuchel will lead his side at the major tournament and while England will be among the favourites, the likes of Spain, France, Portugal and Germany will also be gunning for the trophy.

Euro 2028 will again have six groups of four with the top two sides qualifying for the knockout phase plus the four best third-placed teams.



The tournament will then progress from the Round of 16 through to the showpiece final at Wembley.

And the build-up to the 18th edition of the Euros will officially get going with the draw for qualification.



When is the Euro 2028 qualifying draw?

The Euro 2028 qualifying draw will be conducted on Sunday, December 6.

It will be held at 5pm GMT with the proceedings taking place at the International Convention Centre in Belfast.



talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will bring you full coverage of the draw.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.



3 Spain won Euro 2024 Credit: Getty

What are the Euro 2028 qualifying pots?

Pot One: England, Portugal, France, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Netherlands, Norway, Greece, Italy, Denmark, Croatia

Pot Two: Wales, Serbia, Turkey, Czech Republic, Switzerland, Sweden, Austria, Northern Ireland, Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Hungary, Republic of Ireland

Pot Three: Ukraine, Scotland, Kosovo, Poland, Israel, Romania, Georgia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania, Iceland, Slovakia

Pot Four: Estonia, Belarus, Faroe Islands, Cyprus, Finland, Moldova, Armenia, Bulgaria, Kazakhstan, Luxembourg, Latvia, San Marino

Pot Five: Malta, Azerbaijan, Lithuania, Andorra, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein

How does the Euro 2028 draw work?

The draw procedure will see the 54 teams involved split into five pots.

They will then be drawn into 12 separate qualifying groups - the first six containing four teams and the remaining six having five countries.

The host nations will be drawn in different groups.

The ongoing Nations League will have an impact on the draw.

The groups with five teams will play their opening two ties in the same international break as when the Nations League quarter-finals are being held.



The four Nations League quarter-final winners will be drawn into groups containing four nations with the Final being held during Matchday 3 and 4 of the Euro Qualifying group stage.

Those Nations League Finals teams will get their Euro campaigns underway the following September.

Once the 10 Matchdays are done, 20 teams will make it to the main tournament - the 12 group winners and the eight best runners-up.

There will then be play-offs held in March 2028 to determine the final places.



3 McTominay's Scotland will be determined to secure Euro 2028 qualification Credit: Getty

When are the Euro 2028 qualifying fixtures?

Matchday 1: March 26, 2027

Matchday 2: March 29, 2027

Matchday 3: June 11-12, 2027

Matchday 4: June 14-15, 2027

Matchday 5: September 23-25, 2027

Matchday 6: September 26-28, 2027

Matchday 7: September 30 - October 2, 2027

Matchday 8: October 3-5, 2027

Matchday 9: November 11-13, 2027

Matchday 10: November 14-16, 2027

Play-offs: March 23-28, 2028

Where will the host nations play if they qualify?

The four host nations have had their groups pre-determined should they secure qualification.

Each nation has been designated a group with their home stadiums.

Northern Ireland’s potential group has also been decided ahead of time.

Sports.title: Wesley Fofana picks worst possible time to deliver two bombshell Chelsea revelations
Sports.content:
Wesley Fofana has made another mistake - but this one was not on the pitch.

The Chelsea defender has picked a rather clumsy time to be at the centre of a two-hour podcast with a French influencer.



2 Fofana has not impressed in a Chelsea shirt this season Credit: Getty

Fofana is four years into his Stamford Bridge career and yet to convince supporters he was worth £75million, along with one of the club's most lucrative contracts.

The 25-year-old is thought to be earning around £200,000-a-week, yet Chelsea's defensive record with Fofana in the team makes for grim reading.

This season alone, Chelsea have conceded more than two goals per game on average during his nine appearances, as opposed to one goal per game in the five matches without him.



While it would be unfair to pin this all on Fofana, it is a pattern which extends throughout his Blues career: Chelsea concede fewer goals, keep more clean sheets, and get more points on average when he is not in the team.

Many fans have lost patience after the calamitous 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds on Saturday.



So it is probably not the best time for Fofana to tell that fanbase he only carried on playing to collect his massive wage packet.

And, for good measure, he did not lose much sleep over missing a recent penalty against Liverpool.



Revealing that he nearly retired amid multiple long-term injuries, Fofana told ZackNaniTV: "I sat down with my agents, I told them, 'Yeah, that's it, I'm quitting football'.

"After that, they started talking to me about the contract and all that.

"They said: 'Anyway, it's simple, you've still got so many years left on your contract, and so much money to earn. Even if you're going to give up on football, you'll turn up every day, put on a smile, you'll even stay on the sidelines whilst injured, but you've got a contract. You've got to see it through, even for your future, you see.'

2 Since arriving at Chelsea, Fofana has missed roughly 120 games Credit: AFP



"Yeah, that makes sense."

Fofana not only missed a decisive penalty in the Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool, but also conceded a sloppy one in normal time which allowed the Reds to equalise.

Reflecting on that, the defender said: "It's not the first time I've been attacked. It's fine; it doesn't matter. I couldn't care less. I know there's another match in three days.

"In three days' time, you win, and people forget - they've already forgotten - about your penalty; that's just how football works. I stepped up, took it, and missed.

"I sent a real beauty of a shot way over the bar. Did you see my shot? I really blasted it high [laughs]. I remember a fan, way up high, he actually managed to catch the ball. But yeah, I missed, you know.



"Now, I laugh about it because it's just part of football - that's how it goes. And, well, there you have it. Besides, as I said, we kept the momentum going, we got the win [vs Manchester United a few days later], and it sort of faded into the background. We actually saw a great response in the second half."

Besides his questionable displays, Fofana has caused trouble for Chelsea off the pitch before as well.

The club have previously held formal talks with the Frenchman over repeated driving offences.

Many will feel it is about time he proved his worth to the club before conducting his next interview.

Sports.title: Ally McCoist names the one job David Moyes would prefer over Scotland
Sports.content:
Ally McCoist names the one job David Moyes would prefer over Scotland

Ally McCoist believes taking over at Celtic offers more appeal for David Moyes than the Scotland national team.

Moyes' contract with Everton is due to expire next summer, placing the 63-year-old at a significant crossroads in his career.



2 As it stands, Moyes' future is yet to be decided Credit: AFP

Given his standing as one of the most prominent Scottish managers in the game, some of his countrymen are hopeful Moyes takes over the national job.

However, that is occupied by Sebastien Pocagnoli, who was appointed as Steve Clarke's successor on a two-year contract in August.

Conveniently, incumbent Celtic boss Martin O'Neill's contract will also expire at the end of the season, meaning there will be a vacancy at the Scottish powerhouse.



Although McCoist believes Moyes would be enticed by the prospect of leading his nation, the thought of taking charge at Celtic Park could be too difficult to turn down.

Ally McCoist's verdict on David Moyes' next move

"The Celtic job in particular would be of interest to him, having played there," McCoist said on talkSPORT Breakfast.



"I genuinely don't know what's going on in David's head. But I would think that job (Celtic) might actually appeal to him more than the Scotland job.

"You can argue that the Scotland job would be the one that everybody would want, being a Scotsman.



"But he would look around, he'd look at the squad and where they are at this moment in time and I'm not sure it would be of massive encouragement to him."

McCoist joked that Moyes would also 'struggle to fill his day' should he get involved in international management.

David Moyes' managerial career at a glance

Outside of a year-long stint at LaLiga outfit Real Sociedad, Moyes' managerial career, which dates back to 1998, has been limited to the confines of England.

2 Everton's current owners are looking to sell the club, leaving Moyes in the dark about what's next Credit: Getty



The 63-year-old has spent time, to varying degrees of success, at Preston North End, Manchester United, Sunderland and West Ham.

But no stint has been quite as long as his two with Everton.

He moved to the Toffees in 2002 and spent 11 years at the helm before he was hand-picked to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson at Old Trafford.

It wasn't until January 2025 when Moyes sealed an emotional return to Everton.

Moyes now boasts the record for the most matches in charge of Everton, having overseen 593 games.



The Scot broke Harry Catterick's record on Monday when the Toffees faced Brentford on Monday.

Unfortunately for Moyes, the momentous occasion was marred by a 4-0 defeat to the Bees.
