Sports.title: Beauden Barrett in advanced talks to sign for Bristol Bears: NIK SIMON reveals full details of biggest offer in PREM history - and what sensational coup would mean for English rugby
Sports.content:
Beauden Barrett in advanced talks to sign for Bristol Bears: NIK SIMON reveals full details of biggest offer in PREM history - and what sensational coup would mean for English rugby

Bristol Bears are in advanced talks to sign All Blacks superstar Beauden Barrett.

The double World Player of the Year has been offered a two-year contract that would represent a sensational coup for the English club game.

Daily Mail Sport understands Barrett has been offered a deal worth more than £1million a year, which would make him the highest paid player in the league, coming into effect for the start of next season.

Bristol would make Barrett their marquee signing but it is understood the Kiwi is also weighing up an offer from a club in the Top 14.

Barrett is currently in London for the Nations Championship and it is understood his representatives have spoken at length with Bristol.

Beauden Barrett is in advanced talks over signing a two-year deal with PREM Rugby side Bristol Bears

Barrett currently plays for the Blues in Super Rugby and has also had two spells in Japan, with Suntory Sungoliath and Toyota Verblitz

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport last month, the 35-year-old’s services were also offered to Newcastle Red Bulls.

Newcastle decided against a move for the high-profile playmaker – who plays fly-half and full-back – but Bristol coach Pat Lam is keen to land the statement signing.

With long-standing playmaker AJ MacGinty considering a transition into coaching, the West Country club are in the market for a No 10.

Moving overseas would end Barrett’s hopes of playing for the All Blacks but the 150-cap veteran has played a reduced role under new coach Dave Rennie.

He is unlikely to represent his country beyond next year’s World Cup, which makes it perfect timing for a move to Europe.

Despite being in the advanced stages of his career, Barrett would be one of the most exciting players ever to move to England’s domestic league.

It is understood Beauden's brother Scott is also exploring a move to Europe, but it would be near impossible for any English club to take both Barretts on within the salary cap.

All Blacks forwards Wallace Sititi and Luke Jacobson have already agreed moves to France as players sort out their long-term futures.

He scored his 51st Test try at Twickenham last Saturday on his 150th cap for the All Blacks, in a disappointing defeat by England

ANALYSIS BY NIK SIMON

Beauden Barrett moving to English rugby would be the equivalent of Lionel Messi joining the Premier League. The All Blacks playmaker is in the twilight of his career but his try against England on Saturday reminded the world of his box-office status.

After years of financial decay – watching the likes of Worcester, Wasps and London Irish go bankrupt – the arrival of Barrett would represent a glorious renaissance for the PREM. With Dyson and Red Bull pumping millions into the game, Barrett's arrival would be one of the biggest statements in English rugby history.

With the financial backing of billionaire Steve Lansdown, Bristol have a proud history of box-office recruitment. They recently recruited American superstar Ilona Maher to their women’s team and, in recent years, the men’s backline has been studded with stars such as Charles Piutau and Semi Radradra.

Pat Lam is the coach who pushed hardest to bring back Louis Rees-Zammit from the NFL and now he is leading the charge for one of rugby’s greatest-ever players. Barrett’s highlights reel is unmatched over the past decade. He has won two World Cups and is one of the modern-day icons of the All Blacks.

Let’s hope he takes up Bristol's offer, because it would be priceless for the league’s global footprint.

Sports.title: BBC move Sport Personality of the Year 2026: Salford awards ceremony changed back to a Sunday but will be at 5.45pm and reduced to 90 minutes
Sports.content:
BBC's flagship Sports Personality of the Year awards will have to settle for a reduced spot in the broadcaster's schedule this December, with the annual show swapped out of a primetime slot. The long-running programme is set to air on Sunday, December 13, but will kick off earlier than usual at 5.45pm – and in a format trimmed down to 90 minutes from two hours. Wrapped up by 7.15pm, Sports Personality of the Year will then quickly make way for the final results show of the ballroom dancing contest, with Antiques Roadshow holding onto the 8pm slot. For the past five years, the channel has given more space to a broadcast celebrating the best of British sport, with the 2025, 2024 and 2023 awards all airing from 7pm, with the big winner on the night handed their trophy just after 9pm, with last year's ceremony held on a Thursday. The BBC said in a statement: 'Following the success of last year, we wanted to bring the awards back to a primetime slot on a Sunday evening, making it more accessible so that more people and families can watch and enjoy the celebrations together. 'We’ve made some adjustments to the format to make this work, and we’re looking forward to another fantastic year.' BBC's Sports Personality of the Year awards will run earlier and shorter this year against the backdrop of change at the broadcaster In 2022, Mary Earps won the trophy at 9pm two hours and fifteen minutes after the show started at 6.45pm, with Emma Raducanu announced as the winner at the same time a year earlier. The Corporation argues that Sunday late afternoon is likely to see more families enjoy the awards show and added: 'The shorter format is about creating a more focused, engaging and accessible show for audiences. 'This ensures the key moments, sporting stories and celebrations remain front and centre, delivering a compelling experience for viewers. It allows us to maintain the excitement, emotion and prestige of the awards while keeping the programme moving at pace.' The move comes against the backdrop of a number of cut-backs within the BBC's sports output. The department made a slew of unpopular cuts as recently as September, when it was announced that 41 roles were set to be made redundant with a view to making a saving of £2.5million. Equally unsettling was the decision at the end of last season to scrap BBC's Football Focus. At the time, the BBC denied it was part of the money-saving scheme but instead part of 'the continued shift in how audiences engage with football and our commitment to evolving how we deliver content to reach fans wherever they are'. Another programme to have felt the swing of the axe in recent months was winter sports show Ski Sunday, which was cut from the schedule after a nearly 50-year run. During this summer's World Cup, the channel came under fire for the decision to base BBC's punditry team from Salford instead of flying them to North America, as broadcast rivals ITV did. Big names including Gabby Logan, Wayne Rooney and Alan Shearer did not report Stateside until the semi-final stage, in stark contrast to the elaborate studio in New York constructed for ITV. The award was first presented in 1954, when runner Christopher Chataway beat fellow athlete Roger Bannister. For decades, the BBC show was seen as the centre piece of the broadcaster's sporting year. However, SPOTY has suffered from dwindling viewer figures in recent years.

Sports.title: Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman SPLIT: Sports' biggest power couple call time on romance after two years
Sports.content:
Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman SPLIT: Sports' biggest power couple call time on romance after two years

Tennis star Ben Shelton and soccer sensation Trinity Rodman have split after almost two years together, the Daily Mail can exclusively reveal.

The American sporting couple began dating around March 2025, frequently supporting one another at their various events, but have recently decided to call time on their relationship.

Their conflicting work schedules and constant travel made it too challenging for the couple to continue maintaining their relationship, the Daily Mail understands. However, the pair are believed to remain close, despite their split.

The couple were frequently forced to maintain their romance over long distance with Shelton constantly traveling around the globe while playing on the ATP Tour.

Despite multiple sacrifices and last-minute trips to attend each other's matches, it appears they could no longer make it work.

The Daily Mail has reached out to both Shelton and Rodman's representatives for comment.

Tennis star Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman have split, the Daily Mail understands

Their conflicting work schedules made it too challenging to maintain their relationship

The sporting power couple went public with their relationship around March 2025

Shelton, 24, suffered defeat in the semi-final of the ATP Finals on Saturday, losing 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7-1) to Carlos Alcaraz in Turin, Italy. The same evening, Rodman, 24, and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL final to the KC Current.

The following evening, the American tennis star was spotted at Madison Square Garden for the New York Knicks' game against the Indiana Pacers without Rodman, instead sitting on Celebrity Row alongside a friend and actress Inde Navarette.

The couple first went public with their relationship in March 2025 following speculation from fans.

Mystery surrounded the early stages of their relationship, as they initially dropped a playful hint as part of a TikTok trend last March then 'hard launched' their romance soon afterwards.

Rodman was a near-permanent fixture in Shelton's box throughout the US Open in September. The USWNT star and the Spirit had played an NWSL game in Washington on the day of the final but Rodman left the capital almost immediately after the final whistle to make the mad dash to New York for Shelton's final.

The forward was captured crying inside Arthur Ashe Stadium in the wake of her boyfriend's loss to Alexander Zverev.

Rodman, the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman, had cheered on the World No 4 at multiple other events, making her Wimbledon debut in May 2025.

Meanwhile, the tennis superstar was every bit the supportive boyfriend when he consoled Rodman after her team lost the NWSL championship game last November.

The World No 4 attended the Knicks game on Sunday, one day after losing the ATP semifinal

Rodman and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL Championship to the KC Current on Saturday

The Washington Spirit were stunned by underdogs Gotham FC in California, as footage from the game showed Shelton consoling an emotional Rodman as she burst into tears on the sidelines.

Shelton opened up on the challenges of their relationship in September, admitting that it was tough for the couple to continuously make time for one another.

'It is really difficult,' the Grand Slam finalist told US Weekly. 'I think what a lot of people don't see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we're so exhausted that it's tough to do anything. It is tough to make time.'

He added: 'Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I'm a bit of a zombie. I'm not the most fun person to be around. But we make a lot of sacrifices for our sport. I'd say both of us are chasing things for our sport. We're not where we want to be yet, we're not in our primes. So this is kind of crunch time.

'This is going to be the hardest, most grueling time in our relationship, from my perspective. None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who's such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways.'

Sports.title: David Raya's shoulder injury isn't 'too serious', confirms Mikel Arteta - as relieved Arsenal boss reveals stricken goalkeeper won't need surgery and COULD face Manchester City
Sports.content:
David Raya's shoulder injury isn't 'too serious', confirms Mikel Arteta - as relieved Arsenal boss reveals stricken goalkeeper won't need surgery and COULD face Manchester City

Mikel Arteta said David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.

Raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula. He looked in agony as he left the pitch.

His No 2 Kepa Arrizabalaga is instead expected to play for the north London club in their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.

Though Arteta confirmed Raya doesn’t require surgery and didn’t yet rule him out for Sunday’s Premier League clash against Manchester City.

‘He’s (Raya) not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious,’ said Arteta. ‘We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test shows something much more encouraging.

Arsenal's No 1 David Raya underwent an MRI scan the day after going off against Newcastle

‘There is no need for surgery, which was the main fear because that would have ruled him out for months.’

Asked whether Raya could play at home to Man City, he added: ‘Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team as well.

‘That’s why we are very protective with Kepa and (third-choice) Illan (Meslier). Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen.’

Raya has been sensational for the Premier League champions and his absence is likely to hurt the best defensive unit.

'That's a massive worry,' Ian Wright said on Sky Sports when the stopper went down. 'I don't want to say I'm petrified simply because Kepa is in goal, he's the guy who has got to try and keep the goals out for us now.

'But yeah, that is a massive blow. Someone like him, Declan Rice, Gabriel, it is very tough to replace those guys.'

Meanwhile, Bruno Guimaraes said Arteta is ‘crazy’ about the small details that will take him to ‘another level’.

Since his summer move from Newcastle, the 29-year-old has scored vital goals against Sunderland and Leeds - but is yet to complete a full 90 minutes in the Premier League.

Raya hit the turf in pain and went off the pitch clutching his arm to indicate that something serious had happened

‘I now definitely understand my role in the team and the way Mikel wants me to play but I can still play much better,’ said the Brazilian.

‘I think Mikel (Arteta) is unbelievable. He as a manager is so focused on small details, the way you control the ball, the way that you cannot be aligned with your opposite side.

‘Some details I have never heard before, I just found out with him here. He is crazy a little bit about these small details and I try and take (in) as much as I can because he is so passionate about them.

‘He showed me some clips (from when I was) in Newcastle and some clips here, where he thinks I can do things differently. He's trying to take me to another level.’

NEW TV INNOVATION FOR VIEWERS ON AMAZON PRIME FOR ARSENAL VS DORTMUND Arsenal's clash with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night will feature a new innovation for its TV audience watching on Prime Video. Called 'Progressive Actions' it highlights the passes and ball carries that drive a team up the pitch, and the often-unsung players behind them. Developed by Prime Video's team of producers, engineers, AI experts, and on-air analysts, Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built specifically for the UEFA Champions League. It joins the growing suite of features on Prime Vision, the alternate feed which serves as a laboratory and incubator for new features that often advance to the main broadcast. Progressive Actions is built on proprietary AI-powered models that identify a Progressive Action based on how far the ball travels in each phase of the pitch, with the threshold becoming shorter closer to the opposition goal where defences are more compact and space is harder to find. The metric mirrors the data used behind the scenes at Europe's elite clubs, yet has historically been difficult to show during a live broadcast. As a player makes a Progressive Action, an on-pitch graphic will show where the action started and ended, the player involved, and the distance the ball advanced, allowing fans to see the game as a coaching team would, in real time. 'Prime Vision is where we develop new features that shine a spotlight on the metrics, actions and players that impact a game most, yet aren't always captured by traditional statistics or broadcast techniques,' said Andrew Hornett, Director of Live Sports Production for Europe at Prime Video. 'Every team has players whose influence goes far beyond the scoresheet, the ones doing the crucial work in the build-up, moving the ball forward two or three passes before an assist. Progressive Actions is designed to capture that impact, measuring and visualising these actions during a live broadcast. Fans will see them in real time as they happen, but we'll also aggregate the data across the game, so you can see which players have had the biggest impact on the match.' The feature will debut in the UK and Ireland on Tuesday and will also be available for fans in Germany and Italy. Fans can access Prime Vision, with features including Progressive Actions, via their remote from the match detail page or the in-game menu during any live UCL fixture on Prime Video. Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built from the ground up specifically for Prime Video's UEFA Champions League coverage, and sits alongside Tactical Map, Momentum, Physical Insights, Advanced Analytics, Passing Options, and Player ID in Prime Vision's growing suite of features designed to take football fans closer to the game, all available on the alternate feed during every UEFA Champions League match live on Prime Video. Prime Insights were first developed for Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football, its exclusive weekly NFL package in the US, where AI-powered features including the award-winning Defensive Alerts have become a staple of the coverage, advancing from the alternate feed to the main broadcast each week.

Sports.title: Leny Yoro red card OVERTURNED: Man United star available for Brentford clash after controversial dismissal in Liverpool trouncing
Sports.content:
Leny Yoro’s one-match ban has been lifted by the FA after Manchester United successfully appealed against his sending-off at Liverpool on Sunday, despite Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believing it was the right decision. Yoro was shown a straight red card by referee Sam Barrott in the eighth minute for a challenge on Alexander Isak, and United’s 10 men went on to lose 4-0 in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge. The club launched an appeal over the decision and the FA have confirmed that Yoro will now be available for Saturday’s game against Brentford at Old Trafford. A statement read: ‘Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim for wrongful dismissal. The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The Independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for the decision will be published in due course.’ Barrott sent off Yoro for pushing Isak in the back on the edge of the penalty box, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free kick. However, United insisted that the Frenchman did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first. Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United The overturned decision, contradicts the opinion of Webb who backed Barrott's on-field verdict, when speaking on the Match Officials Mic'd Up show. 'Firstly, I want to say, I think this is a really decisive decision by the referee, Sam Barrott. We know it's clearly a foul. I don't think there's any dispute about that. And we also know that it's outside the penalty area. We're thinking about the sanction, aren't we that's why we're talking about this. 'Is it a denial of an obvious goal scoring opportunity? Four considerations officials have to think about. Direction of play, it's definitely going towards the goal. It's not going out wide. Proximity from goal, well, it's just outside the penalty area. The location of other defenders. Well, there's only Yoro there. The keeper is moving back towards his own goal. 'He has to put the brakes on and possibly come back out. The reason we're talking about it is the fourth consideration, that's control or likelihood of keeping on or gaining control of the ball. Isak's got control of the ball, he's got possession, he's got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro. He's moving at pace at that moment, and a foul comes in and knocks him down. 'And there's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Senne Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. 'That was the referee's call made on the field, and then the VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn't, that if there was any doubt, then it was doubt. 'It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and i think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but i think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.' It’s the third time in the past 14 months that United have been on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials. Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday In September, Pro Ref boss Webb apologised to United when Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand after VAR incorrectly ruled that teammate Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play as he tried to head the ball in an offside position. Last season, Webb acknowledged that the match officials got it wrong when they decided not to send off Brentford captain Nathan Collins for hauling back Bryan Mbeumo inside the box as United lost 3-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium. New United head coach Pochettino blamed Yoro’s red card for the heavy defeat in his first game in charge, and was unhappy that Barrott took no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area moments earlier. ‘It's not okay to start a game in the Premier League with this situation,’ said Pochettino. ‘The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful. ‘In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal. Everyone who plays football can feel it. ‘If you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak. The ball was going to the goalkeeper. ‘If you look before, in the sixth minute, Jacquet on Mbeumo. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty. We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is the truth. ‘It's clear that after eight minutes the plan was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more. ‘The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to the calm: it was an unfair situation that happened.’
