Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Says He Will Knock Out Roided Devin Haney
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is going for the throat with Devin Haney, telling fans on X that he wants Haney to be loaded up on steroids, and it will not save him in their rematch.

WBO welterweight champion Haney is getting bashed by fans this week for refusing to enroll with VADA for his December 19th unification clash with IBF champion Liam Paro in San Francisco. Haney’s decision not to enroll for testing has made him a target for Ryan and fans, who see it as suspicious behavior.

With Ryan’s own history of testing positive for minute amounts of the banned PED Ostarine for his fight with Haney in 2024, he sees it as odd that Haney is not on board with testing for his fight with Paro.

It is a crucial fight for Haney, who needs a victory over the heavy-handed southpaw Paro to move ahead for a big-money rematch with Ryan. That is the one that Haney has been pining away for, bitter still over the memory of being dropped repeatedly by Ryan, arguably saved by the referee in round 7.

“I will KO DEVIN TILL HE CANT WALK ANYMORE EVEN IF HE WAS ON STEROIDS,” Garcia posted on X. “I want him to be so roided up, I want him to feel like he has power just so I can take it away. He is nothing.”

Haney Cannot Fix His Chin

From Ryan’s perspective, it does not matter how much work Haney (33-0-1 NC, 15 KOs) puts in with his training; he is still going to lack power at welterweight, and his habit of dropping his right hand when he jabs is going to make him vulnerable. Ryan took advantage of that flaw to drop him three times with his left hook in their fight in April 2024. Even if Haney does develop a little more power with his weight work, he is still going to need to be able to take Ryan’s left hooks when they land cleanly.

A fighter can build muscle by bulking up or improve their stamina, but there is nothing they can do to improve their punch resistance. Haney is not going to beat Ryan by staying on the outside, jabbing all night. That will not be enough to convince the judges he deserves the win if he is playing it safe, afraid to mix it up for fear of being hurt like he repeatedly was the last time he fought Ryan.

The December 19 Unification Hangover

Devin’s decision not to enroll in VADA for his December 19th unification fight at the Chase Center in San Francisco with Paro (28-1, 16 KOs) has put that fight in jeopardy. Paro has already said he will pull out unless Haney agrees to enroll in VADA. Haney’s dad, Bill, argues that the testing for PEDs is pointless due to there not being enough time.

If Paro pulls out, that would leave Haney with no fight and just his WBO belt. Realistically, he needs two titles to strengthen his position during negotiations with the more popular WBC champion Ryan Garcia. Without that extra belt, Haney is in a bad position trying to get a larger purse split. He would be lucky to be on the small end of a 75/25 split with Ryan without a second title. That is why he needs to be enrolling with VADA pronto so that he does not blow his deal with Paro.

Sports.title: Nobody in America Knows Fury vs. Joshua Is Happening
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are closing in on their Battle of Britain fight in 17 days in Cardiff, and the fight has generated next to no interest for their December 11th bout. For a mega-fight, it’s invisible. Chris Mannix and Sergio Mora put the spotlight on the nonexistent promotion. They mentioned that Netflix and the promoters have done nothing to sell the fight.

“This event needs some promotion,” Mannix said on his channel. “Like, have you seen anything promoting Fury vs Joshua?”

Mora echoed Mannix’s view that the fight’s marketing is nowhere to be found. His thoughts are that the fight should be getting a major promotional push, with it being mentioned everywhere.

“No, I have not. It’s not really being promoted the way it should be,” Mora said. “It should be a mega event. It should be everywhere, on every commercial. If it’s on Netflix, everywhere. I haven’t seen [that].”

Mannix pointed out the lack of visibility in the United States, and that the fight is scheduled for 2:00 AM for the ring walk in Wales to accommodate American prime time.

“Where is the AJ-Fury face-off? Where is that to go viral and build with millions of views to get people excited? The US audience has no idea this fight is happening. There’s nothing out there about this fight.”

The question is, would it even make a difference if there were a Fury vs. Joshua face-off? I don’t see this making a difference. Even if ESPN showed video clips of a face-off, how is that going to help if the fans view the fight as one between two past-their-best heavyweights, collecting a large paycheck in an overdue fight?

With the money Turki Alalshikh is paying Joshua and Fury, said to be $100 million each in guaranteed purses, it takes away the incentive to work hard promoting it. They’re already getting the cash from Turki in purses up front. Eddie Hearn, Frank Warren, Fury, and Joshua don’t need to labor through promoting the event because the money is already there. Why would they need to expend energy conducting daily interviews, flying here and there on a press tour when they’re already getting paid?

For Joshua and Fury, the last thing they want is to be placed in the hot seat, forced to answer questions about why they’ve looked poor in their fights over the last 3 to 7 years.

Fury (39-2-1, 25 KOs) being forced to answer why he chose to fight 46-year-old Mariusz Wach and Arslanbek Makhmudov rather than top contenders. In Joshua’s case, he’s being forced to explain why he didn’t try to avenge his loss to Daniel Dubois after being knocked out.

Getting dropped twice in round 1 by his tune-up opponent, Kristian Prenga, before pulling it out in round 2. It looks so bad how Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) looked in that fight ahead of the Fury clash. That alone makes a clash against Fury a tough sell.

The undercard that is being packaged with the Joshua vs. Fury event looks like it was thrown together on the cheap, hoping fans wouldn’t notice or care to see. They actually do care. Using Martin Bakole as the replacement opponent after Jai Opetaia pulled out to fight 41-year-old Deontay Wilder hasn’t gone over well with fans. Netflix should have put their foot down and insisted on a quality opponent to be brought in to face Wilder. The rest of the undercard is useless fights that don’t belong on this card.

Sports.title: De La Hoya Wants WBA Rules Bent For Ryan Garcia vs Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya is trying to talk a Ryan Garcia vs. Teofimo Lopez unification into existence before the WBA has even cleared the paperwork.

Golden Boy wants the sanctioning body to shove mandatory challenger Jack Catterall aside for February so Lopez can bring his WBA welterweight belt into a bigger money fight. If the WBA refuses to budge, Lopez has to either defend against Catterall or drop the strap.

“A unification supersedes anything,” said De La Hoya on Brian Custer’s The Last Stand. De La Hoya claimed both fighters want the bout and named Las Vegas and Madison Square Garden as possible venues, speaking as though approval was already in the bag. WBA president Gilberto Mendoza poured cold water on that November 20 by confirming no special permit has been granted. Lopez’s manager, Keith Connolly, admitted the process is still dragging on.

Catterall Earned His Title Shot

Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) inherited the Catterall obligation the second he squeezed past Rolly Romero by majority decision in August to grab the WBA title. Back in May in Giza, Egypt, Catterall dropped and outboxed unbeaten contender Shakhram Giyasov over twelve rounds to lock down the mandatory spot. That claim stayed glued to the belt when Lopez took it from Romero. Lopez tried to get out of the fight, only for the WBA to reaffirm the order on November 11.

Golden Boy is banking on WBA Rule C.39, which allows the organization to consider a special permit for a unification bout. Until the WBA actually signs off, Catterall holds an active order for his shot. Even De La Hoya admitted Catterall deserves the fight.

Why Lopez Needs The Belt

Going into a February 6 bout with Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) without a title weakens Lopez’s hand at the negotiating table and leaves only Garcia’s WBC belt up for grabs. Garcia is riding high after winning the WBC strap from Mario Barrios in February and blowing away Conor Benn in two rounds in September. Facing Catterall first carries obvious danger for Lopez’s camp. Catterall is a slick southpaw who can stink out a fight and ruin a massive payday before Lopez ever gets near Garcia.

The WBA holding its ground does not kill the February 6 fight. Lopez can drop the belt, walk in as the challenger for Garcia’s WBC title, and let Golden Boy sell the event anyway. Only one belt would be at stake instead of two. If Lopez wants to keep his WBA title, he has to deal with Catterall first because the sanctioning body has already ordered that defense twice.

Sports.title: Andy Hiraoka Is the Right Test for Richardson Hitchins
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he is returning in February, though he still has no opponent. Zuffa Boxing should give him Andy Hiraoka. More than two years will have passed by then since Hitchins edged Liam Paro by split decision for the IBF light welterweight title. Zuffa paid for an unbeaten former champion. It needs to put him in with someone who can actually beat him.

“FEBUARY I’m Back !!!!” Hitchins posted on X without naming an opponent or a city. Dan Rafael reported in October that Zuffa was mapping out early 2027 dates for Hitchins after talks for a Keyshawn Davis bout stalled. Both Hitchins and Hiraoka used to campaign at light welterweight before moving up to 147 pounds. Hitchins already made his welterweight debut on July 26 against Ricardo Salas, while new Zuffa signee Hiraoka will be fighting at 147 for the first time in his promotional debut.

What Hiraoka Brings at 147

Hitchins stopped George Kambosos Jr. in eight rounds at 140 and swept every round on all three scorecards against Salas in New York. Those shutout scores against Salas show how cleanly Hitchins worked from the outside. They also skip over how frequently he clinched once Salas closed the gap. Hitchins grabbed, waited on the referee to break them, and went right back to his jab without taking much back.

Hiraoka (24-1, 19 KOs) makes those clinches harder to pull off. The southpaw works behind a sharp right jab and digs to the body on the way in. If Hiraoka keeps a hand free when Hitchins reaches to tie him up, Hitchins will spend the night resetting his feet instead of dictating the pace. Hiraoka will have to earn his entry, too. He is coming off a decision loss to Gary Antuanne Russell down at light welterweight in February, so a February 2027 date would show whether his power holds up in his welterweight debut.

Zuffa Needs a Real Answer

If Zuffa wants to book fights the way the UFC does, this matchup is sitting right in front of it. It has two welterweights under contract whose styles clash cleanly. Nobody outside the camp knows how much say Hitchins and his manager, Keith Connolly, have over opponents. If Hitchins has approval rights, passing on Hiraoka makes business sense for him. Keyshawn Davis brings a bigger name and a bigger payday for the risk. Hiraoka offers plenty of trouble inside the ropes without bringing half the attention.

Hitchins (21-0, 8 KOs) and the Salas fight already showed what happens when an opponent lets him stand on the outside and jab all night. Hiraoka won’t give him that kind of space. Putting them together in February is the quickest way for Zuffa to learn what happens when Hitchins gets pushed onto his heels for twelve rounds.

If Zuffa wants to know what Hitchins is really worth at 147, matching him against Hiraoka will give them an answer. Better to get that read now than waste another year protecting him.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Waited Ten Years To Share Schizophrenia Diagnosis
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says doctors diagnosed him with schizophrenia after he beat Wladimir Klitschko in November 2015. He waited nearly ten years to mention it, saving the reveal for a Netflix documentary timed to his fight with Anthony Joshua. The film drops November 27, two weeks before Netflix streams Fury vs. Joshua live from Cardiff on December 11.

“Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” said Fury in excerpts published by BBC Sport. Netflix tied the documentary directly to the Joshua bout in its October 29 announcement, putting the fight right in the headline. You don’t need to guess why the film is dropping now. Fury, 38, hasn’t explained publicly why he waited a full decade until the biggest fight and biggest purse of his career to share a diagnosis he skipped in earlier accounts.

What Fury Said About His 2016 Crisis

Fury was talking publicly about his mental health back in October 2016, less than a year after taking the unified heavyweight titles from Klitschko. He told Rolling Stone he was dealing with depression, drinking heavily and using cocaine. He also said he had been told he had a form of bipolar disorder.

He revisited that breakdown in his book Gloves Off. Fury wrote that doctors told him he had bipolar disorder, paranoia and anxiety. Schizophrenia never appeared in that version. In the Netflix film, Fury says he heard voices threatening him and his family, thought the radio was talking to him, and begged his wife Paris to get him out of a hospital in June 2016 because “the Illuminati” wanted him.

Fury went into that hospital with a suspected heart attack, which doctors diagnosed as an anxiety attack. He says a London psychiatrist later confirmed schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. According to the Los Angeles Times, Paris remembers the psychiatrist telling them Fury was “a mild schizophrenic.”

Fury says a 2017 Halloween night out in a skeleton costume served as his turning point before he returned to the ring and stopped Deontay Wilder in 2020. Everything in these excerpts still comes down to what Fury and his wife say happened, with no word from the doctor who saw him.

Netflix gets a fresh promotional hook heading into a December 11 heavyweight main event it is carrying live. The streamer already owns footage of Fury’s comeback and title runs. He left that diagnosis out of Rolling Stone and his own book for ten years, then brought it out right before the biggest payday of his career. None of that helps him with Joshua’s right hand in Cardiff.

Sports.title: Rayo Calls Shakur Stevenson ‘Not a Real Fighter’
Sports.content:
Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela had plenty to say about Shakur Stevenson leaving Zuffa Boxing without ever fighting him. In an interview with The Ring, the former 140-pound titleholder accused Stevenson of chasing safer paydays while ignoring a dangerous opponent who had already beaten two of Stevenson’s common reference points.

Stevenson spent his time pushing for a bout with Manny Pacquiao and hoping Lamont Roach would get past William Zepeda so he could fight Roach next, according to Valenzuela. His own name barely came up.

“Honestly, I was kind of pissed,” said Valenzuela to Ring Magazine when asked about Stevenson’s departure. “I was like, ‘What a pussy. You’re not a real fighter.’ He just wants to make money and cash out, big fights.”

What Valenzuela’s Resume Showed

A split decision win over Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz gave Valenzuela the WBA super lightweight title and took out a fighter Stevenson had gone back and forth with on social media. Valenzuela also pointed to his knockout claim over Edwin De Los Santos, a puncher who gave Stevenson twelve difficult rounds in November 2023.

“I beat Pit Bull Cruz. I knocked out Edwin De Los Santos, the guy who gave him his toughest fight. So, why not fight me?” said Valenzuela.

Pacquiao still draws a crowd and a large purse even in his forties, which makes the business appeal obvious. Roach had far less commercial traction, especially after Zepeda dominated him. Watching Stevenson openly root for Roach to win while saying almost nothing about a fight with him left Valenzuela convinced Stevenson was looking for the path of least resistance.

“He just wants to box comfortably. He doesn’t want to feel no pressure,” said Valenzuela. “That’s what I do. I bring the pressure, and I bring stress.”

Negotiating Habits and What Comes Next

Ashton Sylve was another name mentioned for Stevenson. Valenzuela questioned what fighting an unproven prospect would say about Stevenson’s willingness to take real risks. Stevenson’s negotiating habits drew criticism too, from weight terms for Devin Haney to wanting Raymond Muratalla at 135 pounds after Stevenson had already moved up to 140.

“He’s not up for a gamble. You know, you got to bet on yourself in a tough fight,” said Valenzuela.

Attention now turns to Floyd Schofield and a chance to become a two-time world champion. Stevenson walked away from Zuffa without ever finding out how his defense holds up against a taller southpaw willing to press him for twelve rounds.

Sports.title: Aaron McKenna Likely To Drop Belt To Avoid Amari Jones
Sports.content:
Aaron McKenna will likely drop his IBF middleweight title rather than defend it against Amari Jones if the sanctioning body orders the bout, according to Chris Mannix.

Right now, that belt looks like a hot potato McKenna is just keeping warm until his December check clears in Saudi Arabia. I can understand why. A negotiation with former WBO champion Denzel Bentley pays better and gives McKenna a cleaner style, assuming both camps revisit the fight that fell apart in September.

Mannix said on his podcast with Sergio Mora that people close to the situation, including on McKenna’s side, expect the champion to pass on Jones. The IBF is expected to order the mandatory after McKenna’s scheduled December defense in Saudi Arabia. Mora didn’t sugarcoat the matchup. “We’ll get a new champion at 160 if that happens,” said Mora.

The Denzel Bentley Alternative

McKenna and Bentley had already agreed to a unification bout before the WBO ordered Bentley to face Yoenli Hernandez. The WBO stripped Bentley in October when he skipped that obligation. Bentley went through with his London fight against Shane Mosley Jr. this month instead, dropping him in the second round on the way to a unanimous decision. Zuffa Boxing promotes both McKenna and Bentley, giving them a fight they already know how to make.

Bentley still poses real danger. He carries enough power to make McKenna think twice before trading, and the Mosley win proved he can bank rounds after an early knockdown without chasing a stoppage. McKenna still gets his own shots off much easier against Bentley than against Jones. Both men also have a real following in Britain and Ireland, which makes the gate work.

What Jones Brings To The Ring

Jones creates a completely different set of problems. He works behind a long jab from both stances. When DeAndre Pettis shelled up upstairs, Jones went to the body until the openings appeared. Mannix noted that Jones told him a cut on the bridge of his nose cost him his final few weeks of sparring before that bout. He still became the first fighter to stop Pettis. McKenna wants to trade in the pocket. Jones has the reach and power to punish him on the way in and keep hitting him once he gets there.

Mannix expects McKenna to move up in weight if he vacates. That leaves Jones fighting for the vacant belt. Jahi Tucker sits next in the rankings, though Mannix heard George Liddard could jump to the No. 2 spot with a win in December. Mannix called Jones against Liddard in early 2027 his “educated guess.”

Bentley already proved he will take a fight without a title on the line. Once the Riyadh purse clears, McKenna can drop the strap and cash in against Bentley rather than walk into Jones’s jab.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Warns Liam Paro Over VADA Testing Dispute
Sports.content:
Bill Haney brought up the possibility of a contract breach on Monday if Liam Paro walks away from his December 19 welterweight unification fight with Devin Haney over VADA testing. Speaking on Instagram Live, Bill mentioned lawyers and asked whether Paro’s side is looking for an exit from the Chase Center main event in San Francisco.

“I think it looks like you might be finding reasons to breach outside of the agreement,” said Bill Haney. He said lawyers handle those disputes and noted that the Haneys would face consequences too if they failed to meet what they signed up for. Bill stopped short of threatening a lawsuit, adding that Devin is already in camp and preparing to fight.

What Bill Says Happened In Negotiations

Bill claims Paro’s team never raised VADA testing during negotiations and only brought it up publicly after the contract was signed. Paro and his promoter, Matt Rose of No Limit Boxing, say VADA was agreed to during talks. Paro has publicly pressed Devin to enroll, though whether Paro himself has entered the pool remains unconfirmed.

Bill pointed to Devin’s bout against Brian Norman Jr. to show how he handles testing when it is part of a deal. VADA was written into that contract before Norman signed, and the disagreement then was over when Norman would enroll. With Paro, Bill said the bout came together on roughly four or five weeks’ notice, and he considers 12 weeks the minimum for VADA.

“Had it been a longer time where we would have had to negotiate, then I would have put it in the agreement,” said Bill.

The contract may say one thing. Devin still has nearly four weeks to volunteer for the program he spent years promoting. Bill said he stopped pushing Devin to enroll after leaving year-round testing because they took ridicule while few other fighters joined. That is a tough sell when the opponent is asking for the exact testing the Haneys used to champion.

What Paro Faces If He Walks

Paro is unlikely to pull out. A welterweight unification and the purse that comes with it would be difficult for him and No Limit Boxing to replace. If he stays in the fight, the Norman bout shows what he has to solve. Haney builds rounds behind his jab and quick combinations, then backs out behind an extended lead hand or ties up his opponent the moment the distance closes. He held Norman repeatedly. Paro has to punch as Haney reaches to clinch, before the referee breaks them and resets Paro at the end of the jab.

Bill says the testing already in place is enough for him. That gets harder to defend if Paro pulls the upset on December 19. You cannot turn down VADA when your opponent asks for it in November and then complain about the rules in January.

Ghana News.title: Addiction To Assignment launches National Anti-Drug High School and Youth Tour
Ghana News.content:
The Addiction to Assignment initiative has launched its National Anti-Drug High School and Youth Tour, a nationwide campaign aimed at raising awareness about drug abuse and preventing substance use among young people.

The initiative, spearheaded by Timothy Bentum, draws on his personal journey from cocaine and heroin addiction to sobriety and purpose, with the aim of using lived experience, celebrity influence and public education to confront the growing drug menace among Ghana’s youth.

The tour is being undertaken in collaboration with the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) and JoyPrime TV.

Speaking at the launch, NACOC Director-General, Maj. Gen. Maxwell Obuba Mantey pledged his outfit’s full support for the initiative.

Discussions are also underway with the Ghana Education Service to facilitate the smooth implementation of the programme across schools nationwide.

The campaign will bring together personalities from the creative arts industry and other stakeholders to engage students directly on the dangers of drug abuse and the importance of making positive life choices.

Organisers are calling on government, corporate Ghana, parents and the general public to support the initiative in safeguarding the future of the next generation.

Ghana News.title: GSE appoints Kojo Darpaah as head of GFIM
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE) has appointed Kojo Darpaah, CFA, as Head of the Ghana Fixed Income Market (GFIM), effective November 30, 2026.

Kojo joins the GSE from Fidelity Bank Ghana, where he served as Director, Financial and Capital Markets with responsibility for the bank's foreign exchange, fixed income, and capital markets businesses.

He brings over 15 years of experience spanning treasury and financial markets, investment banking, and corporate governance.

He began his career at CalBank and has since held progressively senior leadership positions across Ghana’s banking sector, including roles at Barclays Bank Ghana, First National Bank Ghana, UMB, and Fidelity Bank Ghana.

His career has encompassed trading, treasury management and strategic leadership, positioning him as a financial market professional with deep expertise in market development and institutional growth.

He has worked extensively with regulators, local and offshore institutional investors, and development finance institutions, and was an inaugural member of the National Technical Committee that developed the operational framework for the GFIM.

He holds an MSc in Financial Engineering from Claremont Graduate University, USA, and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)holder. He served as an Independent Non-Executive Board Member and Board Treasurer of Fairtrade Africa and as Chair of the Advocacy, Research and Standards Committee of CFA Society Ghana.

In his new role, Mr. Darpaah will oversee and manage all activities of the GFIM and lead the development and implementation of strategic initiatives to enhance the growth, efficiency, and competitiveness of the fixed income market, including its expansion to corporate issuers.

His appointment further strengthens the GSE's commitment to advancing the Ghana Fixed Income Market and supporting the growth, depth, and efficiency of Ghana's capital market.

Ghana News.title: Don’t punish BECE candidates for GES failures – Adutwum’s spokesperson tells Education Minister
Ghana News.content:
The spokesperson for former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has criticised a directive by the current Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, concerning BECE candidates, arguing that learners should not be penalised for administrative failures within the Ghana Education Service (GES).

In a statement, Yaw Opoku Mensah described the directive as “misplaced, unjustifiable, and deeply misguided”, insisting that the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) registration process is managed by GES and not individual candidates.

He said the examination was administered by the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) based on submissions processed through the GES administrative structure, making the service responsible for any irregularities in the registration process.

According to him, headteachers register candidates electronically in line with WAEC's requirements before forwarding the information to District Examination Officers for processing and verification through the Student CASS Portal.

He explained that an Entry Report is generated to allow for corrections before the final submission to WAEC within the stipulated October/November registration period.

“Every stage of this process falls within the administrative responsibility of GES, under the supervision of the Deputy Director-General responsible for Quality and Access, whose portfolio encompasses Schools and Instruction,” he said.

Mr Mensah maintained that candidates do not independently register for the examination and should therefore not be held responsible for errors or omissions arising from the administrative process.

He questioned why learners whose details had been verified and processed through an official government system should suffer the consequences of failures they had no control over.

“So, how does a Minister arrive at the absurd conclusion that learners whose details were verified, registered, and processed through an official government administrative system should suffer the consequences of an institutional failure they neither caused nor had the authority to prevent?” he asked.

He called on the government to investigate any breaches in the registration process and hold the officials responsible accountable instead of imposing sanctions on candidates.

“If GES submitted the names, then GES must answer for the integrity of those submissions. If there were procedural breaches, investigate them. If officials failed to discharge their responsibilities, sanction them. But do not sacrifice the academic future of innocent children to conceal or compensate for institutional incompetence,” he said.

The spokesperson also raised concerns about what he described as the apparent abandonment or scaling down of the Ghana Education Service Management Information System (GESMIS), which he said was introduced under the previous administration to improve the management of educational data.

He said the system was designed to support administrative decision-making, institutional planning, operational efficiency and accountability within GES.

Mr Mensah questioned why the current administration had not strengthened and expanded the digital infrastructure, arguing that weakening such systems could contribute to administrative challenges.

“If the current leadership has deliberately weakened or abandoned systems capable of improving efficiency, transparency, and accountability, it cannot escape responsibility for the administrative consequences,” he said.

He urged the Education Minister to hold GES leadership accountable for any failures in the registration process, stressing that learners had no role in managing the registration portal or supervising examination entries.

“The children are not the administrators. They are not the District Examination Officers. They do not manage the registration portal, and they certainly do not supervise the examination registration process,” he said.

He added that the academic future of learners should not be jeopardised by administrative negligence or institutional failures.

Ghana News.content:
Nutrifoods Ghana named Confectionery Company of the Year at 6th Chamber Business Awards

By Myjoyonline,com

Nutrifoods Ghana Limited, a leading manufacturer of snacks and culinary products in Ghana’s fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector, has been named Confectionery Company of the Year at the 6th Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GNCCI) Chamber Business Awards, in recognition of its commitment to manufacturing excellence, innovation, product quality and contribution to Ghana’s industrial development.

The recognition underscores Nutrifoods Ghana’s continued dedication to delivering quality products that meet consumers’ everyday needs while contributing to the growth and competitiveness of Ghana’s manufacturing industry.

Organised by the Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the Chamber Business Awards is one of the country’s prominent business recognition platforms, celebrating outstanding companies and individuals whose performance, leadership and innovation continue to shape Ghana’s business landscape. This year’s ceremony was held under the theme, “Shaping a Resilient Future: The Role of Sustainability and AI in Business”, bringing together key players from across the private sector to celebrate excellence and spotlight opportunities for sustainable economic growth.

As a member of the GNCCI, Nutrifoods Ghana continues to engage with a platform that champions private sector development, advocates business-friendly policies and promotes an enabling environment for enterprises to thrive. Through its engagement with government, industry stakeholders and development partners, the Chamber plays an important role in advancing the interests of businesses and strengthening Ghana’s economic ecosystem.

Reacting to the recognition, Mr Jay Anjaria, Business and Country Head of Nutrifoods Ghana Limited, expressed gratitude to the company’s employees, customers, distributors, suppliers and business partners, acknowledging their invaluable contributions to the company’s success.

“This award is a testament to our unwavering commitment to delivering quality products that meet the everyday snacking needs of Ghanaians. It reflects the dedication of our people and the trust our consumers place in our brands. We remain focused on investing in innovation, strengthening our capabilities and creating greater value for consumers every day,” he said.

The awards ceremony took place on Saturday, November 21, 2026, at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra, with Her Excellency Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, Vice-President of the Republic of Ghana, as Special Guest of Honour. In her remarks, she underscored the critical role of a strong and competitive private sector in accelerating economic growth, creating jobs and expanding opportunities for Ghanaians.

She also highlighted government initiatives, including the New Economy: New Ghana, Jobs and Prosperity Programme (2027–2030), aimed at addressing structural challenges confronting the private sector and unlocking new pathways for economic growth and prosperity.

The award further reinforces Nutrifoods Ghana Limited’s position within Ghana’s confectionery manufacturing industry and its commitment to building trusted brands, delivering products consumers love and creating moments of joy in homes and communities across the country.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s electricity crisis: Falling fuel consumption is good news, but grid reliability remains a concern
Ghana News.content:
Over the past few weeks I have been a dashboard I built and call the National Electricity Intelligence Platform (NEiP). I built it to pull together everything electricity in Ghana. It’s a sub-dashboard within the bigger Ghana Energy Intelligence Platform.

Peak demand in 2025 hit 4,283 MW, an 8.4% jump on 2024. Total electricity consumption reached 27,015 GWh — above every Base Case projection.

But the cost was staggering. The 2025 plan budgeted for 344,387 barrels of Heavy Fuel Oil. The actual liquid fuel burned, according to the Energy Commission, reached 3,092,066 barrels — nearly 9 times what was planned.

AKSA alone burned 1,040,335 barrels of HFO. SAPP and Cenpower between them burned nearly 2.3 million barrels of LCO and DFO combined.

Natural gas supply fell 5.3% short. To keep the lights on, the grid turned to the most expensive fuels on the planet. We paid for the liquid fuels in scarce foreign exchange and that new levy that was imposed on us.

Last night, when I was going through the National Petroleum Authority's January–September 2026 supply data, I saw some good news. The data showed power plants consumed only 14,269 metric tonnes of Fuel Oil and just 1,441 metric tonnes of Diesel across nine months. This means that the fuel levy is not needed again because we have reduced our dependence on liquid fuel.

AKSA alone burned the equivalent of roughly 142,000 MT of HFO in 2025. If the Jan–Sep 2026 pace holds through Q4, power-sector liquid fuel consumption this year will land at around 10% of 2025 levels. Costs will reduce and the levy must go.

NPA's Q2 2026 bulletin confirms the same direction of travel for fuel imports. Fuel Oil imports fell 76.22% year-on-year against Q2 2025.

Natural gas supply has materially improved in 2026. Whether through better WAGP flows, higher N-Gas imports, or firmer Jubilee/TEN/Sankofa production, I don’t know. The 2027 Energy and Electricity Supply plans will tell us. What makes me happy is that the single biggest driver of our 2025 fuel bill pain appears to have eased. If this holds, Ghana will spend substantially less on thermal fuel in 2026 than the Energy Commission's worst-case US$1.68 billion projection. So the levy must go!

Easing gas supply does not mean the grid is fixed. The Energy Commission's 2026 Outlook (published this February) warned that dependable capacity (5,455 MW) would fall below the 18% Grid Code reserve margin in 11 of 12 months this year.

Only August cleared the bar in the commission’s projections.

Under the High Case, the margin turned negative in February, March, April, May and June.

Then 23 April 2026 arrived. A fire at the Akosombo switchyard removed 1,020 MW of hydro plus 101 MW at Kpong in a single afternoon. About 23% of national peak demand was erased in one incident. The whole grid shutdown. Recovery took 11 days through novel external switchyard injection. All six units are now fully restored.

That fire laid bare a single-point-of-failure risk we have no redundancy for.

GRIDCo's 2025 ESP finally quantified what engineers in the field have long known. At Kadjebi substation, voltage drops to 38.5 kV on a 69 kV nominal network — just 56% of what consumers should receive.

Towns like Bimbila, Kpandai, Salaga and Kete Krachi are served by 34.5 kV feeders running more than 200 km from Yendi. Motors cannot start, fridges cannot cool and industrial equipment trip.

GRIDCo quantified the suppressed demand on NEDCo feeders alone to be 25.78 MW / 151.3 GWh of electricity Ghanaians would consume if the grid could deliver it reliably. Historical NEDCo data shows that when voltages on affected feeders are improved, consumption rises 24%. That is demand nobody is counting.

NEDCo’s operational area demand is small compared to ECG’s so if voltage improvement increases consumption by 24%, just imagine what that would do in the ECG operational areas.

GRIDCo projects peak demand to rise from 4,283 MW (2025) to 6,198 MW by 2030. That is a 1,915 MW jump in five years. To hold reliability at the Grid Code's 18% reserve margin, Ghana must commission an average of 374 MW of new dependable generation every single year.

AKSA Anwomaso began operating in December 2025. CENIT Anwomaso came online in April 2026. The Yendi 50 MW solar came in July.

This is all good but nowhere near enough. If the proposed New Economy can take off, the current need must be met with enough produced to power the New Economy.

The Bridge Power Phase II, Rotan 600 MW, SAAP Solar 200 MW, KTPP combined-cycle — every one of these has to deliver on time, or we enter 2030 already short.

When are we commissioning the 400 mmscfd regasification Tema LNG facility? Or its been done and we didn’t notice?.

Suppressed demand is real. The adundum adundum is happening. The low voltage is widespread.

It would be great to hear from the government the compressing electricity RESET programme and how that would solve our problems.

What we measure, we can manage. What we cannot see, we cannot fix.

Sources: National Petroleum Authority Jan–Sep 2026 National Supply · NPA Q2 2026 Downstream Petroleum Statistical Bulletin · Energy Commission 2026 Energy Outlook for Ghana (February 2026) · GRIDCo 2025 Electricity Supply Plan · GRIDCo Daily System Load Reports.

Ghana News.title: Bagbin raises concerns over reduction in Parliament’s 2027 budget allocation
Ghana News.content:
Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, the Speaker of Parliament

The Speaker of Parliament, Alban Bagbin, has expressed dissatisfaction with a reduction in Parliament’s proposed budget allocation for the 2027 financial year, warning that it could affect the effective functioning of the House.

Parliament had requested GH¢2,953,139,666 for its operations in 2027, but the President has recommended an allocation of GH¢2,283,561,480, representing a reduction of approximately GH¢669.6 million.

Mr Bagbin said the shortfall would affect key areas of expenditure, particularly capital projects, goods and services, as well as the recruitment of additional technical and expert personnel.

He said the reduced allocation could also limit Parliament’s ability to engage consultants and other technical professionals to strengthen its operations.

“Our requests will not be fully met, and there are areas that we are called upon to look at, particularly with regard to capital expenditure and goods and services,” he said.

“Our request to also add additional expert and technical hands have also been affected in the compensation of employees, and so we may not be able to ask for some consultancies and some technical people to support us in some of the areas that we need to be strengthened to do our work,” he added.

The Speaker consequently referred the matter to the Committee on Parliament, alongside the leadership of the Budget and Finance Committees, to consider the proposed allocation and report to the House.

The proposed allocations form part of more than GH¢5 billion earmarked for Parliament, the Judiciary and the Ghana Audit Service for the 2027 financial year.

The budgetary provisions are made in accordance with Article 179 of the 1992 Constitution, which provides for budgetary allocations to state institutions, including the other arms of government.

Ghana News.title: Police kill suspected serial rapist and robber linked to seven cases in Kade
Ghana News.content:
The Eastern South Regional Police Command says a 39-year-old ex-convict suspected of carrying out a series of rape and robbery attacks in the Kade area of the Eastern Region has died after sustaining gunshot wounds during a police operation.

The suspect, identified as Kwaku Asomani, was also linked to the murder of a 28-year-old woman, Esther Opoku, whose body was found on October 1, 2026, opposite Hotel De Nyarko in the Guggisberg area of Kade.

In a press release dated November 24, the Police said preliminary investigations had linked Asomani to seven incidents of robbery and rape involving female victims between February 19 and November 10, 2026.

The victims, aged between 18 and 54, were allegedly robbed of various sums of money and personal belongings before being sexually assaulted.

The Police said a team of investigators from the Anti-Armed Robbery Unit of the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) Headquarters, working with personnel from the Kade District Police Command, located the suspect on November 14 at Assemblies of God in Kade.

The operation followed what the Command described as intensive surveillance.

Asomani reportedly sustained gunshot wounds during the operation and died as a result.

A search of his person and residence led to the retrieval of a face cap and other clothing items, which the Police said had been identified by some of the victims.

The Eastern South Regional Police Command has extended its condolences to the family of Esther Opoku and said it is making arrangements to provide psychosocial support to the surviving victims.

The Command also reaffirmed the Ghana Police Service's commitment to combating violent crime and ensuring public safety.

Ghana News.title: Trade Minister pushes stronger trade and investment ties with Germany
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has called for stronger trade and investment partnerships between Ghana and Germany, with emphasis on industrial development, local production, technology transfer and export growth.

Addressing the sixth German-African Business Summit in Accra, she said the government was committed to translating existing diplomatic relations into meaningful commercial partnerships and investment opportunities.

She noted that trade in goods between Ghana and Germany amounted to approximately €564 million in 2025, describing the figure as an indication of the potential to deepen economic cooperation, particularly in local processing, manufacturing and technical skills development.

Mrs Ofosu-Adjare said Ghana’s position as host of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat offered businesses an opportunity to access markets across the continent.

She, however, stressed the need to strengthen local enterprises to enable them to meet international standards, improve productivity and compete effectively in regional and global markets.

The Minister highlighted government initiatives, including the Feed the Industry Initiative and the Accelerated Export Development Programme, which are aimed at securing raw material supplies, supporting local businesses and expanding Ghana’s export capacity.

She also pointed to Germany’s partnership through the Private Sector and Innovation Promotion in Ghana Programme, which is expected to support more than 1,100 enterprises by 2028.

On efforts to improve the business environment, Mrs Ofosu-Adjare disclosed that her Ministry had developed a proposed Business Regulatory Reform Bill to address overlapping regulations and delays in business approvals.

She said the proposed legislation was intended to simplify regulatory requirements, make compliance easier for businesses and improve the efficiency of their operations.

The Minister urged German and African businesses to use the summit to explore investment opportunities, build stronger commercial relationships and identify practical areas for collaboration.

She expressed confidence that stronger partnerships between Ghanaian and German businesses would accelerate industrial transformation, create employment opportunities, particularly for young people, and support sustainable economic growth.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Colombia at a Crossroads: Searching for peace amid conflict
World.content:
A decade after Colombia’s peace accords, former FARC fighter and artist honours killed signatories with a mural.

Yuheni Izquierdo, a former FARC fighter turned artist, paints a mural commemorating fellow peace signatories killed since Colombia’s 2016 Havana peace accords. More than 50 years of armed conflict formally ended with the agreement, but hundreds of signatories have since been killed as armed groups carry out reprisals and fight for territorial control.

Yuheni fears that the escalating violence threatens to return the country to a past that claimed more than 450,000 lives and hopes her mural will inspire Colombians to believe that a lasting peace is possible.

Colombia at a Crossroads is a documentary film by Rodrigo Vazquez Salessi.

World.title: Cameroon separatist leader pleads not guilty at war crimes trial in Norway
World.content:
Lucas Cho Ayaba is accused of remotely planning attacks that killed and injured dozens of civilians.

Share Cameroon separatist leader pleads not guilty at war crimes trial in Norway on social media

Cameroonian separatist leader Lucas Cho Ayaba has pleaded not guilty in a Norwegian court to being an accessory to war crimes and “terrorism”, charges that carry a sentence of up to 30 years.

The 54-year-old, who appeared in a court in Oslo on Tuesday, is accused of involvement in planning two attacks in Cameroon from Norway, helping to select targets and pay for explosives.

Prosecutors say Ayaba, also known as Cho Lucas Yabah, remotely led the separatist Amazonia Governing Council and commanded its armed wing, the Amazonia Defence Forces, from 2017 until 2024, when he was arrested in Norway, where he has lived since 2008.

Francophone-majority Cameroon has been gripped for nearly 10 years by conflict between state security forces and separatists demanding the independence of two Anglophone regions in the country’s west to form what supporters call “Ambazonia”.

In February 2023, three improvised devices exploded during a mountain run race near Buea in southwestern Cameroon, killing a 38-year-old woman and injuring 19 civilians.

In February of the following year, another improvised device killed a 15-year-old girl during a Youth Day celebration in Nkambe, northwestern Cameroon. More than 90 civilians were wounded, with some undergoing amputations.

‘Send him to hell’

Ayaba is also alleged to have encouraged or ordered the murder or attempted murder of captives and to have orchestrated the torture or humiliation of four women accused of having intimate relations with Cameroonian soldiers.



“Messages on WhatsApp are key evidence in this case,” prosecutor Carl Fredrik Fari told the AFP news agency.

“Wrap a rope around his neck and send him to hell,” Ayaba allegedly said in an audio message sent on WhatsApp in October 2023, after receiving videos showing a mistreated prisoner believed to be a Cameroonian soldier.

Ayaba’s lawyer, Morten Engesbak, told AFP that Ayaba “sees himself as the leader of a struggle to liberate a population that has been oppressed for very many years by the Cameroonian authorities”.

The unrest began in late 2016 after Anglophone lawyers and teachers protested against the appointment of Francophone magistrates unfamiliar with British common law to courts in English-speaking regions, and French-speaking teachers unable to communicate fluently in English.

The protests were met with a violent government crackdown and eventually gave rise to a separatist movement seeking independence for the two regions.

The UN says at least 6,000 civilians have been killed since 2016. More than 330,000 people were displaced within Cameroon in 2026 and another 100,000 took refuge in neighbouring Nigeria.

The trial in the Oslo district court is expected to last until March 12.

World.title: US sanctions on Lebanon’s Hezbollah-affiliates may have limited impact
World.content:
Analysts say US sanctions unlikely to weaken Hezbollah significantly, but risk hurting the Lebanese populace.

Beirut, Lebanon – New United States sanctions on an organisation linked to the Iranian-backed Lebanese group Hezbollah will have a limited impact beyond the political messaging the punishment provides, analysts have told Al Jazeera.

The organisation – a charity called Wa Ta’awanu Association – was among the entities and individuals targeted by the US Treasury in new sanctions announced on November 18, accusing it of being a “front organisation” for Hezbollah. The Treasury said the sanctions were an effort to disrupt Hezbollah’s financing networks.

The sanctions are part of a US campaign against Hezbollah, a Shia political and military group. Washington has put pressure on the Lebanese government to make progress on disarming Hezbollah, which has been engaged in an on-off war with Israel for the past 40 years.

But experts told Al Jazeera, the sanctions will do little to change Lebanon’s domestic situation, in which Hezbollah has been one of the major powers – if not the major power – over the past two decades.

“[The US] is threatening to impose sanctions on political, judicial and security figures but that won’t change the reality,” Qassem Kassir, a Lebanese journalist close to Hezbollah, told Al Jazeera. “Sanctions or the threat of sanctions will not change the reality inside Lebanon.”

Lebanese media reports have suggested that the US, frustrated by the Lebanese government’s lack of progress in disarming the Iran-backed group, could apply sanctions beyond direct Hezbollah affiliates and start to target bankers and businessmen.



“There are other packages, a second, third, maybe a fourth [round of sanctions],” Ali Hamade, a Lebanese journalist with Annahar, claimed in a video posted to social media. “It will focus on Hezbollah funding and money smuggling efforts and may involve several bankers, figures in the world of Lebanese finance and business, in the real estate sector and contractors.

He added that politicians, security personnel, judges, and figures in Lebanese public administration were unlikely to face sanctions yet.

Targeting Hezbollah-affiliated organisations

Hezbollah, a Shia-dominated movement which emerged during the Lebanese civil war, is part of a wider network of Iran-linked groups in the region. The group is believed to receive direct financing from Tehran, as well as its own financing networks.

In its sanctions announcement, the US Treasury claimed that the Wa Ta’awanu Association “provides cover for Hizballah’s activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services”.

But Kassir said the group provided assistance to needy Lebanese people.

“Unfortunately, the Americans and some Lebanese parties want to prevent any assistance or service from reaching people,” he said. “However, sanctions will not stop the work of the Wa Ta’awanu Association, just as it has not been able to stop the Al Qard Al Hassan, educational institutions, construction companies and Jihad Al-Binaa.”

Al Qard Al Hassan, a financial institution, and Jihad Al-Binaa, a construction company, are part of a wide array of Hezbollah-affiliated organisations that have been sanctioned by the US, though both companies also employ or serve people not affiliated with Hezbollah.

Sanctions as leverage

Israel has continued to attack what it says are Hezbollah targets in Lebanon intermittently, despite a “ceasefire” agreement earlier this year.

It also continues to hold territory it invaded up to 10km (6.2 miles) into Lebanese territory.

Israel – backed by the US – has tied its withdrawal from Lebanon to the full disarmament of Hezbollah. Talks between the Israeli and Lebanese governments were held earlier this year and led to a Framework Agreement in June, which designated so-called “pilot zones” where Israeli troops would withdraw, and the Lebanese army would deploy to disarm Hezbollah.

But the pilot zone programme has had little success, as Israel still refuses to withdraw from new territories and accuses the Lebanese army of failing to disarm Hezbollah in the existing pilot zones.

In the meantime, the US has looked for other means to pressure Hezbollah, as it continues attacks against the group’s patron, Iran.



“The US treats sanctions as one of several forms of pressure that it can exert on Hezbollah’s financial networks,” David Wood, the senior Lebanon analyst with International Crisis Group, told Al Jazeera. “Washington has also targeted Hezbollah’s efforts to raise money outside of traditional financial systems – such as receiving physical cash – by insisting that the Lebanese state exert more control over the country’s airport, seaports and border with neighbouring Syria.”

But Wood argued that sanctions against the group and individuals connected to it are only likely to have a limited effect.

“The threat of US sanctions might change the behaviour of some Lebanese elites, but that source of leverage largely disappears after imposing sanctions, because it is not straightforward to lift them,” Wood said. “Imposing US sanctions seeks to raise the cost of doing business with Hezbollah, especially for alleged associates of the party who enjoy lucrative sources of private income. This tactic is probably less effective in relation to direct affiliates of Hezbollah, which are more likely to operate outside traditional financial networks already.”

A political tool

Analysts also argue that the US’s use of sanctions is politically driven, showing that it is not a neutral or balanced actor when it comes to brokering deals between Beirut and Tel Aviv.

“The US is not a fair or equal decision-maker because it is a strategic partner of Israel and that’s the motivation behind sanctions,” Karim Safieddine, a Beirut-based nonresident fellow at the Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy, told Al Jazeera. “Sanctions by, say, the UN or independent bodies or courts that actually assess Hezbollah’s criminal culpability are one thing. But partisan sanctions that are part of warfare obviously only induce further [divisions] in Lebanon and have had lots of repercussions on people who are not Hezbollah.”

The US pressure campaign is still having an adverse effect on Lebanese people who do not support, or in some cases, actively oppose Hezbollah, due to the affiliation of the Shia community with the group – a connection the group itself also stresses at times.

“There are real repercussions on normal Lebanese people, especially Shia, because of supposed affiliations within a party that is very embedded in a community,” Safieddine said. “And it’s very hard to disembed it, as opposed to the genocidal tactics used by Israel. But the issue with sanctions is that they’re not actually based on criteria of human rights respectability.”
