World.title: Killing of NDC Supporters: Oborevwori visits scene, orders arrest of perpetrators
World.content:
Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State, on Tuesday, ordered the arrest of those behind the killings at a campaign rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) at Uduere Community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of the state.

Mr Oborevwori issued the order when he visited the scene where six people were killed, while many others sustained injuries during the attack on Monday.

He urged all political actors to shun violence, maintain peace, and avoid actions that could escalate tensions.

He said he was in the community to assess the situation and reassure residents of their safety and the return of normalcy.

The governor described the incident as “totally unacceptable and a grave threat to the peace and security of the state”.

He expressed deep sadness over the outbreak of violence during the rally and directed the security agencies to pursue the perpetrators and ensure they were brought to justice.

He was accompanied on the visit by the Commissioner of Police in Delta, Samuel Erale; Commander, 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Ibrahim Buhari, a brigadier-general; State Director of the State Security Service; and other top security officials.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘I am not a violent person’

Addressing reporters later, Mr Oborevwori said it was unfortunate that political differences could degenerate into violence and the loss of human lives, particularly when the state had worked hard to sustain a peaceful atmosphere since 2023.

He said it was “unconscionable for anyone to invade a community under the guise of political activity and resort to killing fellow Nigerians.

“Those who know me know that I am not a violent person.

“That is why, in my M.O.R.E Agenda, the fourth pillar is dedicated to enhancing peace and security.

“We have been preaching peace, and Delta has enjoyed relative peace since 2023.

“The important thing is how to sustain that peace. I want to assure the people that this will not happen again,” the governor said.

He condemned the killing, arguing that political ambition or disagreement could never justify the destruction of lives and property.

“The perpetrators must be identified, arrested and made to face the full consequences of their actions,” he said.

According to him, the state cannot afford to allow political activities to become a breeding ground for violence and insecurity.

“This must stop. It must stop. We cannot continue like this,” Mr Oborevwori said.

The governor said peace and security remained indispensable to economic growth, adding that no meaningful business activity or investment could thrive in an atmosphere of violence and uncertainty.

He urged security agencies, particularly the police, to conduct a thorough investigation, arrest all those involved and ensure that justice was served.

Mr Oborevwori said his administration remained resolute in its commitment to protecting lives and property, sustaining the prevailing peace and strengthening security across the state.

(NAN)

World.title: Olam Agri rewards loyal dealers at Customer Awards & Recognition Night
World.content:
Olam Agri’s wheat milling and pasta business, Crown Flour Mill (CFM) Limited, honoured its top customers, dealers and distributors at its Customer Awards & Recognition Night, marking more than 15 years of partnership.

The best-performing dealers displaying their awards. With them are CFM top executives.

Held under the theme “Celebrating Partnerships, Rewarding Excellence,” the event brought together company leadership and long-standing partners from Northern, Eastern and Western Nigeria. It paid tribute to the distributors who built markets and the dealers who stayed committed through shifting economic conditions. Their enterprise and confidence have carried CFM’s products to customers and communities across the country.

The highlight of the evening was the rewarding of CFM’s best-performing dealers across three categories: Trailblazer, Sterling and Titan. Winners received 5-tonne, 10-tonne and 15-tonne trucks and baking ovens. The night closed with the presentation of a 45-tonne truck to the overall best-performing dealer.

Nitin Mehta, Business Head, Wheat Milling & Pasta Business, Olam Agri, said the milestone reflects far more than time.

“Fifteen years of growing together represents relationships built on trust, shared ambition and resilience. Our dealers and distributors have helped us extend our market reach, serve customers better and strengthen our position in the industry. Through changing market dynamics and different challenges, the strength of our partnerships has been a constant source of resilience.”

Bolaji Anifowose, Vice President & Commercial, Olam Agri, described dealers as strategic partners rather than an extension of the distribution network.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Their market knowledge, entrepreneurial drive and commitment connect our brands to consumers across the country. Our focus now is on strengthening these partnerships, improving market reach, enhancing distribution efficiency and creating more opportunities for our partners to grow. A stronger dealer network means a stronger business.”

The overall best-performing dealer, Mr Oluwaseun Sose, called the award a proud moment.

“My relationship with the company has been built on trust, consistency and a shared commitment to growth. It has been a journey of learning, overcoming challenges and identifying opportunities together. This recognition encourages me to keep striving for excellence.”

The runner-up, Mrs Opeyemi Sanusi Modinat, praised the company’s collaborative approach.

“Our partnership has given us opportunities to grow, expand our market presence and serve more customers. What makes it special is the understanding that our success matters too.”

Anil Nair, Managing Director and Country Head, Olam Agri Nigeria, said the evening reflected the company’s enduring commitment to its partners.

“Our dealers and distributors are an integral part of our business, our growth and our connection with consumers. Their resilience and belief in our business have helped us navigate different market realities and seize opportunities together. Our success is strongest when our partners succeed.”

Olam Agri will continue to deepen its relationships with customers and distribution partners, strengthen its market presence and create new opportunities for shared growth. It will do so through improved partner engagement, business development support and initiatives that boost dealers’ competitiveness.

World.title: 2027: Omo-Agege speaks on court judgement nullifying his NDC senatorial ticket
World.content:
Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has rejected a Federal High Court judgement nullifying his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections, saying he will immediately appeal the decision.

Mr Omo-Agege said the judgement, delivered on Tuesday in Warri, Delta State, contained findings he considered inconsistent with the documentary evidence presented before the court.

The court nullified Mr Omo-Agege’s nomination in a suit filed by Alexander Akpodiete, who challenged the legality of the party’s nomination process.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Mr Omo-Agege said he had directed his lawyers to challenge the ruling at the Court of Appeal, insisting that the trial court failed to properly evaluate evidence relating to his membership of the NDC.

Mr Areh said the dispute centred partly on the court’s finding that Mr Omo-Agege’s name was missing from the membership register the NDC submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) at least 21 days before its primary.

He, however, maintained that both the NDC and INEC presented documents showing that the former deputy Senate president’s name was on the register.

According to the statement, the party submitted only one membership register and INEC acknowledged receipt of the document and subsequently issued certified true copies containing Mr Omo-Agege’s name to several individuals.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The statement questioned how the court arrived at a contrary finding despite the documents allegedly presented during the proceedings.

“We believe that some of the findings do not reflect the documentary evidence presented before the court,” Mr Areh said.

The former senator also intends to challenge the court ruling on the plaintiff’s legal standing to institute the suit.

Mr Areh argued that Mr Akpodiete did not obtain nomination forms to participate in the NDC primary, was not cleared by the party to contest and was not listed among the participants in INEC’s monitoring report on the exercise.

He further questioned why the plaintiff sought to invalidate the party’s nomination without asking the court to declare him the winner or award him the senatorial ticket.

These arguments, he said, raised questions about whether Mr Akpodiete had demonstrated sufficient legal interest to challenge the outcome of the primary.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that in its judgement, Justice Hyeladzira Nganjiwa held that the NDC failed to comply with the Electoral Act’s requirement to submit its membership register to INEC at least 21 days before conducting its primary.

The court said Mr Omo-Agege’s name was absent from the register submitted within the stipulated period and that the party failed to provide credible evidence that the register was subsequently updated and submitted as required by law.

Appeal

Mr Areh said Mr Omo-Agege remained committed to pursuing the case through the judicial system, dismissing suggestions that the judgement marked the end of his political ambition.

“Those already celebrating this decision as the end of Senator Omo-Agege’s political journey should exercise patience,” he said.

He added that the former lawmaker would not abandon the democratic process because of a judgement he considered erroneous.

The appeal could prove crucial to Mr Omo-Agege’s ambition to return to the Senate, particularly given the trial court’s pronouncement that the statutory window for conducting a fresh primary had closed.

World.title: NDC boycotts IGP’s security meeting over attacks on members
World.content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has boycotted a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu.

The opposition party accuses the police of failing to protect its members from escalating political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

It said it could no longer participate in security engagements with a police force it accused of allowing attacks on its members, including the killing of six people in Delta State.

The decision follows growing political tension after a deadly attack on supporters of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, during a political campaign event in Ughelli North Local Government Area on Monday.

Mr Omo-Agege is an NDC senatorial candidate in Delta.

In a tweet on Tuesday, the NDC said it would not lend legitimacy to what it described as a failed security process.

The statement was signed by the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, on Monday, 23 November.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

NDC accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of sponsoring thugs to attack opposition members and alleged that security operatives failed to intervene during violent incidents.

It cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Cross River, Enugu, and Delta states, alleging that its members and campaign activities were attacked.

The party also accused the police and other security agencies of failing to investigate the incidents and bring those responsible to justice.

“Presently, the Nigeria Police [have] become an APC Police sustained by taxpayers’ money,” the statement said.

NDC alleged that the killing of its members in Delta occurred in the presence of police officers and other security personnel who were deployed to protect the campaign. These allegations have not been independently established.

IGP summoned political parties

The boycott came as Mr Disu summoned chairpersons and secretaries of political parties to a meeting in Abuja on Tuesday to discuss rising political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The meeting was convened amid concerns over attacks on campaign rallies, destruction of political billboards and other campaign materials, and threats to public peace.

The NDC’s decision to stay away raises fresh questions about opposition parties’ confidence in state actors’ ability to keep them safe as political activities intensify.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the police command in Delta had deployed operatives to Uduere following Monday’s attack and ordered a full-scale investigation.

The state police spokesperson, Bright Edafe, said the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, had directed intensified security operations and assured residents that anyone found culpable would face the law, regardless of political affiliation.

The attack occurred during a campaign visit by Ovie Omo-Agege to the area.

His campaign organisation initially reported that four people, including two aides, were killed and four others critically injured.

Meanwhile, the Chairman of Ughelli North, Jaro Egbo, denied involvement in the violence and gave a different account of the incident, including a claim that three of his supporters were killed. The competing accounts had not been reconciled.

The Delta State Government imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area over the killing.

NDC seeks international intervention

Beyond the boycott, the NDC called on the international community to pressure President Bola Tinubu and the APC-led government to uphold democratic standards.

It also cited an incident in Benue State, alleging that people loyal to the APC government prevented its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering the state.

The party said it remained committed to peaceful and issue-based campaigns but would resist attempts to intimidate its members or exclude them from democratic participation.

“Democracy cannot survive where opposition members are hunted, attacked, and killed with impunity while state institutions look the other way,” the statement said.

World.title: 2027: Atiku promises lower fuel costs at Kogi rally without giving specifics
World.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar took his presidential campaign to Kogi State on Tuesday, promising to reduce fuel costs, support local businesses, and restore Nigerians’ purchasing power, according to a statement from his campaign.

The former vice president continues to campaign on the platform of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), despite a Federal High Court judgement invalidating his presidential nomination, which the party has appealed.

In the statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of pursuing policies that have made basic necessities increasingly difficult for Nigerians to afford.

The campaign said supporters at the rally chanted “Tinubu Must Go”, which Atiku described as an expression of frustration with prevailing economic conditions.

“A mother should not have to choose between feeding her children and paying their school fees. A trader should not open a shop each morning wondering whether anyone can afford to buy. A young person should not work hard all day and still struggle to pay for the journey home,” he said.

Video footage obtained by PREMIUM TIMES, presented as showing the rally, depicts a large gathering of supporters waving flags and surrounding campaign vehicles, with spectators also occupying the stands.

The Kogi State chapter of the ADC had earlier announced that it had secured Buhari Square in Lokoja, the state capital, for Tuesday’s rally.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Atiku’s affordability promises

The former vice president said his campaign, themed “Affordable Life”, would prioritise reducing fuel costs, supporting production and trade, and restoring the value of Nigerians’ earnings.

“When we say we will make life affordable again, we are speaking to the parent counting the last notes in a purse and the worker calculating whether a salary will last until month’s end,” he said.

However, Tuesday’s statement did not specify how much his proposed administration would reduce fuel costs or outline the policy measures, funding arrangements and timelines for delivering the promises.

Economic recovery and household hardship

The cost of living has become a major point of contention between the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general election.

President Tinubu has defended his administration’s removal of petrol subsidy and foreign exchange reforms as necessary measures to stabilise the economy and promote sustainable growth.

In an article published by the State House in October, the president cited economic growth of 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 and a decline in headline inflation from 20.98 per cent in September 2025 to 14.63 per cent in September 2026 as evidence of progress.

More recent figures from the National Bureau of Statistics showed that annual headline inflation fell further to 14.06 per cent in October, while annual food inflation stood at 19.13 per cent.

A decline in annual inflation means prices are rising more slowly than before, not necessarily that goods and services have become cheaper.

On Monday, PREMIUM TIMES reported that Taiwo Oyedele acknowledged that improvements in the country’s economic indicators had yet to translate into substantial relief for households and businesses.

No specific response to Atiku’s remarks at the Kogi rally had been publicly identified at the time of reporting.

Campaign continues amid legal dispute

Atiku’s visit to Kogi comes amid uncertainty over his eligibility to contest the presidential election following litigation over the ADC leadership.

On 5 November 2026, Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja invalidated the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC and decisions taken under it, including those affecting the nomination of Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate.

The Mark-led faction has challenged the judgment on 17 grounds and asked the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership and candidate records pending the determination of the appeal.

Although Atiku’s name remained on INEC’s published presidential candidate list after the judgment, no court order granting the requested stay of execution has been publicly established.

Under Section 17 of the Court of Appeal Act, filing an appeal does not, by itself, suspend the execution of a judgment.

Despite the legal uncertainty, Atiku has continued campaigning across the country.

In Tuesday’s statement, the former vice president thanked his supporters in Kogi and urged them to remain peaceful.

“Let no one mistake your restraint for acceptance of hardship. Let your voices be heard, and let your votes decide Nigeria’s future,” he said.

According to INEC’s official election calendar, the presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027.

World.title: Over 30,000 Nigerians access twice-yearly HIV prevention injection- Official
World.content:
More than 30,000 people at high risk of HIV infection in Nigeria have accessed Lenacapavir, a long-acting injectable drug administered twice a year to prevent HIV infection.

The National Coordinator of Nigeria’s AIDS, Viral Hepatitis and Sexually Transmitted Infections Control Programme (NASCP), Adebobola Bashorun, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja during a press briefing ahead of the 2026 World AIDS Day commemoration.

Mr Bashorun said Nigeria had received nearly 50,000 doses of the injectable medicine, with more than 30,000 eligible people already accessing it under the ongoing pilot programme.

He said the country expected an additional 170,000 doses by January 2027 to expand access to more people at substantial risk of acquiring HIV.

“We have over 30,000 that are currently on it. Don’t forget that the available injectable doses in Nigeria are not as much as in millions, but rather in the piloting phase of implementation,” he said.

Lenacapavir, also known as LEN PrEP, was officially rolled out in Nigeria in March 2026 and is currently being piloted in nine states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The participating states are Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Benue, Cross River, Ebonyi, Gombe, Kano, Kwara and Lagos.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Unlike daily oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), Lenacapavir is administered once every six months, offering another prevention option for people at increased risk of HIV infection.

Mr Bashorun explained that the medicine was specifically intended for eligible high-risk populations rather than the general public.

He said other prevention options available in Nigeria include oral PrEP and injectable Cabotegravir, allowing individuals to choose suitable methods based on their needs.

“There are other options too. You can decide to use oral, you can decide to use Lenacapavir, you can decide to use Cabotegravir. That’s why this theme is access. There are many innovations. Get one that fits you most and access it,” he said.

Nigeria records progress in HIV treatment

Also speaking, the Director-General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA), Temitope Ilori, disclosed that 80 per cent of Nigerians living with HIV knew their status in 2025.

Ms Ilori said 98 per cent of those who knew their HIV status were receiving antiretroviral treatment, while 94 per cent of people receiving treatment had achieved viral suppression.

The figures show that Nigeria has exceeded the second component of the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) 95-95-95 targets but remains below the first and third targets.

The targets seek to ensure that 95 per cent of people living with HIV know their status, 95 per cent of those diagnosed receive treatment, and 95 per cent of those receiving treatment achieve viral suppression.

Ms Ilori said the gaps in diagnosis remained a concern despite improvements in treatment coverage.

“However, the gaps in diagnosis and treatment remind us that more work is required to ensure that everyone knows their status and has uninterrupted access to lifesaving treatment,” she said.

She also disclosed that early infant diagnosis coverage among HIV-exposed infants increased from 15 per cent in 2022 to 66 per cent in 2025.

The NACA boss said the government would continue expanding HIV testing, prevention and treatment services, particularly for underserved populations.

Nigeria to unveil HIV financing strategy

Ms Ilori also announced that Nigeria would unveil its National HIV Domestic Resource Mobilisation and Sustainability Strategy 2026–2030 on 1 December as part of activities marking World AIDS Day.

She said the strategy was developed to strengthen domestic financing, increase national ownership and ensure continuity of HIV services amid changes in international donor funding.

“As the global health financing landscape continues to evolve, Nigeria cannot afford an HIV response that depends solely on external support,” she said.

According to her, sustainable HIV financing requires stronger commitments from state governments, increased domestic resource mobilisation and the integration of HIV services into existing primary healthcare systems.

She said NACA had also developed a National HIV Prevention Plan and advanced work on the National Strategic Plan to strengthen coordination of the country’s HIV response.

The agency is also implementing the 2026 Integrated Biological and Behavioural Surveillance Survey to improve understanding of HIV prevalence, risk behaviours and access to services among key populations.

Ms Ilori said this year’s World AIDS Day theme, “Ending AIDS Starts with Access: Equity, Ownership and Sustainability,” highlights the need to make HIV services available to everyone, irrespective of their location, income or social circumstances.

Stakeholders call for equitable access

The Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN) called for stronger domestic investment, community participation and sustainable healthcare systems to improve HIV prevention and treatment.

In a goodwill message, the Chief Executive Officer, Patrick Dakum, said access to HIV services must be equitable and inclusive.

Mr Dakum, represented by the Director of Prevention, Care and Treatment, Helen Omuh, urged the government and stakeholders to strengthen local capacity, address stigma and discrimination, and support communities in delivering HIV services.

Similarly, Amber Erinmwinhe, the Executive Secretary of the Nigerian Network of Religious Leaders Living with or Personally Affected by HIV/AIDS (NINERELA+) called for greater involvement of religious institutions in addressing HIV-related stigma.

Ms Erinmwinhe said equitable access must include dignity, confidentiality and freedom from discrimination.

She urged faith-based institutions and community organisations to participate actively in HIV prevention, treatment advocacy and programme monitoring.

She also called for increased domestic funding to sustain community-led HIV services as international donor support changes.

World AIDS Day 2026

World AIDS Day is commemorated annually on 1 December to raise awareness about HIV, remember people who have died from AIDS-related illnesses and promote prevention, treatment and care.

As part of this year’s activities, NACA said it would convene a National Prevention Conference under the theme “Reimagining HIV Prevention Strategies in Nigeria.”

Ms Ilori said the conference would examine existing prevention approaches, emerging technologies and strategies for expanding access to HIV services.

She urged Nigerians to know their HIV status and encouraged the media to promote accurate information while challenging stigma and discrimination.

World.title: 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP
World.content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it described as attempts to impose a political coalition on it, insisting that it was not interested in any alliance with the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any other party for the Abia North senatorial seat.

The state Publicity Secretary of the party, Emenike Iroegbu, stated this following the dismantling of a billboard bearing the portraits of Otti and Kalu in Arochukwu Local Government Area.

Iroegbu said the billboard, titled ‘Coalition of Choice’, was intended to create the impression of a political alliance between the governor and the senator, insisting that no such arrangement existed.

The billboard was reportedly dismantled over concerns that it could mislead the public and for allegedly failing to comply with statutory outdoor advertising regulations.

The party condemned its erection, describing it as an attempt to misinform voters in Abia North.

Iroegbu said, “We have made it categorically clear that the Labour Party in Abia State is neither in talks nor in any form of political coalition with the APC or any other political party.

“The Labour Party in Abia State has no coalition with any party as regards Abia North Senatorial Seat, and it is wrong for individuals or groups to erect billboards misinforming our people about a coalition when there is none.

“We call on Senator Orji Uzor Kalu to stop trying to force a coalition on the Labour Party. Our party is not interested in any coalition for the Abia North senatorial seat.”

He further alleged that Kalu was seeking to associate himself politically with Governor Otti ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the Labour Party would not allow the public to be misled.

The party commended the Abia State Signages and Advertising Agency (ABSSAA) for removing the billboard, stressing that public communication materials must comply with relevant regulatory requirements.

Iroegbu also disclosed that the party had a substantive senatorial candidate for Abia North, Chief David Onuoha Bourdex.

He said the party would not allow what it described as misleading political narratives to confuse its supporters across Arochukwu, Bende, Isuikwuato, Ohafia and Umunneochi local government areas.

World.title: PSC appoints CP Usman Adamu Zamfara Police Commissioner
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of CP Usman Sheikh Adamu as the new Commissioner of Police for Zamfara State.

The deployment was approved following an interview session at the commission’s corporate headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, presided over by a board member, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC, rtd), on behalf of the Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd).

In a statement by the commission’s spokesperson, Torty Njoku, the PSC said the new commissioner was charged to demonstrate professionalism and neutrality in the discharge of his duties, particularly as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections.

According to the statement, Adamu was also tasked with addressing the security challenges confronting Zamfara State and prioritising public safety.

Before his new appointment, Adamu served as Area Commander, Jos Metro, Plateau State Command; Area Commander in Yobe State; Deputy Commissioner of Police, Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Plateau State; and Commissioner of Police, SERVICOM, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja.

An alumnus of the University of Maiduguri, where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Linguistics, Adamu joined the Nigeria Police Force on June 10, 1994, as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police.

The commission said the approval had been communicated to the Inspector-General of Police through a letter signed by its Secretary, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani.

World.title: Omo-Agege attack: Makinde campaign accuses APC of political violence
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of promoting political violence to intimidate opposition parties and Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the killing of six people in an attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State.

The organisation said the attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, exposed the dangers of allowing political violence to flourish ahead of the elections, warning that it could undermine peaceful electoral competition.

In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO condemned the November 23 incident, alleging that APC agents were responsible for the attack in Delta State.

It warned that the incident could be part of a broader attempt to deploy armed thugs against opposition parties and frustrate the conduct of peaceful elections.

The organisation said, “This APC’s resort to killing before the 2027 general elections raises apprehension of a bigger design to use armed thugs to unleash mayhem on innocent citizens apparently with the aim to frustrate the smooth conduct of the elections.”

It recalled President Bola Tinubu’s remark to his supporters ahead of the 2023 elections that political power was not served in a restaurant and urged them to ‘at all cost, fight for it, grab it, snatch it and run with it.’

The campaign organisation also cited an alleged threat by Edo State APC Chairman, Jarret Tenebe, to invoke the power of AK-47 against anyone who opposed the party’s plan to secure Tinubu’s re-election, accusing the ruling party of failing to condemn the statement.

It further alleged that opposition parties had suffered attacks in Sokoto, Kebbi, Edo, Lagos, Cross River, Kaduna and Kano states, describing the latest incident in Delta as part of a disturbing pattern.

The MDPCO accused the APC leadership of failing to take decisive action against members allegedly involved in political violence, warning that its silence could further embolden those responsible.

“This deafening silence and apparent reluctance to demand accountability deepen public apprehension and clears every doubt that the APC is not ready for a free fair, credible and peaceful democratic competition,” it said.

The organisation warned that Nigerians would not accept the use of violence or insecurity as instruments of electoral conquest, insisting that political parties must respect citizens’ freedom to choose their leaders.

It declared that the resort to violence would not alter what it described as Nigerians’ determination to vote the APC out of power.

“The resort to violence will not save the President from obvious defeat in January,” the organisation said.

It demanded an immediate end to what it described as attempts to suppress democratic participation, while urging Nigerians to support its principal, Engr. Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), whom it said would reset the country through a government committed to transparency, security and citizens’ welfare.

World.title: Kogi APC chieftain Kasco dumps party, joins PDP
World.content:
By John Alechenu, Abuja

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kogi Central has recorded a defection from the All Progressives Congress (APC) following the resignation of a prominent APC chieftain, Hon. Umar Kareem, popularly known as Kasco.

Kareem, from Odenk Upogoro Ward in Okene Local Government Area of Kogi State, announced his resignation from the ruling party in a letter addressed to the APC ward chairman.

In the letter, made public on Tuesday, he said his resignation took immediate effect.

He explained that the decision followed extensive consultations, careful consideration and an assessment of his political journey, personal convictions and future aspirations.

Kareem said he had remained loyal and committed to the APC over the years, contributing his time, resources and efforts to the growth and development of the party.

However, he said his decision to leave was informed by his belief that political participation should be based on mutual respect, fairness, recognition, inclusiveness and a genuine sense of belonging.

“I firmly believe that political participation should be anchored on mutual respect, fairness, recognition, inclusiveness and a genuine sense of belonging,” he said.

He expressed appreciation to the APC for the relationships he built and experiences gained during his membership, while wishing the party’s leadership well.

Kareem’s defection to the PDP comes amid political realignments in Kogi Central ahead of future electoral contests.

World.title: US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America
World.content:
The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday.

CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the 49th edition of the event at US venues from June 9 to July 9, 2028.

The Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled for July 14-30 but the first pre-Olympic group-stage men’s soccer matches begin on July 10, only hours after the Copa final.

The tournament will feature 16 teams, the 10 nations from South America plus six countries from North America that will qualify through the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup.

The event was also played in the United States in 2016, the Copa America Centenario, and 2024 ahead of the USA co-hosting the World Cup earlier this year.

“The CONMEBOL Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez said.

“In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.”

The host cities and other details will be announced later.

“We’re pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” said CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani.

“We look forward to working alongside CONMEBOL, the host venues, and other key parties to organize a first-class tournament.”

World.title: Nigeria records 46,909 online abuse cases in one year
World.content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — Nigeria accounted for 58 per cent of verified online gender-based violence cases recorded across Africa in the last 12 months, with 46,909 incidents documented in the country, according to data from the OGBV Evidence Tracker.

The figures were unveiled at a high-level consultative meeting on digital safety and online gender-based violence in schools, organised by the Centre for Redefining Alternative Civic Engagement for Africa (RACE Centre) under its Protect Secondary School Initiative in Abuja on Tuesday.

Data from the tracker, powered by the RACE Centre, showed that 46,909 approved incidents were recorded between November 23, 2025, and November 23, 2026.

The tracker monitors online abuse across Africa, with Nigeria recording the highest concentration of incidents with verified locations.

X, formerly Twitter, accounted for 89 per cent of the documented cases, while Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube were also monitored.

Harassment and general abuse topped the categories of violations, with 23,209 incidents, representing 56 per cent of the cases.

Body shaming accounted for 7,662 incidents, representing 18 per cent, while slut shaming recorded 7,332 cases, also representing 18 per cent.

Threats of violence accounted for 2,643 incidents, or six per cent.

Other forms of abuse recorded included doxxing and privacy violations with 1,940 cases, synthetic artificial intelligence image manipulation with 1,730, stalking with 1,590 and impersonation with 790 incidents.

The tracker had yet to publish a finalised report for November 2026 as the month was still ongoing, although its live dashboard indicated that the trend remained high.

Speaking at the meeting, the Executive Director of RACE Centre, Evelyn Ugbe, said the organisation worked with feminist online watchers to document reports of abuse and refer victims to relevant authorities for intervention.

“We have our feminist online watchers. When we get a report, we document and refer them to appropriate agencies such as NAPTIP, NSCDC and or the Police for immediate action,” she said.

Ugbe urged parents to take a keen interest in their children’s online activities and create an enabling environment for teenagers to confide in them about their experiences in cyberspace.

Stakeholders at the meeting said the figures highlighted the need for stronger accountability by digital platforms, improved digital safety education and faster responses to online abuse targeting women and girls.

The meeting was attended by representatives of the Federal Ministry of Education, the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), civil society organisations and the media.

World.title: CAF vows to enforce CAS ruling restoring Senegal’s AFCON title
World.content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling that restored Senegal’s 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title following its dispute with Morocco.

CAF made its position known in a statement on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, saying it respected the decision of the Lausanne based tribunal and would take the necessary steps to give effect to it.

“CAF respects the CAS Award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it,” the football governing body said.

The CAS ruling overturned the CAF Appeal Board’s decision of March 17, 2026, which stripped Senegal of the title and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory after ruling that the Teranga Lions had forfeited the final.

Instead, the tribunal reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board, which had upheld Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the final played in Rabat on January 18, 2026.

The dispute followed a controversial incident late in regulation time when Senegal’s players temporarily left the pitch after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty.

The Senegalese players returned after about 14 minutes, but Morocco captain Brahim Diaz failed to convert the spot kick. Senegal later secured victory through Pape Gueye’s goal in extra time.

Morocco subsequently challenged the result, arguing that Senegal had breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which address situations where a team abandons or refuses to continue a match.

However, CAS ruled that the provisions did not apply because the referee had not permanently abandoned the match. The tribunal also held that the referee acted within his authority when he allowed play to resume.

The decision was unanimous, according to CAS Secretary General Matthieu Reeb, who said the panel found no legal error in the referee’s handling of the incident.

The tribunal’s ruling does not affect separate disciplinary sanctions imposed by CAF on Senegal coach Pape Thiaw and players Iliman Ndiaye and Ismaila Sarr over incidents during the final.

Although CAF has promised to comply with the decision, it has not yet provided details of the administrative steps or a timeline for implementing the ruling.

CAS confirmed that the full grounds for its decision had been communicated to the parties on Tuesday. The award is expected to be made public in due course, unless the parties request that it remain confidential.

The ruling brings an end to the dispute over the final and restores Senegal’s second AFCON title, following its first triumph in 2021.

World.title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement.

“No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said.

The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC.

“In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said.

The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence.

It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria.

“The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said.

The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable.

World.title: Senegal Floor CAF, Morocco As CAS Overturns AFCON 2025 Decision
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Teranga Lions of Senegal have reclaimed the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title they won on the pitch but bizarrely awarded to Morocco in the boardroom.

Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the final but the trophy was taken away and given to hosts Morocco by CAF’s Appeals Board.

Dissatisfied with that decision, Senegal appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sports (CAS).

CAS ruled in favour of Senegal, overturning CAF Appeal Board’s decision and reinstated the original ruling of its Disciplinary Board.

CAS confirmed: “The result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).”

It ruled that the decision of the referee was final.

“After examining the arguments of the parties, the arbitral tribunal considered that the referee’s decision to restart the match or to stop it definitively falls within his sole discretion. By blowing the whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for restarting the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again and both expressed their will to resume,” the decision read in part.

Senegal won the final on the pitch, but were later stripped of the title following the controversial match abandonment incident.

Hosts Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory, but that decision has now been overturned, restoring Senegal as champions.

Unconfirmed sources said Tuesday that the Moroccans were mulling the option of appealing CAS ruling in the Supreme Court of Switzerland.

World.title: Nigeria Showcases National LPG Cylinder Safety Programme At COP31
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Nigeria officially presented its National Cylinder Recirculation Programme (NCRP) at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, introducing a national framework to improve liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) safety, digital traceability and clean cooking accountability.

NCRP was presented November 12 at the Nigerian Pavilion in the Blue Zone of the COP31 Antalya Expo Centre, following a national launch in Abuja, allowing the country to introduce the programme to international delegates, climate finance institutions, and private investors.

Led by the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), alongside the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), the National Council on Climate Change (NCCC), and industry stakeholders, the NCRP governs how LPG cylinders are registered, inspected, tracked and recirculated.

At the centre of the programme is the National Cylinder Registry, a digital platform assigning each registered cylinder a unique QR code.

The system allows stakeholders to track a cylinder’s entire lifecycle—from manufacture and ownership to inspection, refilling, requalification and retirement.

This digital record improves supply chain visibility and helps verify that cylinders meet safety standards before circulation.

Subject to independent verification and regulatory approvals, the registry’s usage and refill data can also help measure emissions reductions to unlock carbon market financing.

In a keynote address, Director-General of SON, Dr Ifeanyi Chukwunonso Okeke, said NCRP remains a critical intervention for Nigeria’s clean cooking, public health and economic goals.

Represented by the Special Technical Adviser, Mr Manji Pious Lawan, Okeke said: “The National Cylinder Recirculation Programme is far more than a cylinder management initiative. It is essential infrastructure for clean cooking, public safety and climate accountability.”

He stated that deployment will roll out in phases across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.

The event also featured a panel discussion moderated by NCRP Chief Implementation Officer, Dr Bekeme Olowola, themed ‘Scaling Clean Cooking in Africa: Unlocking Safety, Traceability, Climate Finance and Investment.’

Panellists included Oyo State Commissioner for Environment and Natural Resources, Mr Ademola Aderinto; Senior Special Adviser to the President on Climate, Technology and Operations, Mr Olamide Fagbuji; Oando PLC Executive Director, Mrs Ayotola Jagun; and Century1 Managing Director, Chidera Ezigbo.

Aderinto warned that unsafe cylinders carry steep health, environmental and financial costs for households.

“Expired and substandard LPG cylinders contribute to air pollution, with consequences for public health, productivity and life expectancy. Beyond this, leakages from faulty cylinders increase emissions and create an economic burden for consumers, who end up paying more for gas they are unable to use. Participation in the NCRP presents an opportunity to reduce pollution and emissions while improving safety and helping households get better value for their money,” he said.

As per Fagbuji, he highlighted how government policy and domestic gas supply are driving clean cooking expansion.

“Nigeria’s energy transition plan has raised its ambition to increase domestic gas supply and impact over two million homes annually. The policy environment has created an enabling space for the private sector to take the lead and ensure long-term sustainability. Ultimately, what this represents is improved access to safe, reliable and affordable LPG for all,” he said.

Mrs Jagun stressed that targeted incentives and affordable capital are required to scale adoption.

“Tax relief and other incentives need to come in. There should be incentives that make it possible for households to receive cylinders at no cost, as well as opportunities for retailers to access carbon credits. There is also a need for cheaper financing to encourage the construction of LPG plants, which are significantly more expensive to build than CNG plants,” she said.

Closing the session, Olowola noted that progress across Africa requires addressing all pillars together.

“Scaling clean cooking in Africa depends on four things moving together: safety, traceability, climate finance and investment. Today’s discussion showed that none of them work alone, and the NCRP is designed to connect them,” she said.

Beyond improving public safety, the NCRP is expected to spur local investment across cylinder manufacturing, inspection, logistics, and technology services, while offering a replicable model for clean cooking accountability across Africa.

World.title: Experts Advocate Land Reforms, Tax Relief to Tackle Housing Crisis
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Real estate professionals have urged the Nigerian government to deploy land allocations, tax incentives and infrastructure development to curb rising rents and construction costs.

The professionals, who spoke at the third edition of the CW Real Estate Academy in Lagos, recently, warned that market forces alone cannot resolve the country’s housing deficit without deliberate policy intervention.

Managing Director of West Norwood Realty, Alfred Osagie, noted that government must move beyond passive regulation and actively use land allocation, title processing, and subsidies to reshape the property market.

“Rent is only a symptom. Value is a symptom of the behavioural pattern in the market,” Osagie said, as he urged policymakers to anticipate market challenges rather than react to them.

To lower housing costs, Osagie proposed dedicating state land exclusively to social housing, offering targeted tax relief to developers, and enforcing strict residency rules so low-income earners, rather than property investors benefit from subsidised homes.

He also called on cement manufacturers to offer discounted supplies for affordable housing projects, and urged Lagos and Ogun States to improve rail and road links so workers can live outside Lagos and commute easily.

Estate surveyor, Akinropo Abraham, echoed the call for public-private collaboration, recommending fast-tracked land titles and mandatory social-housing quotas for private estates.

He also advised large employers to provide staff accommodation to ease pressure on the rental market.

Another speaker, Akin Opatola, identified insecure land titles, poor infrastructure, and weak household purchasing power as the sector’s primary hurdles.

He noted that untitled land restricts property financing, while delayed infrastructure leaves new residential areas unlivable.

Beyond policy reforms, participants flagged unprofessional conduct as a major driver of public distrust in the sector.

Academy administrator, Aramide Olopo, noted that many newcomers mistakenly assume listing properties online makes them qualified estate agents, adding that the forum was designed to bridge that knowledge gap across the property value chain.

To enforce standards, Osagie advocated mandatory ethics training and periodic assessments for members of bodies like the Lagos State Real Estate Regulatory Authority (LASRERA), modelled on the United Kingdom’s Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors.

The three-day event themed ‘The Modern Real Estate Playbook’ brought together professionals from construction, law, finance, and technology to examine market valuation, transaction security, artificial intelligence and business scalability.

World.title: Regina Omo-Agege Condemns Attack on Brother’s Campaign Team, Says ‘Politics Must Never Become a Death Sentence’
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

*Urges Tinubu to ensure protection of Ovie Omo-Agege, other Nigerians irrespective of political affiliations

*Calls on IGP, DSS to conduct thorough, transparent investigation

Pastor Regina Omo-Agege, former INEC director and sister of ex-Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has condemned the killing of four persons and the shooting of several others during an attack on her brother’s campaign team at a political gathering in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

In a press statement issued on Tuesday, Regina described the incident as barbaric, unacceptable and a grave assault on Nigeria’s democracy.

She expressed shock and outrage over the attack, which reportedly claimed the lives of four persons, including members of the campaign team, while several others sustained gunshot injuries.

“Politics must never become a death sentence, and political ambition must never be pursued at the expense of human life,” she declared.

Regina, who said she was speaking both as a concerned sister and a Nigerian familiar with the political system, noted that she had served in government and retired as Director of Political Party Monitoring and Liaison at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

She said her experience working with politicians and political parties across the country had exposed her to intense political competition and electoral disagreements, but described the recent development as particularly disturbing.

“Since when did carrying ammunition to campaign venues become part of our political culture? Why should anyone attend a political gathering with ammunition? What justification can there possibly be for opening fire on people simply because of their political choices or affiliations?” she queried.

According to her, the incident goes beyond political rivalry and represents criminality that must be confronted decisively.



The former INEC director also disclosed that her brother had previously expressed concerns about threats to his life following his departure from the All Progressives Congress (APC).

She said although she did not fully appreciate the seriousness of his concerns at the time, recent events had compelled her to speak out.

“My brother had previously expressed concerns to me about threats to his life since his departure from the All Progressives Congress (APC). At the time, I did not fully appreciate the seriousness of those concerns. The events of recent days have, however, made it impossible for me to remain silent,” she stated.

Regina stressed that Omo-Agege’s political choices should not make him a target of violence, intimidation or assassination.

She also appealed to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to intervene and ensure the protection of her brother and other Nigerians, irrespective of their political affiliations.

“I am not asking for political favour, but for the protection of human life. The government has a constitutional responsibility to safeguard lives, irrespective of political affiliation,” she said.

She further called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant security agencies to conduct a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation into the incident.

Regina insisted that everyone involved in carrying out, sponsoring, financing or facilitating the attack must be identified and brought to justice, regardless of their political connections or influence.

“The families of those killed deserve justice, and the injured deserve every necessary support,” she added.

She maintained that political campaigns should serve as platforms for exchanging ideas rather than grounds for violence and bloodshed.

“Delta State is not a war zone. Nigeria is not a battlefield. Campaigns should be platforms for ideas, not grounds for bloodshed,” she said.

While mourning those who lost their lives and praying for the recovery of the injured, Regina thanked God for sparing her brother’s life.

She made a strong call for an end to political violence, declaring: “Enough is enough. Our democracy must not be built on graves, and no Nigerian should have to pay with their life for participating in politics.”

World.title: AI-Powered Evnti Launches to Streamline Event Planning
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

An artificial intelligence-powered event-planning marketplace, Evnti, has launched to streamline event planning by connecting clients, planners and vendors on a single digital platform.

The platform is designed to bring service providers and prospective customers together to access services in event ecosystem and make bookings through the marketplace.

Eventi is an initiative of Oluwakemi Elizabeth Farinde, a Nigerian Cloud DevOps Engineer specialising in cybersecurity and identity security in the United States.

Farinde noted that by integrating players into one digital space, Evnti seeks to simplify the process of sourcing event services and facilitate connections between customers and service providers.

The platform also incorporates booking and payment functions, making the protection of users’ identities, financial transactions and personal information an important part of its operation.

Also developed by Farinde alongside Eventi, was OnePassPay_ a digital payment security platform designed to reduce the misuse of stolen payment card details.

OnePassPay generates one-time virtual cards for specific merchants, with each card configured to expire within 10 minutes. Users select the merchant they intend to pay and generate a virtual card restricted to that transaction, limiting the potential for compromised card details to be reused elsewhere.

The platform also maintains transaction logs to provide an audit trail of generated cards and payment activities, while its design avoids long-term storage of reusable payment credentials.

Its working prototype, developed with React, Node.js and a cloud database, runs on cloud infrastructure and is designed around the principles of the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) 4.0.

The platform’s development roadmap also includes machine-learning capabilities to identify unusual merchant selections, repeated card-generation requests and login patterns that could indicate account takeover.

Farinde’s development of the two platforms draws on her professional experience as a Cloud DevOps Engineer on the cybersecurity federated identity team at a major United States airline, where her work involves identity management and controlling access to digital systems and resources.

Her technical background also spans cloud architecture, infrastructure automation and data science. She holds a Master of Science degree in Applied Data Science from the University of Essex, United Kingdom.

According to Farinde, businesses need to move beyond relying solely on the detection of suspicious transactions and adopt preventive measures that limit the exposure and misuse of sensitive information.

She also identified cooperation with card issuers and payment networks, encryption, identity controls and effective management of sensitive credentials as important requirements for secure digital payment systems.

World.title: 2027 Polls: IGP Pledges Police Neutrality, Protection for Journalists
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Mr Olatunji Disu, on Tuesday said that the Nigerian Police Force would remain professional, neutral and accountable before, during and after the 2027 general election.

Disu gave the assurance while delivering a keynote address at the ongoing 2026 Media and Development Conference (MDC), organised by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), in Abuja.

The theme of the three-day conference is ‘Media, Technology and the Future of Democratic Societies.’

The IGP emphasised the importance of public trust and police-media collaboration in protecting electoral integrity.

He described the gathering as a family reunion between journalists and police officers, as both professions faced dangerous situations and shared similar challenges in the course of their duties.

He commended CJID and its partners for the investigations and research into foreign information manipulation, AI-generated disinformation, coordinated disinformation campaigns and emerging threats to media and electoral integrity.

He said such threats could distort political participation, erode public confidence and undermine democratic institutions.

He said that electoral integrity was a collective responsibility requiring the media, civil society, security agencies and citizens.

“Nigeria faces several interconnected threats ahead of the 2027 elections, including voter intimidation, suppression, attacks on electoral officials and facilities, misinformation and restrictions on freedom of expression,” he said.

Disu described the information environment as a new battlefield, warning that fake videos, manipulated audio recordings and false narratives on social media could trigger violence and undermine the electoral process.

According to him, public trust is fundamental to effective policing, hence the legitimacy of the police depends, not on uniforms, weapons or personnel strength, but on citizens’ confidence in the institution.

“When citizens trust the police, they give information. They come forward and do their own motions. They obey lawful instructions,” he said.

He, however, said that loss of public confidence could undermine police operations.

“They accept election results because they believe the process was protected fairly. When trust is lost, even the operational plan will fail,” he said.

The IGP assured Nigerians that the police would remain impartial during the elections, but warned that no officer would be allowed to serve as a political tool.

He said officers found supporting political parties, candidates or political leaders would face disciplinary action.

Addressing concerns about journalists’ arrests and prosecution, particularly over cybercrime allegations, he said that the police under his leadership would not be used to oppress individuals with opposing political views.

“Journalism is not a crime. Indeed, journalists are partners in progress and development.

“The media’s role is to hold government accountable,” he said.

He said that journalists in some African countries faced suppression, harassment and institutional censorship, adding that Nigeria enjoyed a relatively better level of press freedom compared with some neighbouring countries in the Sahel region.

The IGP called for improved relations between the police and journalists.

“The force is educating officers to appreciate positive media coverage and cooperate with journalists.

“The police will organise engagements and training sessions for officers and journalists in Abuja and other states ahead of the 2027 elections.

“This is in order to strengthen collaboration on election coverage, reporting and the protection of media practitioners,” he said.

He expressed optimism that the exchange of ideas among stakeholders would generate practical recommendations for strengthening Nigeria’s media ecosystem, public trust and democratic institutions. (NAN)

World.title: Nigeria Showcases National LPG Cylinder Safety Programme At COP31
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Nigeria officially presented its National Cylinder Recirculation Programme (NCRP) at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, introducing a national framework to improve liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) safety, digital traceability and clean cooking accountability.

NCRP was presented November 12 at the Nigerian Pavilion in the Blue Zone of the COP31 Antalya Expo Centre, following a national launch in Abuja, allowing the country to introduce the programme to international delegates, climate finance institutions, and private investors.

Led by the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), alongside the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), the National Council on Climate Change (NCCC), and industry stakeholders, the NCRP governs how LPG cylinders are registered, inspected, tracked and recirculated.

At the centre of the programme is the National Cylinder Registry, a digital platform assigning each registered cylinder a unique QR code.

The system allows stakeholders to track a cylinder’s entire lifecycle—from manufacture and ownership to inspection, refilling, requalification and retirement.

This digital record improves supply chain visibility and helps verify that cylinders meet safety standards before circulation.

Subject to independent verification and regulatory approvals, the registry’s usage and refill data can also help measure emissions reductions to unlock carbon market financing.

In a keynote address, Director-General of SON, Dr Ifeanyi Chukwunonso Okeke, said NCRP remains a critical intervention for Nigeria’s clean cooking, public health and economic goals.

Represented by the Special Technical Adviser, Mr Manji Pious Lawan, Okeke said: “The National Cylinder Recirculation Programme is far more than a cylinder management initiative. It is essential infrastructure for clean cooking, public safety and climate accountability.”

He stated that deployment will roll out in phases across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.

The event also featured a panel discussion moderated by NCRP Chief Implementation Officer, Dr Bekeme Olowola, themed ‘Scaling Clean Cooking in Africa: Unlocking Safety, Traceability, Climate Finance and Investment.’

Panellists included Oyo State Commissioner for Environment and Natural Resources, Mr Ademola Aderinto; Senior Special Adviser to the President on Climate, Technology and Operations, Mr Olamide Fagbuji; Oando PLC Executive Director, Mrs Ayotola Jagun; and Century1 Managing Director, Chidera Ezigbo.

Aderinto warned that unsafe cylinders carry steep health, environmental and financial costs for households.

“Expired and substandard LPG cylinders contribute to air pollution, with consequences for public health, productivity and life expectancy. Beyond this, leakages from faulty cylinders increase emissions and create an economic burden for consumers, who end up paying more for gas they are unable to use. Participation in the NCRP presents an opportunity to reduce pollution and emissions while improving safety and helping households get better value for their money,” he said.

As per Fagbuji, he highlighted how government policy and domestic gas supply are driving clean cooking expansion.

“Nigeria’s energy transition plan has raised its ambition to increase domestic gas supply and impact over two million homes annually. The policy environment has created an enabling space for the private sector to take the lead and ensure long-term sustainability. Ultimately, what this represents is improved access to safe, reliable and affordable LPG for all,” he said.

Mrs Jagun stressed that targeted incentives and affordable capital are required to scale adoption.

“Tax relief and other incentives need to come in. There should be incentives that make it possible for households to receive cylinders at no cost, as well as opportunities for retailers to access carbon credits. There is also a need for cheaper financing to encourage the construction of LPG plants, which are significantly more expensive to build than CNG plants,” she said.

Closing the session, Olowola noted that progress across Africa requires addressing all pillars together.

“Scaling clean cooking in Africa depends on four things moving together: safety, traceability, climate finance and investment. Today’s discussion showed that none of them work alone, and the NCRP is designed to connect them,” she said.

Beyond improving public safety, the NCRP is expected to spur local investment across cylinder manufacturing, inspection, logistics, and technology services, while offering a replicable model for clean cooking accountability across Africa.

World.title: Oyo Gov’s Aide Tasks Tech Developers to Deploy AI for Better Governance, Economic Inclusion
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 





Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

Technology developers, innovators and digital entrepreneurs have been challenged to harness the transformative power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to tackle governance challenges, promote economic inclusion and improve the quality of life of residents.

The Special Assistant on Communication to Oyo State Governor, Oladayo Ogunbowale, who made the call while delivering the keynote address at the 2026 edition of DevFest Ibadan, held in Ibadan, said the growing adoption of AI and digital innovation presented an opportunity for technology professionals to develop practical solutions that would make public services more accessible, strengthen accountability and expand economic opportunities across the state.

Ogunbowale while speaking on the theme ‘Building the Future: How AI and Digital Innovation Can Transform Governance and Society,’ described technology as a critical instrument for building a more responsive, transparent and inclusive system of governance, urging developers to move beyond the creation of commercial technological products and focus on solutions that directly address the challenges confronting individuals, communities and public institutions.

He said the Oyo State government was already laying the foundation for digital transformation, citing the state’s internally generated revenue of N103 billion in 2025, which he said exceeded the combined revenue of the two preceding administrations.

He attributed the achievement to the strategic deployment of science, data and technology in government operations, particularly in plugging financial loopholes, reducing fraud and improving revenue generation in critical sectors, including lands and housing.

According to him, the experience of the state demonstrates how technology can be deployed to improve public-sector efficiency, strengthen financial management and deliver tangible benefits to citizens, maintaining that the ultimate objective of technological advancement should be to make government services more accessible, ensure greater accountability in the management of public resources and create economic opportunities for a wider section of society.

The Lead Organizer, Google Developer Groups (GDG) Ibadan, Abidemi Tiamiyu, described DevFest as an annual, community-driven technology festival designed to equip participants with practical digital skills, expose them to emerging technologies and provide opportunities for mentorship, explaining that the programme offered hands-on workshops covering Google products, AI, coding and other technological tools that participants could deploy to improve their productivity and professional capabilities.

Tiamiyu, who is the Founder, Software Engineer Abit Technologies Hub Limited, disclosed that the organisers recorded more than 2,500 participants at the previous edition and were targeting over 3,000 attendees for the 2026 festival.

He expressed confidence that the projected turnout would surpass the previous year’s figure, adding that the event had continued to attract participants and speakers from different parts of Nigeria and beyond.

The Co-Lead, GDG Ibadan, Joshua Olajide, on his part, said one of the major objectives of DevFest was to transform participants from ordinary consumers of technology into independent product builders, explaining that advancements in AI were making it increasingly possible for individuals to develop websites, create graphics and build digital products without necessarily depending on external professionals for every task.

He said the development had created opportunities for individuals to turn their ideas into practical solutions, provided they were willing to learn and acquire the necessary skills.

The Developer Ecosystem Programme Manager, Google, Sodiq Akinjobi, while speaking with journalists on the sideline of the event, disclosed that developers, engineers, programme managers and product managers are currently building for Nigeria’s markets.

He said: “They are building their apps in Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, not just in English, so that they can cover everyone. So the information, the instruction and technology can reach everyone whether you are learned or not. And with user research, it is now getting easier to apply these technologies in your day to day activities.”
