According to his professional profile, he has spent more than 18 years designing, monitoring, and securing critical networks for Microsoft Corporation, Fortune 500 companies, and United States federal agencies, including the U.S. Department of Defense.

He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Cybersecurity and Information Assurance, a Master of Science degree in Information Technology and Security Management, and a Master of Arts degree in International Affairs Leadership. He is also completing a Master of Public Policy and Management, specializing in global digital and cybersecurity policy.

World.title: Liberia: ‘Move from Promises to Practice’ – Children’s Forum Speaker Urges Government
World.content:
Kakata, Margibi County—The Speaker of the Liberia National Children Representative Forum (LNCRF), Michael Wesseh, has called on the Liberian Government and development partners to place children at the center of national development, stressing the need for greater protection, meaningful participation, and investment in their future.

By Yawah Y. Jaivey

Wesseh made the call over the weekend during the celebration of World Children’s Day in Kakata City, Margibi County, under the global theme:, “My Day, My Rights, My Future,” and the national theme, “Every Child Matters: Our Rights, Our Voices, Our Future.”



The Speaker of the Liberia National Children Representative Forum, addressing scores of government officials, development partners, child protection advocates and children from across the country, emphasized that children should not be treated as an afterthought in Liberia’s national development agenda.

Wesseh, citing the preamble of the Children’s Law of Liberia, 2011, which recognizes children as the pillars and cornerstone of a greater Liberia, argued that government planning, budgeting, policymaking, and decision-making must prioritize children’s welfare and development.

He cautioned against using children as political tools or remembering them only during political campaigns and public ceremonies. “Children should not be used as political tools. We should not be remembered only during campaigns, ceremonies, or when our presence is needed to make an event successful,” Wesseh said.

He referenced Section 23 of the Children’s Law of Liberia, which provides a foundation for children’s participation and expression, urging authorities to ensure that the provision is respected and implemented in practice.



The LNCRF Speaker reflecting on discussions held during the World Children’s Day celebration, Wesseh said children demonstrated that they have ideas, solutions and a vision for a better Liberia.

He referenced an interactive session in which children were asked what they would do if given the opportunity to become President of Liberia for one day.

According to him, some children proposed strengthening healthcare services and improving the quality of education, while others called for stronger measures to protect children from violence in schools and communities.

Wesseh, however, advocated for the establishment of safe spaces across the country where children could freely express themselves, feel protected and participate in decisions affecting their lives.

He maintained that children are not short of ideas but need leaders and institutions willing to listen to their concerns and act on their recommendations.

The LNCRF Speaker also called for collective efforts to end violence against children, emphasizing that the responsibility should not rest solely with one institution or individual.

He urged the Government of Liberia, parents, schools, communities, civil society organizations and development partners to work together to protect children from violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect.

“Every child deserves to feel safe at home, in school, in the community and everywhere they go. We must move beyond speeches and act now,” he stressed.

He also called on the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection to ensure that workshops, training programs and policies translate into practical child-protection interventions and measurable improvements in children’s lives.

Wesseh clarified that the forum’s concerns were not intended to condemn the government but to highlight the realities children face and encourage collective responsibility in addressing them.

Wesseh further stressed that children should be recognized as partners in shaping Liberia’s future rather than merely beneficiaries of development programs.

He noted that children’s participation should extend beyond radio appearances, public ceremonies and other social engagements to include policy development, budget preparation and national decision-making processes.

“Our voices should not only be heard when you need us to appear on radio programs, attend ceremonies, or participate in public events. Our voices must be heard in the rooms where policies are developed, budgets are prepared and decisions are made,” he said.

He further called for the decentralization of children’s representation to ensure that those in all 15 counties have meaningful opportunities to participate in decisions affecting their welfare.

Wesseh appealed to the Ministry of Gender, the Government of Liberia, UNICEF, SOS Children’s Villages, the United Nations, and other development partners to strengthen children’s representation at county, district and community levels.

The children’s representative also urged government ministries, agencies, and development partners to follow through on commitments made during the celebration. He called for the documentation of children’s concerns and recommendations, identification of responsible institutions and establishment of clear mechanisms to monitor implementation.

According to him, commitments made to children must translate into tangible actions and improvements in their lives. He continued, “Children must be able to look back and see that the concerns they raised today resulted in meaningful changes. We must move from promises to practice, from paper to protection and from consultation to genuine inclusion.”

Meanwhile, Wesseh expressed appreciation to the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning for an announced allocation of US$50,000 to the Liberia National Children’s Representative Forum.

He described the support as an important contribution toward strengthening the institution’s work and advancing children’s representation and participation in national development. At the same time, Wesseh challenged national leaders to consider the future of children in their present-day decisions, particularly in education, healthcare, protection and resource allocation.

He noted that children who aspire to protect others from violence, improve healthcare and strengthen education could become future national leaders, including presidents and cabinet ministers.

However, he questioned whether enough was being done to prepare them for those responsibilities through quality education, protection, investment and opportunities for participation.

“The future of Liberia cannot be secured by excluding the very people who will inherit it,” he declared.

The LNCRF speaker reaffirmed the forum’s commitment to ensuring that every child, regardless of background, location, disability, or circumstances, has the opportunity to be heard, protected, educated, and empowered.

He, however, used the occasion to urge government officials and development partners to remember children in national planning, budgeting and decision-making.

“When you are planning, remember the children. When you are budgeting, remember the children. When you are making decisions, include the children. And when you are building Liberia, put the children at the center,” Wesseh said.

For her part, Gbeme Horace Kollie, Minister of Gender, Children and Social Protection, reminded the hundreds of children attending the celebration that the future ahead of them is not just about their individual aspirations but also about the future of Liberia.

Minister Kollie assured the leadership of the Liberia National Children’s Representative Forum (LNCRF) and children across the country of the government’s strong commitment to implementing the Liberia’s children’s laws.

She noted that, as part of its commitment to upholding children’s rights, the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has supported the observance of national and international days dedicated to celebrating children and providing them with platforms to speak out on issues affecting their welfare.

The Gender Minister, however, cautioned members of the LNCRF against making themselves politically attractive, as she alleged some of their predecessors had done. Instead, she encouraged them to focus on advocating for their rights and ensuring that government officials fulfill their obligations to children.

“Don’t make yourself politically attractive; make yourself attractive to be able to meet your needs so your leaders can be challenged to know that they have obligations to you,” Minister Kollie said.

Continuing, she referenced President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s commitment to prioritizing future generations over electoral considerations.

“As President Boakai would always say, he is not concerned about the next elections, but concerned about the next generation, and that next generation is you!,” she stated.

She also urged the children’s representatives to remain polite and respectful in advocating for their rights and welfare, emphasizing that their advocacy should not be driven by self-centered interests but by the broader interests of the children they represent.

Meanwhile, Minister Kollie disclosed that, following consultations with the leadership of the Liberia National Children’s Representative Forum, the government is expected to purchase a bus for the organization to facilitate its activities.

She further revealed that the Ministry has allocated educational support funds to cover the schooling expenses of members of the forum’s leadership who have relocated from their respective counties to Monrovia.

In addition, the Gender Minister announced that funds have been allocated to the Children’s Forum to support community outreach activities aimed at raising awareness about violence against children in Liberia.

Also speaking at the occasion, Shairose Mawji, UNICEF Representative (Country Manager) to Liberia, reaffirmed UNICEF’s commitment to supporting the Liberian Government in ensuring that the rights of children across the country are protected and fulfilled.

Mawji disclosed that UNICEF has established several platforms to engage children and solicit their views, enabling the organization and its partners to better plan and implement programs that address their needs and promote their welfare.

She, however, encouraged the hundreds of children attending the celebration to speak out on issues affecting them, while ensuring that their advocacy is conducted respectfully.

World.title: Chilanga authorities commence ECF vaccination campaign
World.content:
The Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock has commenced the vaccination campaign of cattle against East Coast Fever (ECF) in all the 12 wards of Chilanga district.

District Fisheries and Livestock Services Coordinator Alex Mupango has explained that the government has released one thousand doses of vaccine for the exercise, to be conducted for a period of ten days in all the wards.

Dr Mupango was speaking after monitoring the vaccination exercise in Chilongolo ward, where he explained that the exercise is targeting cattle aged between three months to two years.

He thanked the government through the Enhanced Smallholder Livestock Investment Programme (E-slip) for releasing the doses on time, to avoid an outbreak of the disease in the district.

And Chilanga District Assistant Veterinary Officer Twambo Munsanje explained that the disease can be quite severe on cattle once infected.

Mr Munsanje stated that ECF is among the most expensive diseases to treat as the drugs needed are very expensive and can cost as high as K1000 per bottle for parvexon, among other drugs, meant to treat the disease.

He said the government is conducting the vaccination campaign against East Coast Fever for only K55 per animal vaccinated and noted that the vaccination is done only once in the lifetime of the cattle.

Meanwhile, Buffalo Hill Investment Farm Manager Maureen Mulenga encouraged other farmers to take advantage of the vaccination campaign exercise going on to safeguard their animals.

Ms Mulenga thanked the government for the exercise being conducted in the area.

East Coast Fever (ECF) is a severe, often tick borne disease, which attacks cattle and is caused by the protozoan parasite theileria parva.

World.title: Mulyata hands over to Mwaliteta
World.content:
Immediate past Lusaka Province Minister Sheal Mulyata has advised her successor Obvious Mwaliteta to embrace teamwork as he takes up the helm at the provincial office.

Ms Mulyata who is now Minister of Community Development and Social Services says teamwork is required to achieve the Grow Zambia Agenda.

She was speaking during a ceremony to symbolise the official handing over of the office to the new Lusaka Province Minister.

Ms Mulyata who congratulated her successor expressed confidence that Mr Mwaliteta will deliver in his new role.

She said the Lusaka Province Administration has various developmental tasks which need attention, noting that Mr Mwaliteta is equal to the task.

Meanwhile Mr Mwaliteta thanked Ms Mulyata for laying the foundation, saying he will pick up from where she left.

The Lusaka Province Minister commended Ms Mulyata for her contributions to the office.

And Mr Mwaliteta reiterated that he will be guided by the Eighth National Development Plan and the Grow Zambia Agenda as he serves his role.

World.title: Prudent utilisation of public resources encouraged
World.content:
Northern Province Acting Permanent Secretary Beauty Undi-Phiri has called on Heads of Government Departments to ensure prudent utilisation of public resources.

Ms, Undi-Phiri says government resources should not be spent on unnecessary trips but that priority should be on investments that improve service delivery to the people.

The Acting Northern Province Permanent Secretary has reminded heads of government departments that government resources should not be spent on monitoring activities involving officers who have no direct role in the assignments, but should instead be channelled towards strengthening institutional capacity and improving operations.

She was speaking during a Provincial Heads of Government Departments management meeting in Kasama today.

The acting PS has urged departmental heads to consider investing in essential office equipment to enhance efficiency and ensure government offices remain operational even during power outages.

“It is unacceptable that on a trip for monitoring and officers whose work is not in line with monitoring can be included, invest in things that help you improve service delivery because they are the ones we serve,” she said.

Ms Undi-Phiri says the provincial administration will closely monitor expenditure and travel patterns among government officers to ensure accountability and that public funds are used for their intended purposes.

She has further called on Heads of Government Departments to embrace integrity and accountability, reminding them that government resources belong to the people and should be used to advance the country’s development agenda.

“Let us use government resources prudently, we should always uphold integrity, of knowing that the resources we use are for the people out there in communities,” she advised.

And Ms Undi-Phiri has also urged the department of gender in the province to broaden its focus to include the boy child, alongside efforts to protect girls from early marriage and other forms of abuse.

She said both boys and girls need guidance and support to become responsible citizens.

“All departments here are key in ensuring that the Grow Zambia Agenda is success, the Department of Gender, let us ensure we look at gender to include the boy child too, if we focus on women and girls alone we will be creating a gap, because we will have a population boys who are junkies,” she observed.

“Let us all move together, boys, and girls, women, and men, let each of our gender play their role and appreciate each other,” she added.

She says the development of the province requires collective responsibility and collaboration among government departments, traditional leaders and communities.

World.title: Solwezi Correctional facility undergoes expansion
World.content:
The Northwestern Provincial Administration has called for the expansion of the Solwezi Central Correctional facility to address congestion and deteriorating infrastructure.

Provincial Permanent Secretary Grandson Katambi says an assessment has already been conducted and plans to expand the existing infrastructure have been approved.

Colonel Katambi (Rtd) was speaking in Solwezi today when Zambia Correctional Service Commission Chairperson Evaristo Kalonga paid a courtesy call on him.

He has also urged the correctional facility to take advantage of the increased Constituency Development Funds (CDF) to mobilise resources for the expansion of the facility.

Col Katambi further calls for improved transport for correctional officers to enhance their mobility and enable them to effectively carry out their duties.

Meanwhile, Mr Kalonga says his entourage is in Northwestern Province for the implementation of the decentralisation programme.

He says the team will also facilitate the formulation of various committees to oversee the appointments, promotions, discipline, appeals and welfare of officers at provincial level.

Mr Kalonga says the team has taken note of the shortage of officers at the Solwezi Central Correctional and will consider the challenges affecting the facility.

He has also commended the correctional facility for positioning itself well to contribute to the Grow Zambia Agenda, particularly through agricultural activities.

World.title: Mundubile, Makebi plead not guilty
World.content:
-National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) leaders Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu have pleaded not guilty to two counts of seditious practices.

The two appeared before Lusaka Magistrate Webster Milumbe, where they denied the charges relating to social media posts allegedly published on August 14, 2026.

Mr Mundubile, 55 and Mr Zulu, 45, are alleged to have jointly engaged in seditious practices by publishing statements on Zulu’s facebook page intended to raise discontent and disaffection among the people of Zambia.

In the first count, the two are alleged to have published a statement indicating that Mr Mundubile would address the nation shortly.

The prosecution alleges that the publication was intended to cause discontent and disaffection among members of the public.

In the second count, the accused are alleged to have published a statement claiming that, based on information received from various polling stations and their tabulation, they had won the elections.

The statement further called for the immediate publication of election results in accordance with the law to fulfill the will of the Zambian people.

Both accused persons denied the allegations after the charges were read and explained to them, prompting the court to record pleas of not guilty.

Following the pleas, defence lawyers applied for bail pending trial under Section 123(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, Chapter 88 of the Laws of Zambia.

The defence argued that the offences were bailable and that the two accused persons had fixed abodes and were willing to meet any conditions the court might impose.

Defence Lawyer Norman Siwila submitted that detention before conviction should be an exception rather than the rule, adding that the accused were presumed innocent until proven guilty.

He further argued that both had stable social and economic ties and no history of absconding court proceedings.

The court adjourned the matter to December 1, 2026, at 09:00 hours for hearing of the bail application.

Trial is scheduled to commence from December 14 to 18, 2026.

The State was represented by Deputy Chief State Advocate Samuel Simwaka, alongside other prosecutors.

World.title: DPP Seeks to arrest bail ruling in Mundubile case
World.content:
The Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) has applied to arrest the ruling in the constitutional bail application by Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and others, a move that has delayed the much awaited decision.

Mr Phiri, appearing for the State, asked the court to arrest the ruling when the matter came up for delivery of the ruling in the Lusaka High Court.

Speaking to journalists outside court after the proceedings, a defense lawyer Chifumu Banda said the application was taken up urgently, but argued that most of the defence law firms had not been served with the documents.

He said if service was done at all, it was done after the defence had already been informed of the proceedings.

Arguments were heard for and against the application by the State and the court is now expected to deliver its decision tomorrow.

The defence expressed hope that there would be no further application by the State.

The lawyer also welcomed the release of some of the accused who were not committed to the High Court for trial, saying the defence was looking forward to more releases.

This is in a matter in which Brian Mundubile and 13 others have applied for constitutional bail after the State applied to halt the ruling.

World.title: Chadiza teacher caged for sexual harassment
World.content:
Police in Chadiza have apprehended a teacher at Naviruli Day Secondary School in connection with a case of alleged sexual harassment involving a pupil at the school.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba has confirmed the development to media.

Mr Mweemba says the case was earlier reported on November 20, 2026.

He said Gift Mwanza, 38, a teacher at the school, is alleged to have sexually harassed a 17 year old Grade 10 pupil at the school.

“The alleged incidents occurred between May 2026 and July 2026 at Naviruli Day Secondary School in Chadiza district,” Mr Mweemba said.

He said Mwanza, who was at large, was apprehended today, November 24, 2026, by the Chadiza Police.

Mr Mweemba said the suspect is in police custody, pending court appearance.

World.title: FAZ file complaint to CAF against Burundi goal
World.content:
The Football Association of Zambia (FAZ) has filed a protest with CAF against the match officiating in the Group I AFCON qualifier between Burundi and Zambia played on 13 November, 2026 in Bujumbura.

FAZ General Secretary Charles Chakatazya says the protest is directed at the decision to award Burundi a goal in the 78th minute, scored by Bonfils-Caleb Bimenyimana, who in FAZ’s assessment was in a clear offside position when the ball was played.

Chakatazya says FAZ filed the protest within the required 24-hour window and paid the mandatory fee for the complaint to be admissible by CAF.

“As FAZ, we have formally filed our complaint with CAF and followed all the steps in ensuring that our complaint is valid. We have attached video evidence of our claims and will now wait for the due process to be seen out,” he says.

“We had to take our time to come out in the open to ensure that we met all the due processes that this process demands.”

FAZ has also cited the refereeing quartet from Cape Verde comprising Fabrício Duarte Andrade Santos (referee), Hélio Correia Semedo (assistant referee), Djéry Gomes Lopes (assistant referee II) and Leónidas Lenine Barbosa da Graça (fourth official).

“FAZ’s protest concerns the failure by the assistant referee to signal the apparent offside infringement and the subsequent decision by the centre referee, Mr Fabrício Duarte Andrade Santos, to allow the goal to stand,” he says.

“In our considered view, this constitutes a serious error in the application of Law 11 of the IFAB Laws of the Game. The apparent offside position of the goal scorer was particularly evident, raising serious questions regarding the positioning, concentration and decision-making of the appointed match officials.”

Chakatazya says FAZ is confident justice will prevail given the wider implications on the eventual standings of the group.

Zambia’s hopes of qualifying for the 2027 AFCON suffered a setback following the 1-1 draw against Burundi away in Bujumbura on match-day four last week.

Coach George Lwandamina’s side have now collected five points from a possible 12, after two draws, one win and one defeat.

With two matches remaining, at home against Algeria and away to Togo between 22 and 30 March 2027, Zambia have complicated their chances of reaching the tournament.

Chipolopolo dropped from second to third place in Group I after Togo beat Algeria 3-0 later on Tuesday night.

Algeria top Group I with seven points, followed by Togo on six, Zambia on five and Burundi on three.

The top two teams in the group will qualify for the 2027 AFCON to be hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

World.title: Senegal/Morocco: Senegal Reclaims AFCON Crown After Winning Appeal
World.content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has reinstated Senegal as the official winner of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), following a review of an appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation. The CAS verdict sets aside a previous decision by the CAF Appeal Board to strip Senegal of the trophy after an appeal from the Royal Moroccan Football Federation.

In its initial appeal, Morocco argued that the Senegalese side forfeited the January 18, 2026 AFCON final by walking off the pitch in protest of a late penalty.

In response, the Senegalese federation argued that the referee's decision to resume the match in the 109th minute and allow it to conclude with a "sporting result" could not be overturned.

In its ruling, CAS stated: "After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume."

In the final on January 18 at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, Pape Gueye scored in extra time to give Senegal a 1-0 victory and their second Africa Cup of Nations title.

World.title: Africa: Malawi Agriculture Minister Champions Investment-Led Economic Transformation
World.content:
Roza Fatch Mbilizi calls for a shift from raw commodity exports to agro-industrial development, placing agriculture at the heart of Malawi’s economic transformation.

LILONGWE, Malawi, November 24, 2026 – Malawi’s Minister of Agriculture, Roza Fatch Mbilizi, has called for a fundamental transformation of the country’s agricultural sector, positioning it as a catalyst for industrialisation, export competitiveness and sustainable economic growth.

Presiding over the Malawi Investment Summit 2026 on Monday at the Bingu International Convention Centre in Lilongwe, Mbilizi outlined a vision that seeks to move Malawi beyond its traditional dependence on raw agricultural commodity exports towards a more diversified, productive and value-added economy.

The Minister emphasised the need to accelerate investment in agro-processing, irrigation, agricultural mechanisation and modern storage infrastructure to unlock the country’s productive potential, create employment opportunities and strengthen its position in regional and international markets.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Her leadership at the Summit underscored the central role of agriculture in advancing Malawi 2063, the country’s long-term development blueprint, and delivering on the economic transformation agenda of President Professor Arthur Peter Mutharika.

From dialogue to tangible investment

In a strong call for accountability and results, Mbilizi stressed that the success of the Summit should not be measured by the quality of discussions alone, but by the concrete investments, strategic partnerships and development projects that emerge from it.

Her message reflected a determination to translate policy ambitions into tangible economic outcomes, while positioning the agricultural sector as an attractive destination for domestic and international capital.

For Malawi, where agriculture remains a cornerstone of livelihoods and export earnings, greater investment in value addition presents an opportunity to increase farmers’ incomes, expand industrial capacity, generate foreign exchange and strengthen economic resilience.

Creating an enabling investment environment

The Summit, held under the theme “Transforming Malawi’s Investment Climate for Sustainable Industrial Growth and Export Competitiveness,” also highlighted ongoing government efforts to improve the business environment.

Minister of Industrialisation, Business, Trade and Tourism Simon Itaye reinforced the government’s commitment to attracting investment, acknowledging investor concerns over regulatory predictability, bureaucratic hurdles and the speed of administrative approvals.

He highlighted measures to strengthen the One Stop Service Centre at the Malawi Investment and Trade Centre (MITC) and operationalise the Special Economic Zones framework.

These initiatives complement broader legislative and policy reforms, including the Investment and Export Promotion Act 2024, the Special Economic Zones Act 2024 and the draft National Investment Policy.

According to a Financial Times briefing note prepared for the Summit, MITC projects foreign direct investment inflows of US$1.2 billion by the end of the current fiscal year, although infrastructure gaps and regulatory uncertainty remain challenges.

Agriculture as a gateway to regional and global markets

Malawi’s membership in the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) offers significant opportunities for agricultural producers and investors seeking access to larger markets.

Close 

By championing agro-industrial development, Mbilizi is placing agriculture at the intersection of food security, industrialisation, job creation and international trade.

Organised by the Financial Times and Philip Morris International, in collaboration with MITC and key government ministries, the Summit brought together policymakers, international investors, diplomatic missions, financial institutions, local producers, exporters and development partners.

The gathering provided a platform for Malawi to articulate its investment priorities and demonstrate its commitment to economic reform.

Under Mbilizi’s leadership, the agricultural sector is being positioned not simply as a source of raw commodities, but as a strategic engine of industrial development and long-term prosperity.

The challenge now will be to convert that vision into investments that deliver measurable benefits for farmers, businesses and the wider Malawian economy.

World.title: Mozambique: Mondlane Denies Being Responsible for Inciting Crowds to Destroy Public Infrastructure
World.content:
Maputo — Venâncio Mondlane, a former presidential candidate and leader of the National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique (Anamola), who's standing a trial for allegedly committing five crimes related to 2024 post-election mass demonstrations, denies being responsible for inciting crowds to destroy toll booths, telecommunications towers, or other public and private infrastructure.

Mondlane - who was being questioned on Monday by the lawyer Rodrigo Rocha, who acts as an assistant to the Attorney General's Office (PGR) on behalf of the controversial state-owned company Revimo (Mozambique Road Network) - claims that his calls for demonstrations intended to protest against the alleged fraudulent results of the general elections.

The politician explained that he only called for peaceful demonstrations, which means that he is not responsible for the destruction of public or private infrastructures.

Mondlane challenged Rocha to present video evidence showing him ordering or instigating the burning of public or private facilities, when he was questioned about the real intention behind his statements. He added that his statements were politically motivated and were not intended to encourage acts of destruction or vandalism.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

When questioned about the alleged destruction of 59 telecommunications towers, Mondlane responded that was unaware of such destruction, calling for presentation of evidence. He also said that his calls for demonstrations were peaceful, citing the singing of national anthem as an irrefutable fact of his actions.

Mondlane is standing trial for allegedly committing five crimes related to 2024 post-election mass demonstrations, namely: public apology for a crime; incitement to collective disobedience; public instigation to crime; instigation and incitement to terrorism. The mass demonstration he called to protest started peacefully but then degenerated into rioting.

Revimo is basically a state-owned company. 70 percent of its shares are held by the government's Road Fund, 15 per cent by the Bank of Mozambique Pension Fund, and 15 per cent by the National Social Security Institute (INSS).

Among the roads operated by Revimo are the Maputo Ring Road (71.4 kilometers long), the Maputo-KaTembe bridge, and the connecting roads to the border with the South African province of Kwazulu-Natal (187 kilometres), and the Beira-Zimbabwe highway (287 kilometres).

Rioting and destruction halted the collection of tolls in December 2024. Rioters who infiltrated the demonstrations utterly destroyed some of the tollgates.

World.title: Uganda: Uganda Denies Involvement in Aircraft Shot Down Eastern DR Congo
World.content:
Uganda's military has denied involvement in a fighter jet that was shot down by the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) near Minembwe in eastern DR Congo on Sunday, November 22.

The denial followed the circulation of a video showing one of the survivors being questioned by armed fighters about his nationality and the circumstances under which he entered DR Congo.

The shooting down of the plane was announced this week by Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson for the FRN. He said FRN fighters downed it at around 6am on Sunday, claiming it was preparing to attack civilian populations in the Minembwe area.

Reports from the crash site indicate that two occupants died while two others survived. In the footage, one of the survivors identifies himself as Ugandan and claims to be a junior military officer deployed to the country by his government.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Asked who sent him to DR Congo, he responded: "Uganda."

His identity, military status and claims of government involvement have not been independently verified.

In a social media post, Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, said the Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) had nothing to do with the aircraft.

ALSO READ: FRN forces shoot down fighter jet flying over Minembwe: spokesperson

"UPDF had nothing to do with the aircraft that was shot down in Minembwe. We have penalised that company," Kainerugaba said in a statement shared on X by Chris Magezi, Acting Director of Defence Public Information and Media Affairs.

He did not identify the company or explain the nature of the penalty.

ALSO READ: Former US special forces officer behind FARDC air strikes: investigation

In a separate post, Kainerugaba said he had ordered the arrest of several soldiers and officers linked to a company that had sought to employ them.

"Today, I ordered the arrest of several soldiers and officers. The company that sought to employ them is banned from operating in Uganda. We shall investigate it further," he said.

He also warned Ugandans against working for mercenary companies in DR Congo, threatening severe punishment for those involved.

World.title: Botswana: Belt Tightening Measures Continue - Gaolathe
World.content:
Vice President and Minister of Finance Ndaba Gaolathe addresses a Budget consultation kgotla meeting in Letlhakeng on Thursday. Mr Gaolathe said the current fiscal challenges, largely due to a decline in diamond revenue, could only be addressed through judicious fiscal management, adopting new approaches and intensifying economic diversification efforts. Photo: Mothusi Galekhutle

Letlhakeng — Fiscal prudence is essential while simultaneously accelerating efforts to diversify the economy in order to achieve financial sustainability.

Addressing a budget consultation kgotla meeting in Letlhakeng on Thursday, Vice President Ndaba Gaolathe, who also serves as Minister of Finance, explained that the current fiscal challenges, largely due to a decline in diamond revenue, a key contributor of Botswana's economy, could only be addressed through judicious fiscal management, adopting new approaches and intensifying economic diversification efforts.

Clarifying the financial situation, he said the country's total annual expenditure was approximately P100 billion, while total revenue generated annually stood at P80 billion.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

This gap forces government to borrow from institutions such as the Africa Development Bank, World Bank, and the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) fund for international development, he said.

Mr Gaolathe expressed confidence that Botswana was supported by men and women capable of restoring the economy to its former strength.

He pledged that under his leadership as minister of finance, he would do his utmost to ensure the country's stability, expressing optimism in the Botswana Economic Transformation Programme (BETP), which not only assisted business owners in securing funding but also equipped them with the necessary skills to manage their businesses, find potential partners, and access new and better markets.

The programme also promotes vocational education or training with government enhancing resources for vocational schools, encouraging them to collaborate with independent entities to help produce competitive graduates.

Mr Gaolathe assured residents that the government was working to ease business licensing bottlenecks, to attract more investors and create employment opportunities.

He also said infrastructure development would be carried out at reasonable costs, with feasibility studies conducted before any projects commenced, to avoid exploitation by contractors.

Mr Gaolathe noted that mineral processing would soon be done locally and government was looking for investment partners and that discussions with the government of Zambia regarding the initiative had commenced.

Contributing to the discussions, Kgosi Itsoseng Gaoonwe of Letlhakeng stated that shortage of transport at the Department of Tribal Administration was negatively impacting service delivery hence called for an increased budget to cater for the shortfall.

Letlhakeng Village Development Committee chairperson, Ms Kebafilwe Moselele, appealed to the government to consider building a fully equipped hospital in the region, to cater for health needs of the growing population.

Close 

She also urged government to consider construction of another junior school to reduce overcrowding at Mphuthe Junior Secondary School.

Ms Moselele also requested the Vice President to advocate for the construction of a brigade in Letlhakeng, adding that a plot was long reserved for the project.

Farmers' representative, Mr Falcon Sedimo, called for the fencing and subdivision of Zone 11, as well as the creation of buffer zones to protect livestock in cases of Foot and Mouth Disease and other livestock diseases.

Mr Sedimo also advocated for the promotion of fodder production.

World.title: South Africa: Joburg Mayoral Vote Delayed As Parties Battle Over Power
World.content:
The iconic Brixton Tower in Johannesburg lit up on Wednesday night with messaging calling for an end to exploitative debt in poor countries. World leaders will be gathering in the city this weekend for the G20 summit. The action was done by South African artists who teamed up with activists from the Glasgow Actions Team (GAT).

Johannesburg's 270 newly elected councillors were sworn in on Monday, but all 21 political parties agreed to postpone the election of a mayor.

Former Johannesburg council speaker Margaret Arnolds says she would support ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba's return as mayor if coalition partners agree.

Johannesburg has a new council but residents still do not know who will lead the city for the next five years.

The election of the mayor, council speaker and other council leaders has been postponed until Friday, 27 November, as political parties continue talks over sharing power.

All 270 newly elected councillors were sworn in at the Constance Connie Bapela Council Chamber in Braamfontein on Monday.



However, the election of council leaders did not go ahead after the Democratic Alliance (DA) requested a postponement.

City Manager Floyd Brink said he received a letter from DA leader Helen Zille asking for more time to allow parties to finish their coalition talks.

The party argued that going ahead with the elections could damage negotiations and efforts to form a stable government.

Brink consulted the other political parties before making a decision.

All 21 parties agreed to postpone the election until Friday.

Meanwhile, former council speaker Margaret Arnolds says she has no problem with ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba returning as Johannesburg mayor.

Her party, the African Independent Congress, secured one council seat in the 4 November local government elections.

Arnolds said political leaders must understand that sharing power means making compromises.

"Politics has no permanent friends and no permanent enemies. I believe that if you have the right people behind the mayor, the mayor can do wonders. And if Mashaba has to come in and that is our mayor, then let it be," she said.

Arnolds previously served under Mashaba when he was Johannesburg mayor.

She has been a councillor since 2016 and served on the mayoral committee under three late African National Congress mayors, Geoff Makhubo, Jolidee Matongo and Mpho Moerane.

She also served as council speaker under the outgoing coalition government.

Arnolds said she would respect whatever decision the coalition partners made about the city's leadership.

She called on residents, businesses and political parties to work together to make the new government succeed.

"It must be all of us. We as residents have a responsibility because we as residents have brought in a coalition government," she said.

Close 

Political parties now have until Friday to try to reach an agreement on who should run Johannesburg.

World.title: Kenya: Majority of Kenyans Fear Arrest, Violence If They Join Protests, Afrobarometer Survey Finds
World.content:
A Kenyan protestor holds up a banner against police brutality at demonstrations in Nairobi on June 25, 2025.

Nairobi — A majority of Kenyans fear intimidation, arrest or violence if they participate in public protests, with new Afrobarometer findings pointing to widespread concern over police conduct, government accountability and the protection of human rights.

The survey found that 57 per cent of respondents do not feel free to participate in demonstrations without fear of repression, while only 42 per cent said they felt somewhat or completely free to protest.

"A majority of Kenyans say they fear intimidation, arrest, or violence if they participate in public protests," Afrobarometer said in its news release accompanying the findings.

The findings highlight a sharp contrast between freedom of expression and the exercise of the right to assemble, with 65 per cent of Kenyans saying they are free to express their opinions.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The research also found that 62 per cent of respondents consider police use of force to maintain order during protests unjustified, against 37 per cent who consider such force justified.

More than half of respondents, 53 per cent, believe violence during demonstrations is mainly caused by people hired to cause trouble, commonly referred to as "goons". Another 29 per cent blamed the police, while 16 per cent pointed to protesters.

Views remain divided on whether demonstrations should be allowed even when they sometimes turn violent. While 51 per cent support citizens' right to protest under such circumstances, 45 per cent disagree.

The survey further raises questions about the government's responsiveness to public grievances, with only 37 per cent saying authorities take concerns raised through protests seriously.

The remaining 63 per cent believe the government gives such concerns little or no consideration, including 31 per cent who said it does not take them seriously at all.

The findings come against the backdrop of the 2024 Gen Z-led demonstrations against the Finance Bill, which appear to have influenced public attitudes towards protests. About 51 per cent of Kenyans said the demonstrations had changed their views on using protests to influence government decisions.

Human rights and accountability

Beyond protest participation, the survey found that 53 per cent of Kenyans believe the government is not committed to protecting human rights for all citizens, compared with 42 per cent who consider it committed.

There are also concerns over the conduct of security agencies, with 56 per cent saying police often or always use excessive force against suspects in custody.

On reported abductions, 66 per cent of respondents identified the police or other state security agencies as primarily responsible, while 26 per cent blamed criminal gangs.

An overwhelming 92 per cent said the government needs to do more to investigate and prevent abductions and extrajudicial killings. Of these, 68 per cent said it needs to do "a lot more", while 24 per cent called for somewhat more action.

Confidence in access to justice for victims and their families was also low. Only 34 per cent said they were confident that victims of extrajudicial killings and their families could obtain justice in court, against 65 per cent who expressed little or no confidence.

Concerns over the state of democracy

The survey found that 53 per cent of Kenyans had been concerned in the previous five years that democracy was under threat in the country.

Among those expressing concern, 40 per cent said they had spoken to others or shared their concerns on social media, while 29 per cent had attended meetings where the issues were discussed.

One in five said they had participated in demonstrations in support of democracy, while 19 per cent had contacted elected leaders and five per cent had reached out to the media.

The proportion of Kenyans who consider the country "a full democracy" or "a democracy with minor problems" stood at 54 per cent, down from a high of 68 per cent in 2019.

Satisfaction with the way democracy is working in Kenya has also declined, with 46 per cent saying they were fairly or very satisfied, compared with 59 per cent in 2019.

About the survey

The findings are drawn from Afrobarometer's Round 11 survey, a pan-African, nonpartisan research initiative that tracks public experiences and assessments of democracy, governance and quality of life.

Close 

In Kenya, the research was led by the Institute for Development Studies at the University of Nairobi, with researchers Paul Kamau and Karuti Kanyinga presenting the findings at the university on November 24, 2026.

The Kenyan team interviewed 2,400 adult citizens between September 1 and 20, 2026, using face-to-face interviews conducted in respondents' preferred languages.

The sample was nationally representative, comprising 50 per cent men and 50 per cent women, with 64.7 per cent of respondents drawn from rural areas and 35.3 per cent from urban areas.

Afrobarometer says the sample size produces country-level results with a margin of sampling error of plus or minus two percentage points at a 95 per cent confidence level. The margin of error is higher for demographic subgroups because of their smaller sample sizes.

Afrobarometer, a pan-African survey research network, launched its round 11 surveys in May 2026, building on previous rounds conducted in Kenya bewteen 2003 and 2024.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 24, 2026
World.content:
Amnesty Seeks War Crimes Probe Into Deadly Ethiopia Attacks

Amnesty International is calling for an investigation into possible war crimes following artillery attacks by Ethiopian government forces and their Tigray Peace Forces allies that killed at least 14 civilians in Alamata, northern Tigray, between 26 and 28 September. The organisation said the shelling struck densely populated neighbourhoods, including residential homes and commercial areas, and injured numerous others. Amnesty also found that Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) fighters had established military bases in residential areas and schools, putting civilians at risk. However, it stressed that this did not justify indiscriminate attacks and called for an independent international investigation and accountability for those responsible. The Ethiopian military and its allies had not responded to Amnesty's allegations at the time of publication, while the TPLF rejected the claims against its forces.

Sudan Famine Driven by War, Not Natural Disaster – Report

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Nearly 19.5 million people in Sudan are facing crisis levels of hunger or worse, with the risk of famine remaining high in several parts of the country, according to the World Food Programme and a report by the Somoud Alliance. The ongoing war, displacement, restrictions on humanitarian aid, destruction of farmland and markets, and rising food prices have worsened food insecurity, with around five million people facing emergency levels of hunger and 135,000 in catastrophic conditions. An estimated 825,000 children under five are also expected to suffer acute malnutrition in 2026. The alliance has called for an immediate ceasefire, safe humanitarian access and increased international funding to prevent further loss of life. It warned that funding shortages are leaving many households with only half their food rations, while attacks on aid workers and convoys continue to obstruct relief efforts.

DR Congo Fighting Traps Ebola Responders in Hospital

Heavy fighting near a hospital in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ituri province has forced Ebola responders and World Health Organization staff to shelter in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said teams were working to evacuate trapped staff safely and called for protection for healthcare workers, patients, and medical facilities. The violence has disrupted efforts to contain the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, with Ituri accounting for more than two-thirds of confirmed cases. The outbreak has recorded 11,762 confirmed cases and 5,775 deaths across eight provinces, according to figures released on 20 November. The WHO has also verified more than 87 attacks on healthcare facilities and workers in the DR Congo since the beginning of the year.

Borno School Enrolment Nearly Doubles After Years of Boko Haram Violence

Education is gradually recovering in Nigeria's northeastern Borno State after more than a decade of Boko Haram violence forced schools to close and displaced thousands of families. Government figures show enrolment in public and private schools increased to 1.4 million learners in 2025, up from about 766,000 during the 2017-2018 academic year. Authorities said that they have built 104 new schools and renovated nearly 3,000 classrooms. The number of out-of-school children has reportedly fallen from 2.2 million to fewer than 800,000. However, insecurity, poverty, teacher shortages and limited access to schools in rural communities continue to threaten efforts to restore education. Officials said that rebuilding confidence among parents and ensuring children receive adequate learning support remain key to sustaining the progress.

Zimbabwean Preacher Uebert Angel Arrested on Sexual Assault Allegations

Prominent Zimbabwean preacher Uebert Angel has been arrested in Harare on allegations of indecent assault and sodomy. The founder of Spirit Embassy was reportedly detained during a church service. The police are yet to provide details about the allegations or confirm when he will appear in court. Angel, who was appointed Zimbabwe's special presidential envoy and ambassador-at-large in 2021. He previously faced controversy following a 2023 Al Jazeera undercover investigation that alleged he offered to use his diplomatic status to facilitate money laundering through a gold-smuggling scheme. He has also previously faced allegations of sexual impropriety, which he denied. A member of his team confirmed that he remained in police custody. The timing of his court appearance was still unclear.

Close 

Final Verdict Due in Senegal-Morocco AFCON Title Dispute

The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) is set to deliver its ruling on Senegal's appeal against the decision to strip the country of its 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title and award it to Morocco. Senegal initially won the January final 1-0 after extra time, but the Confederation of African Football's appeals board overturned the result in March, ruling that Senegal had forfeited the match after players walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision. Morocco was subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory. Senegal's football federation challenged the decision, describing it as unfair, and is seeking to have the original result reinstated. The ruling could have wider implications for CAF's credibility and the application of tournament regulations. CAS's decision will be final, barring limited grounds for a further appeal before Switzerland's highest court, potentially bringing an end to the months-long dispute.

World.title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

World.title: Vanity Fair writer ignites firestorm fretting 'accountability journalism' failed to take down Jensen Huang
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A writer for Vanity Fair is getting intense blowback for lamenting that "accountability journalism" failed to take down scandal-plagued Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following his shocking reinstatement on Monday.

Nvidia made international headlines when it announced Huang would be returning as CEO just days after his resignation following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy, and questions whether his company's chips were being sent to China.

The announcement came one day after The New York Times published a bombshell report alleging that U.S. intelligence had been monitoring communications between Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy the Nvidia CEO had the alleged affair with, and a Chinese spy agency.

RUBIO DUCKS QUESTIONS ON NVIDIA CEO'S REINSTATEMENT AFTER REPORTEDLY SOUNDING ALARM OVER SUSPECTED CHINESE SPY

As Jensen's return to Nvidia stunned the nation, Vanity Fair tech correspondent Julia Black appeared sympathetic to the Times reporters.

"My heart goes out to the intrepid team at the @nytimes who did absolutely generational reporting on the Nvidia scandal," Black wrote on X. "I know the feeling of trying to do accountability journalism in a culture that simply does not care about accountability. Incredibly disheartening."

She continued, "There’s a risk calculation you run every time you get a momentous tip about a powerful person. Getting the story out will mean exhausting piles of work, and sometimes considerable personal risk. You have to ask yourself whether it will be worth it—what change you actually hope to see come out of the disclosure. I’d be lying if I said the calculus on this equation hasn’t changed in recent years."

"I am of course not saying that any of these journalists wished to see a specific outcome. (I can’t speak for any of them at all!) But if it were me I would want to feel that my work was being considered thoughtfully, which this (rapid!) outcome suggests it is not. Also yes I’m aware my language is a little melodramatic but some of us still care about things," Black added.

Critics took aim at the sentiment voiced by the Vanity Fair correspondent.

"This is a very disappointing opinion expressed by someone in our industry," NBC News correspondent Tom Winter reacted. "Our job is not to condemn or to affect change. Our job is to provide the most accurate and contextually accurate information so that our audience can have informed points of view and make decisions."

"When we look to 'get' someone it leads to trouble. Should change occur as a result of the information we’ve unearthed then society / the electorate was informed and made decisions accordingly," Winter added.

"Wut? Today’s development does not discount the generational reporting that the NYT team did," CBS News correspondent Weijia Jiang wrote. "This thread implies that the journalists’ end goal was to oust Jensen Huang, which is not the case. They absolutely succeeded at holding someone in power accountable, which IS the job. How the Nvidia board responds is a totally separate issue that doesn’t change the great work they did."

Katie Miller, conservative commentator and wife of White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, reacted to Black, saying, "Reporters should never advocate for an outcome and if they do they should be fired. This Vanity Fair reporter clearly wanted Jensen out. Trust in Legacy Media will remain broken when reporters push intentional outcomes."

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

"What an absolutely bizarre confession for a self-proclaimed 'journalist' to express about what they see as the function and purpose of journalism," journalist Glenn Greenwald wrote.

"Please won't someone think of the journalists," RealClearInvestigations senior writer Mark Hemingway snarked.

Black offered a clarification, replying to Jiang, "I guess what I meant is that the WAY Jensen was reinstated (Trump heard lots of tech complaints/looked at stock market and didn't like what he saw) makes one question whether reporting/facts matter anymore. I'm not sure how this rushed reinstatement mid-investigation counts as accountability."

Representatives for Vanity Fair's parent company, Condé Nast, nor The New York Times responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

World.title: Boston marks Thanksgiving as ‘Day of Mourning’ while historic Plymouth battles anti-Thanksgiving activists
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Boston City Council recognized Thanksgiving as a "National Day of Mourning" ahead of the holiday, continuing a recurring acknowledgment from city leaders as nearby Plymouth, home of the "first Thanksgiving," battles activists in court over their Indigenous peoples observances.

Last week, the Boston City Council passed a resolution designating Thursday, Nov. 26, as a "National Day of Mourning" in Boston after it was introduced by Councilor Benjamin Weber and co-sponsored by 11 other councilors. While the resolution carries no legal weight or changes to city operations, it reflects an annual tradition for the Boston City Council, which has passed similar ceremonial recognitions ahead of Thanksgiving in previous years.

"The story of Thanksgiving that so many of us grew up learning in school fails to acknowledge the devastating consequences that colonialization had and continues to have on Indigenous peoples, " Boston City Councilor At-Large Julia Mejia said in favor of the resolution during a city council meeting on Nov. 18.

HOW VIRGINIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SHAMES KIDS TO MARK THANKSGIVING

"I think it's important that we recognize that these are not simply injustices of the past," Mejia continued. "And as a city, we have a responsibility to ensure that our commitment to equity and justice includes the Indigenous peoples whose lands we live on."

Meanwhile, in nearby Plymouth — the famed site of the 1621 "first Thanksgiving" feast between the Pilgrims and the Wampanoag people, where the United American Indians of New England (UAINE) has held the annual National Day of Mourning every year since 1970 — town officials and organizers appeared in court Monday over a dispute about this year's event logistics.

ARIZONA MAN THREATENED WITH ARREST FOR PREACHING AT HOLIDAY FESTIVAL FILES LAWSUIT

The legal battle centers on a 1998 settlement, signed after a clash between police and demonstrators the year prior, that requires Plymouth to make a mobile stage available for the event.

According to CBS Boston, town officials now say they will not set up a stage on state property without proof of insurance or an outside vendor, citing liability concerns, while UAINE argues the demand violates the decades-old agreement.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Plymouth Independent reported that Plymouth Superior Court Judge Brian Glenny took the arguments under advisement Monday, leaving a ruling pending just days before Thursday's 57th annual gathering on Cole's Hill. According to the outlet, Glenny did not express when a ruling might come, though lawyers involved indicated he understands "time is of the essence."

However, regardless, a UAINE leader told the Plymouth Independent that the event would continue as planned. "I can assure you we will be there Thursday," Mahtowin Munro told the local outlet.

World.title: Florida woman rocking 'Retired Drug Dealer' T-shirt got arrested on, you guessed it, several drug charges
World.content:
The promise of a quieter life in retirement isn't for everyone. Some people call it a career and are able to take life in a completely different direction.

They start checking off the list of things they didn’t get to do while they were working and they don't look back. For others, it isn't that easy.

For whatever reason, they find themselves drawn back to their work. Is it a love for what they do? Is it passion and obsession that drives them?

That's a mystery that's hard to crack. A Florida woman rocking a "Retired Drug Dealer" T-shirt, if what the Citrus County deputies allege is true, appears to be one of those people who can't let their work go.

Angela Moore was arrested on Friday, Nov. 20, following a traffic stop for a vehicle that the Citrus County Sheriff's Office says was unable to maintain its lane, FOX 13 reports.

Moore was a passenger in the backseat of the vehicle and, as it was being searched, deputies found a cut straw on her seat. When a deputy went to retrieve it, she allegedly positioned herself between the open door and the seat.

She then asked while attempting to block his view if she could grab a jacket from inside the vehicle. That's when, thanks to her shirt, they noticed they were dealing with a retired drug dealer.

They searched a backpack belonging to Moore and allegedly found crack cocaine. But that's not all. She also allegedly had items that an active, not retired, drug dealer might have.

FLORIDA WOMAN TELLS POLICE SHE KNOWS NOTHING ABOUT DRUGS THAT ALLEGEDLY FELL OUT OF HER ‘JAIL PURSE’

Deputies said they found "a digital scale, approximately 150 unused plastic baggies and a handwritten ledger containing names and dollar amounts that investigators said were consistent with narcotics transactions."

There were more allegations made once they arrived at the Citrus County Detention Facility. The sheriff's office says that the staff at the facility found cut straws "hidden in her undergarments" that tested positive for fentanyl.

World.title: Congress reacts with anger and skepticism about Jensen Huang reinstatement
World.content:
The stock market was thrilled with the announcement that Jensen Huang was returning as CEO of Nvidia, but lawmakers on both sides of the aisle reacted with shock — and said they still expect him to answer questions next week on Capitol Hill.

“You gotta be kidding me,” Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, told MS NOW when he learned of Huang’s reinstatement 11 days after he resigned in the wake of revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy.

In its announcement, the board said it reached the decision after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that his “reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

“No national security risk? Based on what?” Cornyn asked in a post on X.

President Donald Trump told CNBC he’d spoken to the board “directly and indirectly.”

“One of the things the board wanted to know, is there a national security problem?” Trump said. “And after a lot of research, we — you know, we’ve been looking at this for more than a couple of days, right? This has been a story for a few weeks. We said no, it’s not a problem.”

Lawmakers made clear they still need answers.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 14, 2026. Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty

The Senate Banking Committee, chaired by Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., announced that Huang was scheduled to testify publicly Dec. 3.

“The national security concerns and adherence to export controls will be central to the committee’s oversight and the congressional hearing. Our markets demand transparency. Americans deserve the truth. Our committee will deliver answers,” Scott said in a statement.

A spokesperson for the House Intelligence Committee told NBC News that Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO “changes nothing” for the three House committees that are set to conduct a closed-door transcribed interview with Huang on Dec. 1.

“There are serious questions on national security implications that still need answers. Seems like the only thing that is consistent these days on this issue is our three Committee’s commitment to oversight,” the spokesperson said in a statement.

In a joint statement later Monday, the chairs of the House Select Committee on China, the Intelligence Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee said Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter “have confirmed they will appear for their transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 as previously planned.”

“We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of NVIDIA products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities,” said the three Republicans, Reps. John Moolenaar of Michigan, Rick Crawford of Arkansas and Brian Mast of Florida.

The speedy reinstatement and assurances of the lack of a security risk came after the Justice and Commerce departments last week shared details about their investigation into Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company tied to Alice Huang, the suspected spy with whom Huang was allegedly involved.

Megaspeed reportedly acquired billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips and is also being investigated over concerns that it — and its subsidiaries — smuggled chips to China.

Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said in an X post that “the legal and reputational risk of hiring a CEO who may very well be convicted in the United States or other nations of violating espionage and export control laws is now born by the board of Nvidia, but the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens. The risk of extortion by a Chinese asset who’s been banned by Singapore is risk enough to not rehire Huang.”

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., told NBC News in a phone interview “It’s not my job as a public official to tell a private company who to pick for their CEO. That’s up to the board of directors.”

But, he added, “What I want to know is whether Nvidia violated the export controls of our country with respect to advanced chips. And I want to know if the Department of Commerce did. That will be the purpose of the Banking Committee hearing.”

Sen. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, said in a statement that the administration appears to have known about the Chinese espionage efforts targeting the Nvidia CEO for the past year and his reinstatement “without any apparent accounting or response to the risks to our national security, demands an explanation.”

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said the administration’s “rush to reinstate Jensen Huang underscores the need for Congress to act.”

“Trump is putting his own financial interests and the needs of his billionaire buddies before our national security, emphasizing that he’s learned nothing from his resounding election defeat,” Schumer said in a statement. He added that “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.”

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.”

“Congress will not be deterred from conducting a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce,” Jeffries said.

Lutnick agreed earlier this month to testify before Congress about the Huang scandal amid lawmakers’ scrutiny of China’s access to advanced AI chips.

Democrats pointed Trump’s financial ties to Nvidia, with Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the ranking member on the Oversight Committee, noting the president has a sizeable amount of Nvidia stock. “No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions,” Garcia said.

Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-Ill., cited Nvidia’s donation to Trump’s White House ballroom project as a reason to give the board’s decision extra scrutiny.

“Trump’s assurances cannot be taken at face value, especially after Nvidia’s $25 million donation to his ballroom. Huang must testify at a full public congressional hearing, with every member of the relevant committees allowed to question him,” he posted on X.

Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., questioned the Nvidia board’s decision in a post on social media.

“Jensen Huang had multiple affairs including with subordinates and an alleged Chinese spy,” Ricketts wrote. “His own board described his behavior as lacking ‘candor.’ I’ve served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement.”

“Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress,” he continued. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. I look forward to Mr. Huang coming to the Senate in December.”

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., called the president’s actions “Exhibit A about the political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration’s big tech and AI policy.” He told reporters it was a “good sign” that Republican senators and lawmakers have spoken out because they “realize this is a threat to national security.”
