World.title: Turning Michoacán’s lake fibers into art: An interview with Mexican designer Ana Karina Herrera Gálvez
World.content:
Ana Karina Herrera Gálvez is a 37-year-old Mexican architect whose career has taken an interesting turn toward interior design. Her project, Albaricoque, stands out for breathing new life into some of the oldest craft techniques from her home state, Michoacán.

One of these ancient materials is chuspata, a type of palm that grows along the shores of lakes Pátzcuaro and Cuitzeo. For hundreds of years, even before the colonial period, people have used this plant to make beautiful, practical items. Today, Albaricoque honors this craft by creating masterful objects that help revive the tradition.

Although Herrera Gálvez specializes in furniture design, her work transcends the boundaries of traditional craftsmanship, venturing into artistic expression. She creates totems, sculptures and a variety of forms that blend modern art with ancestral techniques.

Chuspata is woven into remarkably intricate fabrics, and her work showcases both the material and the technique, while its use in contemporary design also helps preserve the craft. In an interview with Mexico News Daily, she shared her thoughts on art, crafts and their significant role in shaping identity and culture.

What is the story behind Albaricoque?

I was working at an architecture firm in Mexico City when I decided to take a trip to Bali. The experience made me appreciate the richness of Mexico’s materials and techniques; I began to recognize the incredible wealth of this country in terms of its history, nature and identity, so I decided to set up Albaricoque in 2020.

The project started in Morelia, where I still live, in the midst of the pandemic. Its aim is to honor the artisanal legacy while creating objects that go beyond aesthetics and connect people with spaces, generating emotions that positively influence their lives.

What inspires you?

I draw a lot of inspiration from nature, shapes, architecture and travel. For me, it also comes during the creative process. Sometimes I start with an idea, but as I experiment with the material, I discover something completely different, and new possibilities or challenges arise.

Can you tell us about your relationship with traditional crafts and techniques in Michoacán?

Living in Michoacán means being surrounded by incredible artisanal crafts. I have always been struck by how simple materials, such as clay and palm fronds, can be transformed into objects with their own identity, meaning and power.

Why are crafts important to you?

Because for me, they represent more than just a way of making things — they embody heritage, knowledge and culture. These techniques have been passed down from generation to generation for centuries and in a world of mass production and quick fixes, we’ve often lost sight of that.

Craftsmanship reminds us of the value of things made with time, patience and experience. Every craft tells a story, has an identity and represents a fulfilling way of life.

1 of 2

Why is it important to you to preserve the craft of working with chuspata fibers from the lakes of Michoacán specifically?

Chuspata fiber is harvested from the lakes Pátzcuaro and Cuitzeo. The braiding techniques used to create furniture and other objects are extremely elaborate and complex, and the craft is deeply rooted in the region’s cultural heritage. The artisanal process involves extracting the fiber, drying it and determining how much water is needed to moisten it before shaping.

Working with chuspata is a lengthy process, and the manual dexterity required for braiding is impressive. At Albaricoque, we work with different types of chuspata weave, including “chain,” “fish” and “openwork.”

How do you collaborate with the artisans?

We collaborate with a variety of artisans who specialize in woodworking, pottery and chuspata weaving, both here in Morelia and in smaller communities such as Ihuatzio and Zinapécuaro. Working with the artisans is an ongoing process of getting to know the materials. It requires patience, plenty of dialogue and a great deal of openness on both sides. While I propose a design, we learn from each other about the limits and possibilities of each material and process.

What threats are currently endangering the preservation of this technique?

Overall, I think climate change poses an immediate threat to chuspata. This year, the area experienced excessive rainfall. Some of the material was salvaged, but it began to rot and deteriorate, leaving very little usable fiber; some of it was also damaged or stained.

In addition, younger generations are beginning to work with this material, but they often struggle to find ways to commercialize their work.

In what ways are you helping to preserve the craft?

I think that by working with local workshops and respecting their prices, we recognize and promote the value of this art in the region.

Collaboration with the workshops is also very important. When artisans see new pieces and new possibilities for materials and techniques, it encourages them to preserve the craft and imagine how their work might connect with other industries, such as architecture, interior design and hospitality.

It is also encouraging to see that many young people, including students, are continuing these traditions.

What are your thoughts on the current Mexican interior design scene?

In my view, Mexico is currently experiencing a really interesting period in interior design. There are more projects with distinctive identities that explore Mexican culture through materials, processes and colors.

However, I believe it is important to move beyond viewing craftsmanship merely as an aesthetic or decorative element and to recognize its value more fully, in a way that reflects its profound richness.

Ana Paula de la Torre is a Mexican journalist and collaborator for various outlets, including Milenio, Animal Político, Vice, Newsweek en Español, Televisa and Mexico News Daily.

World.title: While at APEC, President Sheinbaum took a moment to center her qi
World.content:
President Claudia Sheinbaum shared a video on her official TikTok account over the weekend that showed her practicing qigong in China, where she was attending the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting last week.

In the video, Sheinbaum says that she has been practicing the ancient Chinese exercise for several months because it is “particularly good for your health.” When she was offered a free class in Shenzhen, she decided to take it.

According to the Chinese media outlet Global Times, the session took place on Nov. 17, from 7 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. local time, in the elevator lobby of the hotel where the Mexican delegation was staying.

The session was led by Niu Aijun, vice-dean of the School of Sports and Physical Education at the Shenzhen Polytechnic Institute of Information Technology. The reports identify the sequence as Baduanjin, or The Eight Pieces of Brocade.

Niu told the Global Times that Sheinbaum remarked that she had learned more in that session than in the entire previous year of practicing on her own.

At the end of the session, Niu gave her a pair of cotton insoles that had been hand-embroidered by his mother, and the two of them posed for a photo.

Qigong combines gentle movements, breathing and concentration, and is part of traditional Chinese medicine. It is based on exercises aimed at harmonizing the energy of the body, mind and spirit to promote health and well-being.

Niu cited tennis player Novak Djokovic and German influencer Pamela Reif among other notable foreign practitioners. He attributed qigong’s popularity to its transcendence of language barriers and to the spreading appeal of Chinese culture.

Sheinbaum’s qigong practice is not a new revelation. In August, she said she took up the discipline at the suggestion of Rommel Pacheco, a Pan-American Games multiple medalist in diving before serving in the Chamber of Deputies. He’s now director of the National Commission for Physical Culture and Sport.

With reports from El Sol de México

World.title: In Q3, Mexico’s economy grew 3.3% over 2025, its best showing since 2023
World.content:
Mexico’s economy grew 0.9% during the third quarter of 2026 compared to the previous three months and 3.3% compared to the same period of last year, according to final seasonally adjusted data published by the national statistics agency INEGI on Monday.

The quarter-over-quarter growth rate was unchanged from that reported in preliminary data in late October, while the year-over-year expansion was 0.1 percentage points higher.

The 3.3% year-over-year growth rate is the highest for any quarter since the second quarter of 2023, when Mexico’s economy also expanded 3.3%. The quarter-over-quarter growth rate is lower than the 1.4% expansion in Q2 of 2026, but a much better result than the 0.6% contraction in Q1.

INEGI also reported that Mexico’s economy grew 1.9% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same period of 2025.

Services sector drives growth

The tertiary or services sector outperformed the primary and secondary sectors in terms of growth in the third quarter of 2026 and in the first nine months of the year. The tertiary sector grew:

1.2% in Q3 compared to the April-June quarter.

3.6% in Q3 compared to the third quarter of last year.

2.5% between January and September compared to the first nine months of 2025.

The secondary sector, which includes manufacturing and construction, grew:

0.4% in Q3 compared to Q2.

2.7% in Q3 compared to the same period of last year.

1.1% year over year in the first nine months of 2026.

The primary sector, which includes agriculture and fishing, was Mexico’s worst-performing sector. It grew:

0.3% in Q3 compared to Q2.

1.5% in Q3 compared to the same period of last year.

In the first nine months of 2026, the primary sector contracted 0.9% compared to the same period of last year.

2026 growth forecasts for Mexico’s economy

The most recent Citi Mexico Expectations Survey yielded a median GDP growth projection of 1.8% for 2026, unchanged from the previous survey.

In a social media post after INEGI published its Q3 growth data on Monday morning, Gabriela Siller, director of economic analysis at Banco Base, predicted growth of 2.1% in 2026.

Mexico’s economy grew just 0.8% in 2025, the worst result since a sharp pandemic-induced contraction in 2020.

Other need-to-know economic data

The USD:MXN exchange rate was 19.12 at 1:30 p.m. Monday Mexico City time, according to Bloomberg.

Mexico’s annual headline inflation rate was 3.75% in October, up from 3.45% in September.

The Bank of Mexico’s benchmark interest rate is currently set at 6.25% after a 25-basis-point cut earlier this month.

Mexico received US $47.16 billion in remittances in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 2.1% compared to the same period of last year.

With reports from Reuters and El CEO

World.title: A new WhatsApp chatbot in Mexico has a mission: protecting children from recruitment by organized crime
World.content:
A new WhatsApp chatbot named Fran is seeking to combat the recruitment of children by Mexico’s criminal groups.

Developed by the Mexican nonprofit Reinserta with support from Meta, the parent company of Facebook and WhatsApp, the chatbot provides free information to help young people and families spot the warning signs before an offer of friendship or work becomes a trap.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Reinserta, A.C. (@reinserta)

The automated chatbot also offers emotional support tools and options for those seeking help. It’s designed for adolescents, caregivers and frontline workers who may encounter children at risk.

Reinserta works with young people affected by violence, including children living with incarcerated mothers, and helps young offenders reintegrate into society.

The nonprofit presented Fran last week at its care center in Mexico City, noting that recruitment into cartels and criminal organizations can begin in schools, parks, families or online, including through video games.

Criminal groups exploit vulnerabilities through deception, coercion and promises of jobs or belonging, the organization added.

The danger often comes through someone familiar.

According to figures from a 2022 study Reinserta cited at the launch, half of the detained adolescents it studied who had been recruited by organized crime identified a friend as their recruiter.

Among those studied, eight in 10 had not belonged to gangs before joining a cartel, and seven in 10 reported receiving training within the criminal organization. The study used a nonrandom sample, so its findings are not nationally representative.

Fran grew out of messages from people worried about recruitment and unsure what to do, said Carmen Mari Suárez, Reinserta’s communications director. The organization, whose name means “reintegrate,” was founded in 2013 by psychologists Saskia Niño de Rivera and Mercedes Castañeda.

Reinserta developed the chatbot using its research, prevention guides, and experience supporting adolescents and families.

The goal is to put guidance within reach when concerns first emerge, rather than after recruitment has occurred.

Past cases show how those approaches can escalate.

Mexico News Daily reported in 2021 that three boys were rescued in Oaxaca after a cartel recruiter approached one through the online shooting game Free Fire and offered him work as a lookout.

Another report described a boy recruited as a lookout at 13 who later received hitman training.

The chatbot was inspired by Francisco, who experienced organized crime violence at 6 and became a hitman at 12, Uno TV reported.

Fran is available on WhatsApp by sending a message to “Chatbot Reinserta” at +52 (566) 984-8797.

With reports from Infobae, Uno TV, MVS Noticias and Linea Politica

World.title: Center for experimental sargassum solutions to open in Playa del Carmen
World.content:
Mexico’s first Experimental Center Sargassum Collection and Treatment (CEATS) will be developed in the Caribbean beach town of Playa del Carmen in Quintana Roo, with the aim of finding innovative ways to tackle increasing arrivals of sargassum in high-tourism-value areas.

Playa del Carmen’s mayor, Estefanía Mercado, announced that CEATS will be developed by the National Fund for Tourism Development (Fonatur), in coordination with the Quintana Roo State Government and the Playa del Carmen City Council, with operations expected to commence in the first half of 2027.

The federal government has earmarked more than 2.6 billion pesos (US $135.8 million) to confront the problem, with part of the funding going toward the development of the center. The investment follows a record season in which 162,226 metric tonnes of sargassum were cleared from Quintana Roo’s beaches between April and November, more than double the 85,000 tonnes recorded in 2025.

The center will study the collecting, separating and processing of the algae to explore alternative uses. Authorities say the goal is to limit environmental damage and prevent the loss of sand that results from conventional cleanup methods along the state’s coastline.

Mercado emphasized that the initiative was the result of coordination between President Sheinbaum and the Governor of Quintana Roo, María Lezama Espinosa. She said that if CEATS proves to be successful, the technologies and solutions could be deployed in other sargassum-prone areas.

This year, in Playa del Carmen alone, officials collected 55,378 tonnes of sargassum. Local media sources reported that around 4.3 billion pesos (US $231 million) were allocated to cleanup efforts across the state, carried out by hoteliers and all three levels of government.

“Protecting our beaches also means protecting the livelihoods of thousands of families and the future of Playa del Carmen,” Mercado wrote on her official social media pages on Nov. 16.

With reports from Quadratín Quintana Roo

World.title: Zambelli Asks Court to Cut Her Prison Term
World.content:
A petition to Brazil’s top court asks to subtract time spent in Italian and Brazilian custody, which would shorten the sentence by about 20 months but leave the convictions untouched.

Brazil's Supreme Federal Court in Brasília at night. (File photo: Falcão Alado, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Politics: Brazil

Lawyers for Carla Zambelli, a conservative former federal deputy now living in Italy, asked Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court on Monday 23 November 2026 to count her custody against her sentence. The petition went to Justice Alexandre de Moraes, the judge in charge of her case, and was undecided on Tuesday 24 November.

Zambelli, who represented São Paulo state for the Liberal Party (PL), received a combined sentence of 15 years and 3 months in 2025. She remains a fugitive from Brazilian justice and is on the wanted list of Interpol, the international police cooperation body.

Key Facts Who. Carla Zambelli, a former federal deputy, and Justice Alexandre de Moraes of the Supreme Federal Court.

What. Filed Monday 23 November 2026: her lawyers want about 20 months of custody deducted. No ruling date is known.

Where. The petition is in Brazil; Zambelli lives in Italy, where its top court annulled both extradition approvals.

A petition to Brazil’s top court asks to subtract time spent in Italian and Brazilian custody, which would shorten the sentence by about 20 months but leave the convictions untouched.

What the Petition Asks of Moraes

The defence relies on “detração penal”, a legal rule that counts custody before a final verdict against the eventual sentence. It cites Article 66 of Brazil’s Penal Execution Law, the statute that governs how prison terms are served, which, the defence says, lets the execution judge correct the sentence calculation.

The petition asks to deduct two periods from her combined 15 years and 3 months. One is about 10 months of custody in Italy; the other is 298 days of provisional detention and precautionary measures in Brazil.

The National Council of Justice (CNJ) building in Brasília, whose systems Zambelli was convicted of invading. (File photo)

The defence says the official sentence calculation wrongly records that there are no earlier periods of detention to deduct. It adds that the two periods are missing from the field reserved for deductions in her sentence-execution guide.

The lawyers, who are not named in the petition as reported, argue that ignoring the 10 months in Italy would mean serving a sentence without legal cause. They call opposition to the deduction an unlawful constraint through excess of execution.

The defence argues that her Italian custody was a direct result of Brazil’s own request. Brazil asked for her extradition after Moraes had her name put on Interpol’s wanted list, the petition says.

In 2025 the Supreme Federal Court gave her 10 years in closed regime for invading the systems of the National Council of Justice (CNJ), the judiciary’s oversight body. She also inserted a fake arrest warrant against Moraes, and hacker Walter Delgatti was convicted alongside her.

In August 2025 the court added 5 years and 3 months in semi-open regime for illegal firearm possession and unlawful constraint. The charge stemmed from her chase of journalist Luan Araújo at gunpoint in São Paulo on the eve of the 2022 presidential runoff.

Nine of the 11 justices backed the rapporteur’s vote in that ruling. It became final in October 2025, and Zambelli resigned her seat in December 2025.

Italy Has Twice Blocked Her Return

She had fled Brazil and was detained in Italy from July 2025, and a Rome court authorised her extradition. On 22 May 2026 Italy’s Court of Cassation, its top criminal court, annulled that authorisation in the CNJ case, and she was released.

The reasons, published on 12 June 2026, said the trial did not protect the right to an impartial judge, which they treated as part of the right to defence. They also said Moraes’s concentration of roles, as victim and judge, breached judicial impartiality.

On 1 July 2026 the same court annulled the second authorisation, in the firearm case, and sent it back for a new judgment by another panel of the Rome Court of Appeal. That retrial is pending.

Her Italian lawyer at the time, Fábio Pagnozzi, said that day that the Court of Cassation had found defects in the trial. He added, in words translated from Portuguese: “I am sure that in the end the extradition will be refused.”

Brazil’s federal Attorney General’s Office (AGU) renewed Brazil’s extradition request in the week before 1 July 2026, citing the Brazil-Italy extradition treaty. The Rome court had not yet ruled again on either request at the time of writing.

In a separate filing, the defence asked the Supreme Federal Court to annul the armed-pursuit conviction through a “criminal review”, a challenge to a final sentence. It asked that Supreme Federal Court Justices Gilmar Mendes and Cármen Lúcia not sit on it.

Lawyer Eduardo Maurício said, in words translated from Portuguese: “The intention is to ensure the new trial happens by free draw.” The defence announced the filing on Wednesday 18 November 2026.

The current petition is only a filing, and Moraes decides whether to grant it. The prosecutors’ position and his own are not known, and the Italian proceedings run on a separate track.

If he agrees, her sentence would end about 20 months earlier, roughly 11% of the 15 years and 3 months in total. That would not undo the convictions, lift the 10-year closed-regime duty or settle the extradition fight.

No ruling date or deadline has been announced. Until Moraes acts, Zambelli remains in Italy and on the Interpol list.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Zambelli asking the court to do?

Her lawyers want time already spent in custody counted against her sentence. If Moraes agrees, the end date of the sentence moves earlier.

Does the petition clear her of the convictions?

No. It only asks for a recalculation of the sentence, so the convictions stand.

Could she be sent back to Brazil?

That depends on the retrial in Rome, which is separate from this petition. Italy’s top criminal court has so far annulled both extradition approvals.

World.title: Microsoft Declares Code Red After Outage
World.content:
A failure inside one US software company paused legal deadlines in Brazil, and Microsoft now says its engineers must be able to fix such faults worldwide within an hour.

A plaza on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, Washington, 2006. Photo: Jonathan Schilling, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Technology: Brazil

Microsoft declared a “Code Red”, its most urgent internal alert, on Tuesday 24 November 2026 to overhaul how it prevents and handles major outages, according to internal memos seen by journalists. The move follows the global failure of Thursday 12 to Friday 13 November that took down Exchange Online (Microsoft’s cloud email service), Outlook, Teams and the Copilot AI assistant for about 24 hours.

In Brazil the failure was serious enough that the National Council of Justice (CNJ), the judiciary’s oversight body chaired by the Supreme Federal Court (STF) president, stopped the clock on procedural deadlines nationwide for two days. Latin America’s largest country thus felt an email fault at one US company as a legal pause.

He wrote: “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team.” He added: “Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday.”

Microsoft’s preliminary report, summarised by Charles Lamanna, executive vice-president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, in a public post on Monday 16 November, blames a change made in July to the servers that route connections to Microsoft 365. The defect hid for more than three months and surfaced only when Teams began using the same network layer as Exchange Online about 15 hours before the outage.

The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life. Yesterday’s subject line: “Petrobras plans US$122 billion of investment” Get the brief

By then nearly 14% of capacity in that layer was already out of service, and at the worst point more than 80% of its servers stopped responding. Microsoft says the incident was not linked to cyber activity or AI agents, and chief executive Satya Nadella apologised publicly during the week of 16 November.

Amanda Silver, corporate vice-president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ (the company’s workplace intelligence platform for AI agents), described a “fog of war” in a memo on Monday 23 November. Responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats while diagnostic data sat in fragmented internal tracking systems.

Silver set out five workstreams, among them load shedding (cutting non-essential load to keep core services running), geographic traffic partitioning (splitting traffic by region) and faster recovery. Lamanna told a Code Red review, as reported in her memo, that the failed component had seen “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures”.

Microsoft’s target is to resolve future incidents worldwide within an hour, and it plans to use AI agents to help engineers read system-health data faster. A Microsoft spokesperson said its teams keep working around the clock to apply the lessons learned.

An earlier November memo from Henderson shows the gap. An urgent production fix had taken five to six days to reach worldwide saturation, he wrote, while for the most urgent security issues Microsoft needs “an hour from detection to safe worldwide deployment”, and “we aren’t here yet”.

The memos say the outage hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms and disrupted airline communications. Henderson wrote that he had reviewed the organisational and structural issues that allowed the failures to occur.

In Brazil, Betto Simonetti, president of the Federal Council of the Brazilian Bar Association (OAB, the national body of lawyers), asked on Friday 13 November that court deadlines be suspended. His letter cited the state courts of Santa Catarina, whose confirmed e-mail was unavailable on 12 November, and of São Paulo and Paraná, which warned of harm to their tools.

Edson Fachin, who presides over both the STF and the CNJ, granted the request. Procedural deadlines nationwide stopped counting on Thursday 12 and Friday 13 November and resumed on Monday 16 November.

Fachin noted that Outlook and Teams broadcasts were hit, but the electronic judgment system and other court work were not. The episode shows how a 24-hour email failure at one US company can freeze legal clocks in Latin America’s largest country.

Microsoft has not said what the Code Red will cost or how many engineers it will involve. It has also not said whether customers will receive compensation.

Microsoft said in mid-November that it expected to publish a final root-cause analysis that week. The reporting seen for this story does not say when, or whether, it has appeared.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Code Red at Microsoft?

It is the company’s most urgent internal alert. It makes outage prevention and recovery the top priority for the teams involved.

Did Brazil’s courts stop working?

Court deadlines were paused nationwide, but the electronic judgment system and other court work kept running, according to the court’s president.

Why does this matter outside Microsoft?

Governments, courts and companies rely on its cloud services. A single fault can therefore stop work in many countries at once.

World.title: Two Rio Police Officers Die in Patrol Car
World.content:
Police describe the deaths of the two officers in São Gonçalo as a likely accident, but forensic examinations that should confirm the cause are still pending.

Rio de Janeiro Military Police patrol cars at a vehicle handover ceremony, 26 April 2018, file photo (Photo: Carlos Magno / Governo do Rio de Janeiro, CC BY 2.0 BR, via Wikimedia Commons)

Security: Brazil

Two Military Police officers (the state’s uniformed patrol force) from Rio de Janeiro state were found dead inside their patrol car beside the BR-101, a major federal highway, in São Gonçalo early on Tuesday 24 November 2026. Police suspect an accident, saying the two men, a corporal and a soldier, may have inhaled carbon monoxide, a poisonous exhaust gas, inside the vehicle.

The Federal Highway Police (PRF), the force that patrols federal roads, placed the car at kilometre 308 of the BR-101, in the Itaúna district of São Gonçalo. The city lies in the Rio de Janeiro metropolitan region.

Key Facts Who. Two Rio de Janeiro state Military Police officers, aged 39 and 26, found dead in their patrol car.

What. Police suspect accidental carbon monoxide poisoning from the car itself; forensic tests are pending.

Where. Beside the BR-101 highway, kilometre 308, Itaúna district, São Gonçalo.

The official accounts differ on the timing of the first alarm, so the report here says only that it came early on Tuesday morning. The Federal Highway Police put the discovery at about 07:10, while another account says the Fire Brigade was called at 06:20.

Police identified the dead as corporal Rômulo Medeiros Vinagre, aged 39, and soldier Patrick Trindade Silva, aged 26. The Military Police said both belonged to its 1st Battalion, based in Venda da Cruz, in São Gonçalo.

The Federal Highway Police said the suspicion is accidental death after the two men inhaled carbon monoxide inside the vehicle. The Civil Police of Rio de Janeiro state (PCERJ), the force that investigates crimes, said its main line of inquiry is a carbon monoxide leak from the car itself.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention describes carbon monoxide as an odorless, colorless gas that can cause sudden illness and death if inhaled. It warns people never to run a car inside a garage attached to a house, even with the garage door open.

The case was registered at the 72nd Police Station in São Gonçalo, the local station that opens a formal investigation file. Forensic experts worked at the scene, and police said further investigative steps are under way.

Several questions remain open for the families, colleagues and readers following the case. Police have not said what caused any leak or how long the engine had been running, and no date has been announced for the forensic findings.

Police describe it as a likely accident. The Civil Police say their main line of inquiry is a leak from the vehicle.

What happens next?

Investigators are continuing their work and forensic results are awaited. No date has been announced.

World.title: Brazil’s Dollar Falls 1.3% After Fiscal Vote
World.content:
The rally is relief, not a verdict, and traders say Brazil’s hardest fiscal choices still lie ahead.

Markets: Brazil

Brazil’s currency woke up to relief on Tuesday 24 November 2026 after a sharp sell-off. The US dollar fell as much as 2.2% against the real in morning trading, touching R$5.798, after the Chamber of Deputies passed the government’s fiscal plan late on Monday.

The plan is known in Brazil as the Moretti plan, after Bruno Moretti, the planning minister, and the Chamber approved it unchanged from the text the Senate approved, so it now goes to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for signature. At 10:30 a.m. ET the dollar stood at R$5.851, down 1.3% on the day, and the Ibovespa, São Paulo’s main share index, was up 0.7% at 166,024 points, Rio Times market data show.

The government estimates it is worth R$46 billion to R$56 billion next year (about US$7.9 billion to US$9.6 billion at R$5.85 per dollar). Finance Minister Dario Durigan told a conference hosted by the bank Itaú on Monday 23 November that the government should press ahead with fiscal measures.

He also said the government should settle its central bank board nominations within two weeks. The debt numbers explain why markets care.

Gross government debt stood at 82.9% of national output in September, and net debt at 70%, the central bank reported on 29 October. Otávio Araújo, a senior consultant at the trading firm Zero Markets Brasil, said the plan may bring short-term relief to Brazilian assets.

Investors, he said, still doubt that the government can hold down spending growth and stabilise debt. Thiago Valencia, a partner at the investment firm Valor Investimentos, saw the drop as a market correction more than a vote of confidence.

“It is much more a correction,” he said in Portuguese. “When it hit R$6, the dollar met resistance and took profits.

In recent days the currency had been rising without any correction.”A softer global dollar explained only part of it. The DXY, an index of the dollar against six major currencies, fell about 0.4% in morning trading, while the real’s gain was larger, which suggests part of the move was specific to Brazil.

Rodrigo Moliterno, head of equities at the investment firm Veedha Investimentos, said the approval advanced the government’s fiscal agenda and eased some pressure on the economic team. He added that investors will keep demanding new measures and clarity on who will run economic policy.

The government has not said who will lead the Finance Ministry in the next term, and that gap is one of the things traders say they are watching. For US investors the move shows up twice.

The fund EWZ, the main US-listed Brazil fund, rose about 2% to US$29.82 on Tuesday morning while the Ibovespa gained less than 1% in reais, because a stronger real lifts the dollar value of Brazilian shares.

What Prediction Markets Say Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, priced “no change” at 91.5% for Brazil’s central-bank rate decision in December, with a quarter-point rise at 2.9% and a quarter-point cut at 2.1%, on 24 November at 10:30 a.m. ET. About US$160,000 had been traded on the market. These prices are bets, not polls. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. The reverse also holds: if the real slips back above R$6, dollar returns on Brazilian bonds and ADRs, the US-listed shares of Brazilian companies, shrink. A strong US inflation reading could do that, and the US core PCE price index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, is due on Wednesday 25 November at 8:30 a.m. ET.

Under Article 66 of Brazil’s Constitution, Lula has 15 working days from receipt to sign or veto the plan, which points to roughly Tuesday 15 December. Durigan’s two-week window for the central bank nominations ends around Monday 7 December.

Brazil’s mid-month inflation reading, the IPCA-15, comes on Thursday 26 November, forecast at 4.78% over twelve months against 4.62% before, and the October jobless rate follows on Friday 27 November, forecast at 5.1%, the Rio Times economic calendar shows. Both feed into the central bank’s December rate decision.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did the dollar fall against the real?

The Chamber’s approval of the fiscal plan eased worries about Brazil’s public accounts, and traders also took profits after the dollar touched R$6. Analysts quoted in Brazil say investors still doubt the government can hold down spending.

What happens to the plan next?

President Lula must sign or veto it within 15 working days of receiving it. Markets will then look to the next steps on spending and to the choice of a finance minister.

World.title: US Confidence Jumps to 103.3 in November
World.content:
Rio Times Markets · United States · Brief

American households ended the autumn in a clearly better mood. The Conference Board, a US business research group, said its consumer confidence index jumped to 103.3 in November, far above the 92.5 analysts expected.

The survey is watched as an early hint of how much US households will spend. It also matters abroad, since American demand is what many Latin American and African exporters sell into.

Why. Possible driver: less uncertainty after the US midterm elections, the Conference Board says.

US consumer confidence rose to 103.3 in November, back to levels last seen in January 2025, as households grew more upbeat about jobs.

The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index rose by 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, up from 91.9 in October, the group said on Tuesday, 24 November 2026. The index is set so that 1985 equals 100.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Conference Board Email address Follow

Analysts in the RT economic calendar, our own data feed, had forecast 92.5, so the result beat it by 10.8 points. The survey ran from 1 to 17 November, which means the preliminary figure does not capture the last two weeks of the month.

The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life. Yesterday’s subject line: “Petrobras plans US$122 billion of investment” Get the brief

Jobs Lead the Improvement

The Present Situation Index, which measures how households judge current business and job conditions, rose 13.7 points to 132.8. The Expectations Index, which tracks the short-term outlook for income, business and jobs, gained 9.9 points to 83.6.

The share of consumers calling jobs “plentiful” rose to 30.8% from 26.2%, while those saying jobs are “hard to get” fell to 18.4% from 21.4%. Fergus McCormick, senior economist for global indicators at the Conference Board, said the gain “was led by stronger perceptions of present and future labor market conditions.”

What the Conference Board Says

“Consumer confidence rallied again in November, potentially due to lower uncertainty following the midterm elections,” McCormick said in the release. The midterms are the US congressional elections held in early November.

Prices remain a worry. Consumers’ average 12-month inflation expectations declined for a second month but stayed elevated at 5.7%, and shoppers still expected higher interest rates over the next year.

Spending Plans Edge Up

The Conference Board said consumers planned slightly higher spending on goods and vacations. The share of consumers considering a vacation in the next six months reached 44.9%, up from 42.7% in October.

Plans to buy cars and homes also improved a little. Views split along party lines: confidence among Democrats and Independents rose sharply, while it slipped slightly among Republicans, who still reported the highest level.

What Is Not Known Yet

A survey of opinion is not a count of purchases, and households can feel upbeat while spending little. The release also covers only the first 17 days of November, so it cannot show how the mood moved after that.

The jump is large enough that economists will want to see whether December repeats it. The Conference Board itself called the election link only “potential,” so the link to the election is a view, not a proven finding.

What to Watch Next

Wednesday, 25 November brings the US inflation gauge for October, the PCE price index (personal consumption expenditures), forecast at 3.8% year on year against 3.6% before. The same day brings the second estimate of third-quarter GDP, forecast at 3.5% against 1.5% before.

Firm confidence helps when those numbers arrive, but a hotter inflation print could cool the mood again. For Latin American exporters, steady American demand is the point to follow into the holiday season.

Sources: The Conference Board, US Consumer Confidence press release (24 November 2026); consensus forecasts and earlier values from the RT economic calendar. This is news, not investment advice.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Consumer Confidence Index?

It is a monthly survey of US households run by the Conference Board. A higher number means households feel better about jobs, business conditions and income.

How big was the November jump?

The index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 from 91.9. Analysts had forecast 92.5, per the RT economic calendar.

Does confidence predict spending?

Not reliably. Households can feel gloomy and still spend, or the reverse, so the index is one signal among many.

World.title: Rodrigues on Tsunami Watch After Big Quake
World.content:
Disaster: Mauritius

A strong earthquake struck the Indian Ocean about 326 km north-east of Rodrigues, an island of Mauritius, at 15:06 local time (11:06 GMT) on Tuesday 24 November 2026. Mauritius Meteorological Services, the national weather and warning service, put Rodrigues under a Tsunami Watch, an advance alert for the coast, while the island’s Police Information Room, an emergency desk, said no shaking was felt there.

A strong earthquake struck in the Indian Ocean north-east of Rodrigues, a Mauritius island, on Tuesday.

Alert. Rodrigues is under a Tsunami Watch, a precautionary alert; at 17:40 local time no tsunami had been confirmed.

Impact. No shaking was felt on Rodrigues.

Status. As of 24 November 2026, 15:20 GMT

A strong quake far out in the Indian Ocean has put Rodrigues on a precautionary Tsunami Watch, while agencies differ on its size and no shaking was felt.

The island has seen a closer quake this year. On Tuesday 6 January 2026 at 14:09 local time, a magnitude 5.4 quake struck about 77 km north-east of Rodrigues at 10 km depth, according to a 14:30 bulletin from Mauritius Meteorological Services, the national weather service.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on USGS Email address Follow

Prithiviraj Booneeady, acting director of the service’s station at Vacoas on Mauritius island, told Radio Plus, a Mauritian radio station, that day that it was the closest quake ever recorded to Rodrigues. “At 77 km from Rodrigues, this is the first time we have recorded one so close; that is the reason the tremor was felt in several places,” he said.

That quake caused no victims and no material damage, Defimedia, a Mauritian news site, reported the same day. Tuesday’s event lay about four times farther away, and the Mauritius Police Information Room told Defimedia that no shaking was felt on Rodrigues.

Grand Baie, on the north coast of Mauritius island. (Photo: mwanasimba, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

On Tuesday the weather service placed the epicentre at 17.7°S, 65.7°E, at about 10 km depth, in the Indian Ocean north-east of the island. Its first bulletin, issued at 15:45 local time (11:45 GMT), gave a magnitude of 6.4, Defimedia reported on Tuesday afternoon.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Dangote refinery share sale reportedly cleared” Get the brief

A later bulletin, at 17:40 local time (13:40 GMT), raised the figure to 6.6. USGS, the US Geological Survey, the American government’s seismology agency, lists the same event, us6000ud6h, at 6.4 and at 11:06:14 GMT.

EMSC, the Euro-Mediterranean Seismological Centre, a European monitoring body, gives the same size but places the epicentre at 17.9°S, 65.95°E and the depth at about 3 km. Both outside agencies use moment magnitude (Mw), a scale based on the energy a quake releases.

The scale is logarithmic, so the 0.2 gap between the two estimates is not trivial: it corresponds to roughly twice the released energy. Until the agencies converge, both figures stand side by side.

Either estimate for Tuesday sits at least one full step above the 5.4 of January, which on this logarithmic scale means roughly 30 times more energy released. Size and distance pull in opposite directions here, since the larger quake also struck much farther from the island.

That 17:40 bulletin also placed Rodrigues under a Tsunami Watch, a precautionary alert that the service distinguishes from a warning, valid until 21:00 local time (17:00 GMT). It advised coastal residents, sea users and fishermen not to go to beaches or into the sea, and said an earthquake of this size can sometimes cause a tsunami, according to the bulletin itself.

A watch keeps the possibility of a tsunami open without confirming one, and when it was issued the service had confirmed none and said its checks were continuing. USGS, for its part, rated the event green on its alert scale and did not flag a tsunami.

Rodrigues is an autonomous island of the Republic of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean, roughly 560 km east of Mauritius island. The Police Information Room, relayed by Defimedia on Tuesday afternoon, reported no shaking on the island.

The magnitude is therefore unsettled, and it is not known whether a tsunami formed or was measured. Nor is it known whether the watch has been lifted or whether any damage occurred, because no source consulted reports on either.

The next fixed point is 21:00 Mauritius time (17:00 GMT) on Tuesday 24 November, when the validity of the watch bulletin ends. Any lifting, extension or tsunami finding would come from the service itself.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Tsunami Watch?

A Tsunami Watch is a precautionary alert, distinct from a warning, issued when a quake could cause a tsunami but none has been confirmed. Mauritius Meteorological Services issued one for Rodrigues.

Was the earthquake felt on Rodrigues?

No. The Mauritius Police Information Room told Defimedia that no shaking was felt.

Why do the sources give different magnitudes?

Mauritius Meteorological Services raised its estimate in a later bulletin, while USGS and EMSC list a lower figure. The final agreed magnitude is not yet known.

World.title: Cuba Visitors Down 65.7% Through October
World.content:
Cuba’s government blames US pressure for hotel closures and the exit of foreign chains, while October’s count stays far below last year’s.

Photo: Tacorontey / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Economy: Cuba

Cuba is entering its winter tourist season with far fewer visitors than a year ago. Only 29,376 international visitors arrived in October 2026, according to ONEI, the country’s national statistics office.

Over January to October the island received 507,083 visitors, 65.7% fewer than in the same months of 2025. The slump is one more strain in the standoff with Washington that we follow in our Cuba news coverage.

The October figure may still change when ONEI closes its books. It was only slightly above September’s 27,354, the weakest of the first nine months, so the monthly pace has barely moved.

The slump has built all year. At the end of September ONEI had counted 477,707 visitors, 65.1% below the same period of 2025, as we reported in our earlier look at the slide; the full year 2025 closed at 1,810,663.

The count has slipped with each reporting period: 450,353 visitors for January–August (down 64.4%), 477,707 for January–September (down 65.1%) and 507,083 for January–October (down 65.7%). Monthly arrivals have stayed in a narrow band since August, at 30,490, then 27,354, then 29,376.

A year earlier, January–October 2025 had brought 1,477,892 visitors, according to ONEI’s earlier series. ONEI’s monthly bulletin is the main public measure of arrivals, and the October edition is labelled preliminary.

File photo: Plaza de la Catedral in Old Havana, August 2016. Photo: Yoeztudioz / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

On Wednesday, July 29, 2026, Prime Minister Manuel Marrero told the National Assembly of People’s Power, Cuba’s parliament, that US pressure had driven seven international hotel chains out of the country. Spanish groups Meliá, Iberostar and Barceló were among those that had announced their exit by then.

Marrero said 73% of hotel facilities were closed, leaving 25,000 jobs in limbo, and blamed what he called a US oil blockade and the threat of US sanctions on international companies. He said the pressure had brought tourism close to a standstill.

In the same session he announced steps to revive the sector: private management of hotels, car rental and passenger transport, and permission for private operators to work as tourist agents and guides. Cuba’s parliament had approved a package of 176 economic reforms in June.

Official figures put arrivals at about 4.6 million in 2018 and more than 4.2 million in 2019, when Washington had eased travel limits and relations were thawing. This year’s ten-month total is a fraction of those peaks.

For US travellers and investors, the bulletin shows how thin Cuba’s tourism base has become before the busy months. ONEI counts a visitor as anyone travelling temporarily for holidays, family visits or business, so the total is wider than hotel guests.

Cuba treats November to April as its high season, so the next monthly bulletins will show whether October was the bottom. The bulletin does not say how much visitors spent, so the hit to Cuba’s hard-currency income cannot be measured from it.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why are fewer people visiting Cuba?

Cuba’s government says US pressure pushed foreign hotel chains out of the country, and 73% of hotels were closed by late July. We found no US response to the latest visitor data.

Does the visitor count include Cubans living abroad?

ONEI lists them on a separate line. Its definition of a visitor also covers family trips and business travel, so it is wider than hotel guests.

Sources: ONEI bulletin “Arribo de viajeros. Visitantes internacionales, octubre de 2026”; ONEI visitor data for January–September 2026; Prime Minister Manuel Marrero, address to the National Assembly, July 29, 2026. The ONEI release could not be opened directly; its figures are as published in Cuban and regional press.

World.title: Nicaragua Natural Resources Explained 2026
World.content:
NICARAGUA · RESOURCES

Nicaragua sells gold, coffee, beef and sugar abroad, with exports up 15.4% to US$8.9089 billion in 2025, the Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN) said on 27 February 2026, and its president called it a record on 25 March. Gold alone earned US$1.9710 billion, the BCN’s fourth-quarter 2025 foreign trade report shows.

For readers in the United States, these goods connect Nicaragua to American sanctions lists, tariff schedules and supermarket shelves. The BCN’s export table for January to September 2026 shows US$2.1323 billion of goods going to the US, of which gold was US$1.2593 billion.

Key Facts Total exports Record US$8.9089 billion in 2025, including US$3.581 billion from export-factory parks called free zones.

Gold US$1.9710 billion in 2025, up 45.6%, at an average US$3,319.7 per ounce.

Coffee, beef, sugar Coffee earned US$918.4 million and beef US$960.8 million in 2025; sugar fell 30.4% to US$165.9 million.

Sanctions US Treasury has sanctioned Nicaragua’s state miner and gold firms since 2022, most recently on 16 April 2026.

As of 24 November 2026: full-year data runs to 2025; the latest quarterly report cited is Q1 2026.

A plain-English guide to what Nicaragua digs, grows and generates, who buys it, and how US sanctions and tariffs shape that trade.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Nicaragua 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 2 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

Gold and Mining Concessions

Gold is Nicaragua’s top commodity export, according to US Treasury press release jy2339 of 15 May 2024. In 2025 the BCN’s fourth-quarter foreign trade report put gold exports up 45.6% on 2024.

Price explains a large part of the rise. The BCN reports 593.7 thousand ounces sold in 2025 at an average US$3,319.7 per ounce, against US$2,340.7 per ounce in 2024, when exports were US$1.3539 billion.

The first quarter of 2026 made the pattern clearer. The BCN’s first-quarter 2026 foreign trade report shows gold exports of US$898.7 million, up 152.1%, on 190.0 thousand ounces at US$4,728.9 per ounce.

A year earlier, in the first quarter of 2025, the BCN recorded US$356.5 million on 128.6 thousand ounces at US$2,772.6 per ounce. Price and volume both rose, and price rose by more.

On 12 December 2023, La Gaceta, the official gazette, listed 20 inactive mining concessions (state licences to mine a set area). The Ministry of Energy and Mines, which grants and withdraws mining licences, cancelled them.

On 12 February 2025, the ministry revoked eight open-pit concessions, officially 79,373.38 hectares. Mineral Trading S.A., a mining company, lost four of them.

On 31 October 2025, Calibre Mining Nicaragua, now part of the Canadian miner Equinox Gold, relinquished two permits, Kisauri and Geranio. Kisauri covers 43,457.09 hectares and Geranio 47,895.22, or 91,352.31 in all, and two more permits of 87,541.45 hectares were given up in the days before.

Our report on a mining concession extension in Nueva Segovia shows one recent local case. This guide leaves 2026 grants out because no gazette notice could be confirmed.

Equinox Gold’s Form 6-K to 30 June 2026, a report foreign companies file with US regulators, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, shows Nicaragua gold output of 140,757 ounces in the first half of 2026. The second quarter gave 59,476 ounces, and 2026 guidance is 225,000 to 250,000.

The filing gives output and guidance, not sales by buyer, so any effect of sanctions is not stated there. Our report on gold sanctions and US buyers follows that side of the story.

File photo, 2016. A picker holds a basket of coffee cherries at El Tuma-La Dalia, Nicaragua. Photo: Maren Barbee, CC BY-SA 2.0, Wikimedia Commons.

US Sanctions and the Gold Trade

The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), the Treasury office that enforces US sanctions, built its pressure on gold in steps. On 27 November 2018, OFAC listed the first people under Executive Order 13851, a US order aimed at repression and corruption in Nicaragua: Néstor Moncada Lau, national security adviser to President Daniel Ortega, and Rosario Murillo, his wife and then vice president.

On 17 June 2022, Treasury sanctioned ENIMINAS (Empresa Nicaragüense de Minas, the state miner) and its board president Ruy Delgado López. Its press release jy0822 said Nicaraguan gold exports to the US in 2021 were above US$744 million, up 30%, and 79% of all gold exports.

Brian Nelson, Treasury’s Under Secretary for Terrorism and Financial Intelligence, said that day that “the regime has turned its back on the Nicaraguan people”. On 24 October 2022, Treasury designated the General Directorate of Mines, the Energy Ministry’s mining office, and a new executive order amended Order 13851 to allow sanctions on the gold sector.

A general licence, a blanket permission to finish existing deals, gave a wind-down period, according to release jy1046 of 24 October 2022. Nelson said then: “we can and will use every tool at our disposal to deny the Ortega-Murillo regime the resources they need”.

On 15 May 2024, release jy2339 named COMINTSA, a mining company, and Capital Mining Investment Nicaragua, a gold intermediary. On 16 April 2026, release sb0451 named seven gold firms (EMSA, Minero, Thomas Metal, Xinxin, Brother Metal, Zhong Fu and Santa Rita).

Treasury tied those listings to the 2025 seizure of the BHMB Mining Nicaragua plant, which had US investment, and says BHMB reportedly received no compensation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said: “The United States will not allow the illicit confiscation of American-owned assets”.

The BCN’s January to September 2026 export table shows how large the US link still is, with US$1.2593 billion of gold among US$2.1323 billion of goods sent to the US. Gold to Canada was US$903.7 million, and all markets together took US$5.0291 billion.

The BCN’s first-quarter 2026 report puts the US share of goods exports at 41.1%, with Canada at 20.9% and El Salvador at 6.6%. In the fourth quarter of 2025 the US took 38.0% and Canada 17.4%.

For US readers, these listings name specific firms and people, not the whole country, and each round added names. Whether they will reach more gold buyers is not known.

Who owns and runs these firms is covered in our guide to who runs Nicaragua’s economy. The Treasury releases cited above list the named firms.

Coffee, Beef and Sugar

Coffee earned US$918.4 million in 2025, up from US$524.4 million in 2024, the BCN’s fourth-quarter 2025 report shows. Exporters sold 3,370.6 thousand quintales (100-pound sacks) at an average US$272.5 per quintal.

In the first quarter of 2026, coffee exports were US$366.0 million, up 60%, on 1,195.0 thousand quintales at US$306.3 each, the BCN’s first-quarter 2026 report says. The season ahead is covered in our report on the 2026/27 coffee harvest.

Beef earned US$960.8 million in 2025, up 27.1%, on 329.8 million pounds at US$2.9 per pound, the BCN’s fourth-quarter 2025 report shows. Ovidio Reyes, the BCN’s president, said on 25 March 2026 that beef exports were above US$900 million.

In the first quarter of 2026, beef exports were US$289.6 million, up 35.7%, on 89.7 million pounds, the BCN reports. Its January to September 2026 table shows US$357.0 million of beef going to the US.

Reyes said on 25 March 2026 that 2025 exports came to almost US$9 billion, a record. Free zones, the export-factory parks, contributed US$3.581 billion of that total, up 1.6%.

Sugar earned US$165.9 million in 2025, down 30.4%, on 7.6 million quintales at US$21.8 each, the BCN’s fourth-quarter 2025 report says. In the first quarter of 2026 it earned US$82.7 million, down 23.0%.

Coffee to the US was US$243.5 million and sugar US$36.0 million from January to September 2026, the BCN’s export table shows. Lobster to the US added US$27.2 million, and the fishing sector earned US$186.4 million in 2025, up 6.7%, per the BCN’s fourth-quarter report.

2026 Targets, Not Results Food BCN reports food exports of US$3.4079 billion in 2025, up 18.3% (Reyes to Nicaragua’s National Assembly, 7 May 2026); the wider 2026 food and forestry target is US$3.5957 billion.

Beef The BCN’s national production plan targets US$1.0757 billion in 2026 and a 2026/27 production of 433.9 million pounds, up 4.2%.

Coffee Plan target of US$1.0263 billion in 2026 and 3.0 million quintales in 2026/27, a 7.1% decline.

Sugar Plan target of US$160.8 million in 2026 and 17.5 million quintales in 2026/27, up 9.6%.

CAFTA-DR, the Sugar Quota and Section 301 Tariffs

CAFTA-DR is the free-trade deal between the US, Central American countries and the Dominican Republic. It gives Nicaragua a duty-free sugar quota of 30,800 metric tons for calendar 2026, a notice of 18 December 2025 in the Federal Register, the US government’s daily gazette, states.

The US Trade Representative (USTR), the White House trade office, opened a case on Nicaragua under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, a US trade law against unfair practices, on 10 December 2024. On 20 October 2025 it found Nicaragua’s practices actionable.

On 10 December 2025 USTR announced a tariff on goods not originating under CAFTA-DR. The Federal Register notice of 29 December 2025 (volume 90, page 60850) sets it at 0% from 1 January 2026, 10% from 2027 and 15% from 2028. Other US tariffs changed repeatedly during 2026, so the picture has moved.

Check the current USTR notice before relying on any rate; our explainer on US tariffs on Nicaragua gives background.

Electricity Mix in 2025

Nicaragua generated 4,670.1 gigawatt-hours (GWh), a standard unit for large amounts of electricity, in 2025. The figure comes from the BCN’s Statistical Yearbook 2025, Table I-29, which uses preliminary data from INE, the national energy institute.

Electricity Mix 2025 Hydro 637.0 GWh, or 13.6% of generation.

Geothermal 720.5 GWh, or 15.4%, from underground heat.

Thermal 1,571.1 GWh, or 33.6%, from plants that burn fuel.

Others 1,730.2 GWh, or 37.0%; the table does not split this group.

Isolated systems 11.4 GWh.

The table does not split the others group into wind, biomass and solar, and it does not label which sources are renewable. Hydro and geothermal alone gave 29.1% of 2025 generation.

An upper bound follows from the table. If every unit in the others group were renewable, hydro, geothermal and others would add to about 66%, an inference from the table and not an official number.

Thermal plants still supplied about one third of 2025 generation, so fuel prices remain part of the story. The table is preliminary, so shares may change.

Lake Cocibolca and the Canal That Was Never Built

Lake Cocibolca, also called Lake Nicaragua, is Central America’s largest lake and Nicaragua’s biggest freshwater reservoir. No official area or depth figure from INETER, the national territorial institute, was found.

The Río San Juan drains the lake to the Caribbean and runs along much of the border with Costa Rica. That makes the lake and river a border matter too.

The Río San Juan and its rapids near El Castillo, Nicaragua, on the river that runs along much of the border with Costa Rica. Photo: Stoschmidt, CC BY 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.

On 13 June 2013 the National Assembly approved Law 840, which gave the Grand Canal concession to HKND Group, a Cayman Islands company owned by Chinese businessman Wang Jing. Article 3 of the law set the concession at 50 years from the start of commercial operations, renewable for another 50 at the investor’s option.

On 8 May 2024 the National Assembly, Nicaragua’s parliament, voted unanimously to repeal Law 840. It also reformed Law 800, the canal’s legal regime.

No canal has been built. The political background is in our explainer on Nicaragua’s history.

What Is Not Known

Installed capacity by plant and the renewable share are not in any official table found for this guide. The renewable share of electricity is therefore not confirmed.

Full-year 2026 export totals are not out, and the latest data are the first quarter of 2026 and the BCN’s January to September table. The official area and depth of Lake Cocibolca are also unconfirmed.

The 2026 figures in the targets list are goals, not results. Full-year 2026 figures from the BCN will show whether the 2025 record, built on high gold prices, holds.

In Plain English Concession A state licence to explore or mine a defined area under set terms.

Free zone A park where firms make goods for export under a special legal regime.

Quintal A 100-pound sack, the trade unit for coffee and sugar in this guide.

OFAC The US Treasury office that enforces sanctions and lists the people and firms it targets.

CAFTA-DR The free-trade deal between the US, Central American countries and the Dominican Republic.

Section 301 A US trade-law power that lets USTR act against practices it finds unfair.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are Nicaragua’s main natural resources?

Gold, coffee, beef and sugar lead its exports, alongside hydro and geothermal power. The BCN reported total exports of US$8.9089 billion in 2025.

How much gold does Nicaragua export?

The BCN reports US$1.9710 billion of gold exports in 2025, up 45.6%, and US$898.7 million in the first quarter of 2026. Higher prices drove much of the rise.

Does the US sanction Nicaraguan gold?

US Treasury has sanctioned the state miner ENIMINAS, the General Directorate of Mines, the Energy Ministry’s mining office and several gold firms between 2022 and 2026. The listings name specific firms and people.

What tariff applies outside CAFTA-DR?

USTR’s schedule is 0% from 1 January 2026, 10% from 1 January 2027 and 15% from 1 January 2028. US tariffs changed repeatedly in 2026, so check the current USTR notice.

Was the Nicaragua canal ever built?

No. The National Assembly repealed Law 840, the Grand Canal concession, on 8 May 2024, and no canal has been built.

Sources: Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN), foreign trade reports for the fourth quarter of 2025 and the first quarter of 2026, export table for January to September 2026, and Statistical Yearbook 2025 (Table I-29); BCN press note of 27 February 2026, BCN statements of 25 March 2026 and 7 May 2026; US Treasury press releases jy0822, jy1046, jy2339 and sb0451; US Treasury OFAC page of 27 November 2018 on Executive Order 13851; USTR Section 301 notice, Federal Register 90 FR 60850 (29 December 2025); Federal Register notice on the CAFTA-DR sugar quota (18 December 2025); Equinox Gold Form 6-K to 30 June 2026 (US Securities and Exchange Commission, EDGAR); Ministry of Energy and Mines notices, La Gaceta of 12 December 2023; National Assembly decisions on Law 840 and Law 800 (8 May 2024) (all accessed 24 November 2026).
