World.title: Developer drops Haapsalu wind farm plans
World.content:
Haapsalu 1 Energiapark OÜ, which had planned to build a wind farm in the villages of Käpla, Jõõdre, Lannuste, Vätse, Haeska and Ammuta, has informed the Haapsalu city government that it is abandoning the project.

Haapsalu 1 Energiapark OÜ is owned by RNW Projects OÜ and Ignitis Renewables DevCo1 OÜ, the latter of which is part of Ignitis Renewables, a green energy company operating in the Baltic states and Poland. The developer had sought to erect up to 10 wind turbines with a maximum blade tip height of 280 meters in Lääne County.

Ignitis told local paper Lääne Elu that studies showed the proposed site lies along important flight corridors for the white-tailed eagle and the lesser white-fronted goose, both of which are Category I protected species in Estonia. As a result, the area is unsuitable for wind farm development.

Sander Sorts, Ignitis Renewables' head of development in Estonia, said the company had known from the outset that the site's proximity to Matsalu would require thorough environmental studies, the findings of which would ultimately determine the site's suitability.

"The data available at the time suggested that it might be possible to build a wind farm at this location by implementing measures to mitigate the impact on birdlife. However, the findings of the studies did not confirm our initial assumption that the site was suitable, prompting us to decide not to proceed with the project," Sorts told Lääne Elu.

Ignitis conducted the bird survey before the City of Haapsalu had initiated a local government designated spatial plan or a strategic environmental assessment. City authorities were aware of the survey and wanted to review its findings before deciding whether to initiate the designated spatial plan. Deputy Mayor Peep Aedviir told Lääne Elu that the city government never saw the study.

World.title: Estonian PM: Closing rail border crossing with Russia could be next step
World.content:
Prime Minister Kristen Michal said Estonia's decision to close its land border with Russia is effectively indefinite and designed to withstand legal challenges. The government has not yet decided whether to close the rail border crossing, but Michal said that option could be considered as a future step.

Speaking on an ERR radio program Tuesday, Michal said the government reached the border closure decision only after careful consideration, but Russia's continued hostile actions and attacks left Estonia with no alternative.

According to the prime minister, Estonia has been targeted 12 times in incidents attributable to Russia, and previous warnings — including reduced border crossing hours and the introduction of full customs inspections — failed to change Moscow's behavior.

"We acted in a very Estonian way — calmly, firmly and perhaps even somewhat slowly. In response to Russia's actions, we reduced border crossing hours and imposed full customs controls while continually sending a signal. The message all along has been: understand, friends, that if you do not behave reasonably, we will eventually reach the point where crossing the border is no longer possible," Michal said.

Narva border station on the Estonian side. Source: Sergei Stepanov/ERR

Although the measure is officially described as a temporary closure, the government has tied it to a review of the security situation in six months, which in practice means the border could remain closed indefinitely.

"The official title is a temporary border closure, but in substance it is an indefinite closure. We included a clause stating that the border will remain closed until the government reviews whether the security situation or the grounds for the decision have changed after six months. I personally do not believe the threat from Russia will have diminished by then, so the border will remain closed unless a future government decides otherwise," Michal said.

Asked whether the decision would hold up legally if challenged in court by, for example, the Narva City Council, Michal replied in the affirmative.

The prime minister acknowledged that the closure will have consequences for border regions and said the state must introduce mitigation measures. However, he emphasized that the move is primarily painful for Russia.

Michal also said domestic criticism of the decision has mainly come from the Center Party and circles around MP Aleksandr Tšaplõgin, while Estonia's actions are understood internationally.

Border crossing in Narva. Source: Sergei Stepanov/ERR

As for the future of the Narva rail crossing, Michal said no final decision has been made. In his view, responses do not always need to be symmetrical, and pressure can be applied through other measures at the European Union level.

"We have not made any additional decision on that yet, and it remains the next step if one is needed. Responses do not always have to be symmetrical or identical. They can come elsewhere. For example, we have long advocated in Europe for measures that are very painful for Russia, such as freezing assets, monitoring the shadow fleet and imposing visa bans on Russian fighters," Michal said.

He added that the European Commission's recent proposal to place Russian fighters on a visa ban list, together with the border closure, sends a clear message that they are not welcome in Europe.

The Estonian government decided on November 20 to close all road border crossings between Estonia and Russia. Border crossings at Narva, Luhamaa, Koidula and Saatse will be closed to pedestrians and vehicles starting at 7 a.m. on December 1. Rail freight traffic will continue. The government said the decision was made in response to sabotage attacks by Russian intelligence services targeting Estonia's defense industry companies.

People crossing the Estonia-Russia border in Narva. Source: Sergei Stepanov/ERR

World.title: Data center grid requests exceed Estonia's peak power demand several times over
World.content:
With 600 megawatts already signed up for and 1,300 megawatts in active offers, Elering is nearing capacity, prompting calls for developers to build matching domestic generation.

Although only one major data center currently operates in Estonia, Elering has already signed connection agreements for 600 megawatts and issued active connection offers for a further 1,300 megawatts, even as some of the additional 3,300 megawatts in pending applications may never materialize.

The surge follows seven major data center connection filings totaling 2,900 megawatts reported in recent days, prompting warning flags over grid bandwidth and consumer power prices.

"First, the grid, including its power lines and substations, needs enough capacity to carry that electricity. Given the 600 megawatts in connection agreements we've signed and the 1,300 megawatts in offers that are still valid, we're close to the point where we can't issue any new connection offers. What matters is where the electricity will be generated," Elering board member Reigo Kebja told "Aktuaalne kaamera".

Building energy-hungry server farms without adding matching domestic generation will drive up electricity prices, warned Mart Landsberg, a professor at Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech).

"If we want these data centers to come to Estonia instead of going elsewhere, we need to start attracting new investment in electricity generation now. There are several ways to do that. One option would be to require each data center to add generation capacity in Estonia to help meet its demand," Landsberg said.

Unlike Finland, which is already considering such a requirement, Estonia imposes no obligation on data centers to pair projects with new power generation. Economy and Industry Minister Erkki Keldo said he plans to discuss with developers how the projects can deliver broader public value.

"Data centers generate less direct tax revenue than traditional industry, for example. They do create jobs, including well-paid ones, and buy services from outside suppliers. They have a positive impact on the economy, but it's limited. That's why I want to discuss with businesses what measures could benefit society, whether through additional taxes or by bringing new power generation to Estonia," Keldo said.

Most of the proposed data center capacity is clustered along high-voltage transmission lines in western Estonia's Lääne-Nigula and Lääneranna municipalities, particularly around the small towns of Risti and Lihula but with multi-billion-euro projects also eyed in Tapa, east of Tallinn. By contrast, Estonia's sole existing next-generation facility — Greenergy Data Centers in Hüüru, Harju County, — currently draws just 2 megawatts, though there are plans in place to scale that right up to 200 megawatts by early 2028.

Energy analysts have warned that building even a fraction of the proposed capacity without matching domestic generation would increase Estonia's reliance on power imports from Finland, and place new balancing strain on the grid.

Data centers are large-scale facilities housing networked servers that power cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI), and they place heavy demands on the grid because they require uninterrupted electricity 24 hours a day to run energy-intensive processors and constant cooling systems.

World.title: Government to offset district heating and network fees during winter
World.content:
The government has decided to cushion the impact of high energy prices during the heating season by compensating part of district heating costs and reducing electricity and gas network charges for consumers.

In addition to eliminating Elering's transmission network fee and compensating electricity and gas network charges, the government will reimburse household consumers for 80 percent of district heating costs above €110 per megawatt-hour.

Energy Minister Erkki Keldo said Tuesday's cabinet discussion focused on helping those most affected by rising energy prices.

"We made a principled decision to ease the impact of high energy prices on consumers during the upcoming heating season, from December through the end of March. High energy bills affect all of us, but they hit lower-income households the hardest," Keldo said.

Erkki Keldo. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Beyond district heating, the plan also covers other energy sources. The government will allocate €36 million in congestion fee revenue to reduce Elering's transmission network fee to zero, benefiting households, businesses and local governments.

Household consumers will also receive full compensation for gas network charges up to monthly consumption of 2,500 kilowatt-hours, while electricity network charges will also be compensated, with exact details to be announced in the coming days.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal said on an ERR radio program Tuesday that the district heating support measure is primarily aimed at residents in areas with higher heating costs who have limited opportunities to switch to cheaper contracts.

"The government's understanding was that we would compensate part of district heating costs for household consumers in areas where heating is more expensive. In some regions, where investments have not yet been made and where district heating remains costly, this helps reduce the impact. Fortunately, many people have already fixed their energy contracts, but in higher-cost district heating areas that often is not possible," Michal said.

The prime minister added that using €36 million in congestion fee revenue would help reduce inflation and would not require a supplementary budget. The exact cost and implementation details of the remaining support measures are expected to be finalized this week or next.

"€36 million comes from congestion fee revenue, so we do not need a supplementary budget for that. As for district heating support and compensation of gas and electricity network charges, we are talking about roughly €30 million — and I emphasize roughly, because the figure will be refined. The preliminary estimate is around €30 million, but it may change depending on the mechanisms we ultimately agree on," Michal said.

World.title: Omnicom consolidates MENA operations under single leadership
World.content:
LONDON: Omnicom has launched a new unified regional structure that brings its operations in the Middle East and North Africa under a single leadership team.

The move consolidates the group’s media, advertising, public relations and data businesses in the region under one operating framework.

Ghassan Harfouche, who led the Middle East Communications Network for more than 15 years, has been appointed group CEO.

Elda Choucair will lead Omnicom Media MENA, while Reda Raad will lead Omnicom Advertising MENA.

The leadership team will join a newly formed Omnicom MENA Executive Board that includes Omnicom Chairman and CEO John Wren, Omnicom Media Global CEO Florian Adamski, Omnicom Media EMEA CEO Dan Clays, and Omnicom Advertising Global CEO Andrew Robertson.

Wren said the new structure would create a “stronger, more connected” Omnicom across the region.

He said: “Ghassan’s experience leading MCN gives him the insight and credibility to connect our capabilities and strengthen our client partnerships.”

Omnicom MENA employs more than 3,500 people across 14 markets.

The company said the unified operating and leadership structure would strengthen its regional position and bring together expertise from across the group to address clients’ business challenges.

It said the new organization would deliver more integrated solutions, accelerate knowledge-sharing and scale innovation in areas including artificial intelligence, data-driven solutions and platforms.

Under the new structure, Omnicom Media MENA, led by Choucair, becomes the region’s largest media network, bringing together UM, OMD, PHD, Hearts United and Initiative.

Omnicom Advertising MENA, led by Raad, will unite Impact BBDO, McCann and TBWA\Raad.

Omnicom Public Relations’ communications group, including Weber Shandwick, FleishmanHillard and Portland, will be led by Ziad Hasbani. Karim Slim will oversee the company’s Data & Tech operations in MENA, including Precision Marketing and Acxiom. Mohamad Haidar has been appointed chief financial officer of Omnicom MENA.

The move comes as Omnicom continues to integrate Interpublic Group, which it acquired in November 2025 for $9 billion, making it the world’s largest advertising and marketing holding company.

The acquisition has prompted a global restructuring that has included agency consolidations and workforce reductions.

World.title: French officials order former President Sarkozy’s corruption case to trial
World.content:
PARIS: French officials on Tuesday ordered a corruption case involving former President Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, model and singer Carla Bruni, to go to trial, setting an initial pre-trial hearing for April 1, 2027.

Investigators had been probing the retraction of testimony by French-Lebanese businessman Ziad Takieddine, a self-described “middleman in the shadows” who had alleged that late Libyan leader Muammar Qaddafi sent Sarkozy’s successful 2007 presidential campaign millions of euros in cash before withdrawing his account in 2020.

Takieddine has since died.

Sarkozy and his wife have been charged with receiving stolen goods, witness tampering and criminal conspiracy, the French financial prosecutor’s office said in a statement on Tuesday. Lawyers for Sarkozy and Bruni did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Sarkozy was convicted last year in a related case, of criminal conspiracy over attempts to procure campaign funds from Libya. He received a five-year jail sentence, making him the first post-war French president to be imprisoned. Three weeks into his jail sentence, a court released him under judicial supervision, with terms including a ban on leaving France. He has appealed the conviction.

Sarkozy has denied the allegations, which were first made by one of Qaddafi’s sons.

Sarkozy hosted Qaddafi on a visit to Paris five months after his election, with the Libyan leader pitching a Bedouin-style tent near the Elysee Palace, before becoming one of the chief advocates of the NATO-led campaign against Qaddafi that resulted in his overthrow and killing by rebels in 2011.

Sarkozy has also been convicted for corruption and influence peddling and illegal campaign financing over his failed 2012 re-election bid.

World.title: Turkish military helicopter crashes during training flight, killing 5 crew members
World.content:
ISTANBUL: A Turkish Air Force helicopter crashed during a training flight in western Turkiye on Tuesday evening, killing five crew, the Defense Ministry said. It was the second helicopter crash to hit the Turkish Armed Forces in as many weeks.

The AS-532 Cougar went down after taking off from Eskisehir, home to the air force’s 1st Main Jet Base Command.

“An AS-532 type helicopter belonging to our air force, which took off from Eskisehir for training purposes, has crashed,” the ministry said in a statement. “The wreckage of the helicopter has been reached and search and rescue operations are continuing.”

The ministry later confirmed fatalities, saying: “Five of our heroic comrades-in-arms serving in the air force helicopter that crashed ... have been martyred.”

Media footage showed emergency teams at the scene of the crash near Yorukakcayir, a village around 15 kilometers (9 miles) west of Eskisehir city center. The helicopter’s smoking fuselage appeared to be largely destroyed.

The Cougar is a twin-engine, multi-purpose helicopter widely deployed by militaries around the world.

On Nov. 12, an army Sikorsky S-70 crashed near Malatya in southern Turkiye, killing four crew members.

World.title: Twenty-five hostages taken in botched robbery in Colombia’s Cartagena
World.content:
BOGOTA: Gunmen held 25 people hostage Tuesday in a supermarket in the Colombian tourist city of Cartagena, prompting a major police operation, authorities said.

The drama added to tension in a country reeling from a car bombing overnight in another city but there were no reports of the two events being linked.

Images shared by local media showed people kneeling inside the Exito supermarket as police snipers went into position on the roofs of surrounding buildings.

President Abelardo de la Espriella said the assailants are now holding 25 people hostage after releasing a first group of five captives.

❗️ ARMED MEN take ENTIRE SUPERMARKET HOSTAGE in Cartagena, Colombia Hostages FILMED SITTING on CHAIRS as GUNMEN PATROL directly BEHIND THEIR HEADS https://t.co/AaJvvPCzQa — RT (@RT_com) November 24, 2026

He said the attackers had meant to rob an armored vehicle in a shopping center but when police were called in, the would-be robbers took refuge in the supermarket.

“They had no choice but to take cover in one of the stores and abduct 30 people, of which they have now freed five, who were old women,” De la Espriella told a news conference.

The international airport of the colonial-era Caribbean city, the jewel in Colombia’s tourism crown, briefly suspended landings.

Local media reported that the gunmen were demanding nearly $2 million, two armored cars and safe passage to the city of Barranquilla, 130 kilometers (80 miles) to the northeast, on the Caribbean coast.

The standoff added to tension in Colombia as it reels from the massive car bombing overnight in the central city of Villavicencio that left 25 people wounded and destroyed many buildings.

De la Espriella blamed the attack on a breakaway faction of the defunct guerrilla group FARC.

World.title: Lulu offers massive savings in ‘Super Friday’ campaign
World.content:
LuLu Hypermarket Saudi Arabia has announced the return of Lulu Super Friday, featuring massive savings of up to 70 percent across all categories — including tech, electronics and grocery. Promotions continue until Dec. 1 across all outlets nationwide.



The LuLu Super Friday campaign was officially inaugurated in Riyadh by Chief Guest Lipeng (Jerry), channel director, Huawei Saudi Arabia. The launch ceremony took place in the presence of Mohammed Haris, director — LuLu Hypermarkets Saudi Arabia, alongside members of the LuLumanagement team and representatives from leading partner brands.



This year’s LuLu Super Friday brings together incredible discounts across a wide range of categories from grocery essentials and home furnishings to cutting-edge electronics, mobiles, computers, fashion, household items and products for infants and kids. Shoppers can also explore promotions on fashion — including LuLu’s homegrown brand Reo Fashion, ethnic wear, footwear, ladies’ bags, and baby accessories. Whether customers are upgrading their gadgets, refreshing their homes or stocking up on style and essentials, they will find offers across the stores to suit every need and budget.



For those who prefer to shop on the go, LuLu Super Friday offers are available online too. For the first time in the Kingdom, LuLu has introduced home delivery for gadgets within minutes via the LuLu Minutes online platform as part of the Super Friday offers, making it quick and easy for customers to get their favorite tech delivered instantly. Beyond the LuLu app, customers can also conveniently order their Super Friday essentials through delivery partners including Locate, Noon, HungerStation and Trendyol. All gadgets and category items featured in the Super Friday promotions will be available with up to 70 percent off across both online and offline channels.



Shoppers looking to upgrade their eyewear can enjoy up to 60 percent off on spectacles, sunglasses, contact lenses and other optical items — including major international brands. Additionally, a flat 50 percent discount is available on LuLu Exclusive Styles campaign.



Shoppers can take advantage of discounts of up to 70 percent across major tech and home electrical categories, featuring incredible deals on dishwashers, iron boxes, “buy 1 get 1 free” offers on selected consumer electronics products and accessories, boAt products, LED TVs, soundbars, party speakers, TWS earbuds, headphones, personal care items from Philips, Wahl and Beurer, security and action cameras, healthcare products and exclusive offers on smartphones such as the Motorola Fold.



While customers normally have the option of four installment payments with Tabby and Tamara, the Super Friday promotion expands this flexibility to allow payments to be completed over six convenient installments. This extended six-installment facility is available on a minimum purchase of SR2,000 ($533) across both online and offline purchases.



Haris said: “LuLu Super Friday has become a much-loved occasion for families across the Kingdom and we are delighted to bring it back this year with up to 70 percent savings across all categories. Our aim is to give our customers real value on the products they need and love, backed by the quality and service they trust from LuLu.”



To maximize value during the LuLu Super Friday shopping celebration, zero-percent installment plans are available with participating banks, including Riyad Bank, Arab National Bank, Saudi National Bank, SAB, Emirates NBD and Alrajhi Bank. Major banks are also offering credit card promotions and cashback rewards at checkout.

World.title: Quinones and Reijnders excel as Al-Qadsiah brush aside Shabab Al-Ahli
World.content:
RIYADH: After five matches, Al-Qadsiah remain one of two teams in the 2026/27 AFC Champions League Elite to maintain an undefeated record. Draws against Pakhtakor and Al-Sadd may have stalled their start to the competition, but the Eastern Province club have bounced back in stellar fashion, following up their 5-0 thrashing of Al-Gharafa with a 5-1 demolition of Shabab Al-Ahli.

At the heart of Al-Qadsiah’s dominance is Julian Quinones. The Mexican scored his second consecutive brace in the competition to put his tally at six goals in five games, with his overall total for the club since his arrival in 2024 now at 74 goals in 85 games.

His goalscoring exploits have led Al-Qadsiah to challenge the very best in the Saudi Pro League, and with a certain Tijjani Reijnders roaming in behind and scoring goals of his own, Brendan Rodgers’ side are looking to send the same message to continental opposition.

It took just 13 minutes for Quinones to complete his brace against Shabab Al-Ahli. As early as the third minute, he received a pass from Musab Al-Juwayr in the heart of the pitch and unleashed a shot from nearly 35 yards out to break the deadlock, with opposition goalkeeper Hamad Al-Meqbaali fumbling the save for Al-Qadsiah to burst into the lead.

Ten minutes later, Reijnders found himself in front of goal, but spotted Quinones unmarked on the edge of the six-yard box — releasing him for a crisp finish into the bottom corner.

Reijnders grabbed his first goal of the night with a shot from outside the 18-yard box at the hour mark to extend Al-Qadsiah’s lead to three, before Mateusao pulled one back for Shabab Al-Ahli in the 71st minute.

Six minutes later, it was Reijnders again — assisted by Al-Juwayr, again — to make it 4-1 for Al-Qadsiah. Al-Juwayr provided a fourth assist in the 86th minute, when he released Abdullah Al-Salem on goal with a through ball from deep to secure the 5-1 victory for the visitors.

Al-Qadsiah now sit second on 11 points, two behind table-toppers Al-Ain, and remain the only Saudi side yet to taste defeat in the competition. That record will face a major test further down the line, when the two meet on Matchday 7 in February with top spot in the West League stage within reach. Before that, Qatar's Al-Shamal, who have defeated Al-Hilal and Al-Ahli and drawn with Al-Ittihad, await on Dec. 7.

World.title: Bayern score ‘own goal’ as Musiala firestorm builds
World.content:
MUNICH: Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala.

Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round.

While Lille are languishing in 35th spot, last season’s semifinalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders.

Jamal Musiala having fun with his teammates in today's training [🎥 @ransport] https://t.co/3nNnkgZBCs — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) November 24, 2026

Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern’s bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February.

But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week’s match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut.

That the club decided to kick-start the furor a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed.

- ‘Own goal’ -

In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures,” having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season.

After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition — and should consider taking a pay cut.

“If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany.

Rummenigge’s statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen.

On Sunday, player union FIFPRO slammed Bayern, accusing the club of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut.

“A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement.

FIFPRO’s German counterparts VDV joined the chorus on Monday, saying the comments would “leave a lasting impression” on Musiala and on the club in general.

“I believe those in charge have scored a real ‘own goal’ here,” VDV president Carsten Ramelow said in a statement.

World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner Lothar Matthaeus, who has never been afraid to butt heads with Hoeness and the Bayern brass, said the club should provide Musiala with “every bit of support.”

“Right now, everything is being placed on Musiala’s shoulders,” Matthaeus told RTL.

“Perhaps all parties can sit down and talk later at a more opportune moment,” he added.

- An opportunity for Musiala -

For their part, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany and powerful sporting director Max Eberl have thrown their support behind Musiala publicly.

Kompany, who himself returned on Friday from a month out after being hospitalized with meningeal irritation in October, backed Musiala.

“The coach must be the one to believe in the player. And if we manage to bring him back, then everyone wins: the club, the fans — and all of German football.”

Eberl said on Friday he was confident Musiala would return to his best form if given the chance.

Bayern’s injury crisis has provided Musiala with an opportunity to illustrate his importance to the club by starring in the coming months.

Besides Kane, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer will miss Wednesday’s match.

Michael Olise and Luis Diaz are also injury doubts, meaning the only recognized fit forward is 18-year-old winger Lennart Karl.

Musiala has not addressed the controversy directly, but gave an insight into how he shuts out pressure and critique at a fan event this weekend.

Asked by a fan how he handled the weight of expectation, Musiala said he was still in the process of finding the right approach.

“I’m still learning... Too much pressure isn’t good, but a hunger for victory is important,” Musiala said.

“Finding that balance is a very important part of life.”

World.title: Doughty to Asharq Al-Awsat: Houthi escalation prompted broad punitive measures
World.content:
LONDON: British Minister of State for the Middle East Stephen Doughty stressed that the sanctions imposed by his country on Tuesday against the Houthi group are a "very significant step" in confronting the group's escalation of attacks inside Yemen and against neighboring countries.

He expressed confidence in the effectiveness of the new measures, without disclosing whether London is considering designating the Houthis as a terrorist organization.

In remarks to Asharq Al-Awsat, Doughty revealed close cooperation between Britain and the Yemeni Coast Guard to intercept illicit arms shipments to the Houthis as part of efforts to safeguard international navigation.

He also condemned Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, confirming that Britain is providing defensive military support to Riyadh, including air defense, aerial refueling, and Typhoon fighter jet support.

The minister described the Iranian threats facing the United Kingdom as "wide-ranging," calling on Tehran to halt its destabilizing activities inside and outside the region.

Broad sanctions package

The British government announced on Tuesday sanctions on the Houthi group, including an asset freeze, as well as sanctions targeting four of its officials over their involvement in serious human rights violations, comprising asset freezes and travel bans to the United Kingdom.

The British Foreign Office said the decision stemmed from the Houthis' escalation of fighting inside Yemen, their targeting of civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, and their disruption of international shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, which has disrupted global supply chains and added to cost-of-living pressures in the United Kingdom.

Amid the Houthis' continued escalation of attacks despite previous punitive measures, Doughty stressed that what sets the new package apart is that it targets the group in its entirety.

This is an important announcement that comes in response to the reckless escalation and aggression carried out by the Houthis, not only inside Yemen and against the Yemeni people, but also against neighboring countries in the region, including Saudi Arabia, he said.

This is completely unacceptable. There is immense humanitarian harm inside Yemen, hundreds of thousands of people are fleeing their homes, and there are horrific reports of human rights abuses and atrocities being committed. That is why the UK acted, he stressed.

Doughty noted that the sanctions also targeted four senior Houthi officials implicated in human rights violations and implementing these policies, adding that the new measures as a "very important step forward" and a direct response to the Houthis' actions.

Asked whether the British government is considering blacklisting the Houthi group and designating it as a terrorist organization, following the lead of the US, he replied that listing the Houthi group in its entirety on the sanctions list represents a very significant step.

It takes effect immediately, and it will have the impact London is seeking to achieve, he stated.

He likewise did not specify whether Britain intends to take additional measures to target the military and financial support Iran provides to the Houthis.

He noted that the number of British sanctions imposed on Iran now runs into the hundreds, and that London enacted a series of measures on September 8 against Iran and its proxy groups, including Lebanon's Hezbollah.

Red Sea maritime security

Within the framework of British efforts to protect international navigation in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, Doughty confirmed that his country is cooperating closely with the Yemeni Coast Guard to intercept illicit weapons supplies to the Houthis.

The Houthi actions against freedom of navigation and their threats to shipping are completely unacceptable. Maritime security and freedom of navigation must be respected, he said, pointing to a series of measures to bolster maritime security in the region.

These efforts are not limited to cooperation with Yemeni authorities. Doughty noted that London is working with a range of regional partners, while underlining the need to work toward ending the conflict in Yemen.

Ultimately, diplomatic pathways to de-escalate, ensuring freedom of navigation, but also, fundamentally, ending the conflict in Yemen are needed. This conflict is having devastating effects on hundreds of thousands of Yemenis and is destabilizing the region, he said.

He stressed that attacks targeting civilians and infrastructure in neighboring countries, such as the strikes that hit Saudi airports, are "completely unacceptable."

Military support for Saudi Arabia

Doughty condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, stressing that the UK has been supporting the Kingdom for weeks through a range of measures, including air defense, aerial refueling, as well as support with Typhoon aircraft.

This is extremely important as part of the defensive role the UK is playing to support its close partner and friend, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, he stressed, adding that his country will listen carefully to any further requests it may put forward.

The UK and Saudi Arabia are working very closely together, he remarked.

Recalling his recent visit to Riyadh, he said what the Kingdom was subjected to is "completely unacceptable," citing attacks on its airports, and the killing and injury of innocent civilians.

He demanded that the Houthis cease these actions immediately.

Prospects of renewed war with Iran

At a time when world capitals are monitoring indicators regarding a potential resumption of military confrontation between the United States and Iran in the coming months, Doughty stressed London's commitment to the diplomatic track, pointing to its close cooperation with regional partners and its support for talks mediated by Oman, as well as efforts by Qatar and others.

Doughty said London wants to reach a negotiated diplomatic solution that allows the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, which is vital for the global economy, the British economy, and the economies of the region.

He underlined the importance of defending the principles of maritime security and freedom of navigation.

The minister, who assumed office four months ago, also affirmed the United Kingdom's readiness to defend its partners and interests. "When our partners and allies, as well as British interests, are threatened, we will of course defend our partners and our interests," he said.

Doughty reiterated his country's rejection of Iran acquiring a nuclear weapon.

Iran cannot be allowed to develop a nuclear weapon. It must stop its attacks on its neighbors and halt its destabilizing activities in the region and beyond, he urged.

He underscored the importance of diplomacy, and that has been conveyed directly to Tehran. The UK will continue to work with its regional partners to reach a diplomatic solution.

Iran's ‘wide-ranging’ threats

British concerns over Iran's activities are not confined to the Middle East. Following European Union accusations that Tehran was behind cyberattacks targeting cooling systems in several European countries days ago, Doughty described the threats Iran poses to the United Kingdom as "wide-ranging," stressing the need for them to stop.

He pointed to the varied nature of these threats, ranging from those targeting military bases and cyberattacks to the targeting of individuals and communities, recalling that the British government has previously spoken publicly about several of these issues.

Doughty expressed his country's full solidarity with France and other nations, condemning any attempts at cyber interference targeting the UK's partners and allies, and urging Iran to cease these activities immediately.

While declining to go into detail regarding British defensive capabilities, he underlined London's awareness of the hybrid threats it faces from various actors, whether Russia, Iran, or others.

"We will defend our infrastructure and our citizens," he said.

World.title: Iraqi security seizes two drone launchers in Maysan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security forces seized on Tuesday two drone launchers and drone engine components hidden in an agricultural area in the southeastern province of Maysan.

The operation was announced by Iraq’s Security Media Cell and carried out by a specialized intelligence and technical team supervised by the director of Maysan Intelligence and Counterterrorism.

Following intelligence reports, security forces deployed to cordon off and search the farmland, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Alongside the two concealed launch platforms, authorities recovered scattered remnants and components of a drone engine.

Authorities have seized the equipment and initiated legal and technical procedures. Officials have not yet identified who placed the launchers or confirmed whether they had been used in previous attacks.

After a drone attack targeted a pipeline in Saudi Arabia in September, which Riyadh and Baghdad said was launched from Iraqi territory, Iraqi security forces have discovered drone launchers near the border with Iran.

World.title: Iraqi political blocs name nominees to replace Communications and Transport Ministers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Political factions within Iraq’s Coordination Framework have finalized their nominees to replace key cabinet members in an upcoming ministerial reshuffle led by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, including the portfolios of Communications, Transport, and Oil, according to a coalition source speaking on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

The source disclosed that the Islamic Supreme Council of Iraq (ISCI), headed by Humam Hamoudi, has put forward several candidates—prominently Ahmed Abdul-Jabbar and former Health Minister Saleh Al-Hasnawi—to assume the Ministry of Communications in place of incumbent Minister Mustafa Jabbar Sanad.

Meanwhile, the Badr Organization, led by Hadi Al-Amiri, has selected Mohammed Al-Zubaidi as its nominee for the Ministry of Transport to succeed current Minister Wahab Al-Hassani.

The nominations follow revelations by a government source on Monday, November 23, confirming a political and executive agreement to carry out a phased cabinet reshuffle immediately after Parliament settles the federal general budget bill. Driven by formal performance evaluations and consultations with nominating blocs, the first phase is expected to target three portfolios for distinct reasons:

Ministry of Transport: The planned replacement of Minister Wahab Al-Hassani is attributed to health reasons.

Ministry of Oil: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi is weighing the dismissal of Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi due to operational shortcomings across multiple files and recent revelations of crude oil theft and smuggling networks across several Iraqi cities. Alongside naming new ministers, the government is considering merging the Ministries of Oil and Electricity into a unified “Ministry of Energy”, potentially placing both portfolios under the current Electricity Minister.

Ministry of Communications: Coalition sources confirmed the move to replace Mustafa Sanad, though specific official grounds for the change have not yet been detailed.

The impending shakeup comes roughly six months after the Council of Representatives granted confidence to Al-Zaidi’s cabinet on May 14, 2026, and just over a month after the government completed its 25-ministry lineup on October 15.

World.title: Baghdad to take over border crossings in Iraqi Kurdistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered federal authorities on Tuesday to take control of all border crossings in Iraqi Kurdistan and directed the Oil Ministry to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salah al-Din, and Nineveh provinces as part of a crackdown on oil smuggling.

The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) was instructed to approve crude oil and petroleum product exports only through the federal Oil Ministry.

Baghdad also announced plans to monitor oilfields with cameras and deploy Oil Ministry personnel at checkpoints leading into the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

Al-Zaidi directed the federal border crossings authority to assume control of all crossings in the Kurdistan region of Iraq. He also instructed the Border Forces Command to close unofficial international border crossings and ordered the shutdown of seasonal roads and unpaved routes connecting the four provinces and Iraqi Kurdistan.

The prime minister removed the head of the border crossings authority, suspended the director general of the state-owned North Oil Company and his deputies pending investigation, and dismissed several security officials in Kirkuk.

The directives followed an investigation into smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company and a wider campaign against illicit oil networks—including alleged smuggling in Jurf al-Sakhar linked to the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah group, which denied the accusation.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Egyptian businessmen in Cairo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi affirmed on Monday that Iraq has a promising investment environment and opportunities in several sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting with a group of Egyptian businessmen in the Egyptian capital, Cairo, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The meeting is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to strengthen the economic partnership between the two countries and expand investment cooperation.

The Iraqi government is striving to increase the presence of the private sector, recognizing its critical role in bolstering the country’s economy and attaining progress, according to al-Zaidi.

The Iraqi prime minister noted that the Iraqi investment law offers investors benefits and protection, including tax and customs exemptions.

Al-Zaidi listened to the views, recommendations, and suggestions put forward by Egyptian business leaders to increase investments in Iraq.

Egyptian business leaders conveyed their gratitude for the incentives that Iraq provides to investors as well as their interest in the available investment prospects.

World.title: Iraq, Egypt sign several memoranda of understanding
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly oversaw a ceremony held to sign 10 bilateral cooperation documents and memoranda of understanding (MoUs) on Monday in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital.

The ceremony followed the fourth session of the Egyptian-Iraqi Joint Higher Committee, co-chaired by both leaders during Al-Zaidi’s first official visit to Egypt since taking office.

The two countries signed a treaty to prevent tax evasion and eliminate double taxation on income and capital.

Health and trade officials finalized a MoU covering medical supplies and pharmaceuticals.

Regulators inked deals for radio and TV broadcasting cooperation alongside nuclear and radiation oversight.

Additionally, both sides signed five other documents establishing joint programs in fisheries, scientific research, national planning, youth, and sports.

Prior to the ceremony, al-Zaidi met President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to expand economic cooperation and coordinate diplomatic efforts on regional security.

World.title: US exports to Iraq reach $727 million in first nine months of 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – U.S. exports to Iraq surpassed $700 million during the first nine months of 2026, reaching a cumulative total of $727 million across the first three quarters of the year, according to U.S. Census Bureau figures published via the International Trade Centre’s (ITC) Trade Map platform on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

Quarterly data shows that bilateral shipments held steady through the first half of the year before gaining momentum in the third quarter:

Q1 2026: $238 million

Q2 2026: $238 million

Q3 2026: $251 million

Nine-Month Cumulative Total: $727 million

The $727 million export volume spans a diverse range of industrial, energy, agricultural, and healthcare goods shipped to the Iraqi market.

Primary export categories include pharmaceuticals and medical products, heavy industrial equipment, gas turbines, machinery and appliances, petroleum derivatives, and agricultural staples such as rice.

World.title: US dollar holds near 169,500 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar hovered just shy of the 170,000-dinar threshold across major domestic parallel markets on Tuesday morning, November 24, 2026, with purchasing bids settling near 169,000 IQD per $100 in key commercial hubs.

According to morning monitoring figures, physical banknote rates opened across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra with minor regional variations.

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,500 IQD against buying offers of 169,000 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks matched Baghdad’s 169,500 IQD retail selling quote while offering slightly lower purchasing bids at 168,750 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices recorded marginally softer retail selling rates at 169,250 IQD alongside buying offers of 168,750 IQD per $100.

Overall, parallel cash rates continue to trade at a spread of 17,250 to 17,500 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official cash rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Baghdad welcomes Arab leaders as Al Zaidi wraps up Cairo talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi government formally opened Baghdad’s doors to Arab heads of state and representatives of pan-Arab organizations on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, just hours after Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi concluded his visit to the League of Arab States headquarters in Cairo.

In statements to the official newspaper, Government Spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi revealed that Al-Zaidi’s talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi focused heavily on coordinating bilateral efforts to ward off economic risks and mitigate the fallout inflicted on regional economies by the ongoing war.

Al-Aboudi also confirmed that the Prime Minister extended a direct invitation to the Grand Imam of Al-Azhar to visit Baghdad to foster deeper institutional communication and promote a moderate religious discourse between Iraq and Egypt.

Characterizing Cairo as a pivotal stop in Baghdad’s broader foreign policy of balanced international engagement, Al-Aboudi noted that Al-Zaidi’s diplomatic outreach has previously spanned Washington, Paris, Berlin, and several Arab and Gulf capitals.

He emphasized that Iraq’s diplomacy prioritizes Arab economic integration and the activation of joint Arab action mechanisms to safeguard regional sovereignty and resources.

Addressing Al-Zaidi’s appearance at the Arab League headquarters and meetings with member-state representatives, Al-Aboudi stated that Iraq’s historical founding role in the institution motivated the visit, underscoring Baghdad’s determination to strengthen its Arab presence and help confront shared regional threats.

Welcoming Arab leaders, prominent figures, and active regional organizations to convene in Baghdad, Al-Aboudi concluded that the Cairo summit reflects Iraq’s commitment to consolidating Arab ties and expanding joint cooperation in support of regional stability.

World.title: 'Hold serious discussions with us': Akhilesh's public message to Congress on UP seat-sharing

NEW DELHI:

chief

on Tuesday called for a consensus-based seat-sharing deal with

for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying both parties must prioritise winnability over the number of seats.

In a public message, the SP chief asked Congress to hold "serious discussions" on the seat-sharing deal.

In a lengthy social media post on X, Akhilesh said the INDIA bloc had a "historic opportunity" to defeat the "communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies" once and for all.

"This time, we have a historic opportunity to come together as the two secular parties and defeat the communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies once and for all, saving the country from falling into the wrong hands and being ruined," the SP chief said.



"We want you and us to hold serious discussions, taking public expectations and realities into account, to ensure our âallianceâ wins in most constituencies. Only victory will make the division of seats respectable, because only the seats we win will bring us respect," he added.

He also urged Congress to identify and send potential seats in addition to the 26 seats discussed during the seat-sharing meeting.





"Therefore, in addition to the 26 seats from the priority list your team provided that we have discussed today, please identify and send us all other potential seats. Then we will sit down together and assess which seats, and which candidates for those seats, are in a winning position. Based on our assessment and the mathematical equation for victory, we may also be able to tell the Congress about many winnable seats it has not even considered for some reason," Akhilesh said.

"Our aim is that when the senior leaders meet, the discussion should be about candidates for the âINDIA allianceâ in every constituency, not Congress or SP candidates. And the best and most positive outcome would be for us to present our candidates as âPDA candidatesâ," he added.

World.title: Indians among 13 killed in UAE bus-truck crash, 14 injured
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

At least 13 people were killed and 14 injured after a bus collided with a truck in the UAE's Ras Al Khaimah on Tuesday. Indian nationals were among those killed, the Indian consulate in Dubai confirmed.The bus was carrying 41 passengers when it crashed into a truck parked on the roadside following a technical breakdown, according to local authorities. The accident took place on Al Watan Road in the early hours of Tuesday. World.title: 'Customary practices, age-old traditions': Thiruparankundram temple clarifies why deepam was lit at usual spot
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple on Tuesday issued a clarification after the

was lit at the usual spot instead of the 'Deepathoon', despite the

's order.

In a statement, the temple's deputy commissioner and executive officer said that the Deepam is traditionally lit at the Deepa Mandapam located near the Uchipillaiyar Temple atop the hill.

"Specifically, as per the long-standing customary practice of the temple, the Karthigai Maha Deepam is traditionally lit at the Deepa Mandapam located near the Uchipillaiyar Temple atop the hill, directly above the sanctum of the presiding deity (Moolavar)," the statement read.

"Such long-standing and continuous religious practices (age-old continued practices), along with customs and rituals and Agama rules, are considered distinctive religious traditions and integral aspects of the temple's identity," it added.



The statement said that the temple's board of trustees had unanimously passed a resolution stating that its age-old traditions and customary practices must be protected.

"Therefore, the temple's board of trustees has unanimously passed a resolution stating that the age-old traditions, customary practices, Agama regulations and established religious practices followed at the temple must be protected. Based on historical records establishing the continuity and religious significance of these practices, Agama-related documents and the opinions of temple functionaries (Sthanikars), the Board resolved to light the Karthigai Maha Deepam this year as well at the customary location," the statement read.





"It also resolved that the temple's traditions and customary practices should be brought to the attention of the court," it added.

"In accordance with the above resolution passed by the Board of Trustees, the Karthigai Maha Deepam of the temple was lit today, November 24, 2026, at around 6.00 pm, at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple atop the hill, directly above the sanctum of the presiding deity (Moolavar)," it added.

This comes after a scuffle broke out between members of Hindu outfits and police officials at Thiruparankundram after the Karthigai Deepam was lit at the usual spot instead of the âDeepathoonâ, despite the Supreme Court's order.

Tamil Nadu law minister R Nirmal Kumar said in a brief statement that the Deepam was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, close to the Uchipillaiyar Temple, which is right above the shrine of the presiding deity, Lord Subramania Swamy.

The ceremony was held amid heightened security, with police detaining several people citing apprehensions of disorder based on intelligence inputs and their past conduct.

The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.

The Subramaniya Swamy Temple is situated at the foothills, while a Dargah is located near the hilltop.

A Shiva temple is also situated on the hill.

Hindu groups maintain that the stone pillar where they seek to light the lamp belongs to the temple, citing civil court decisions dating back about a century.

Dargah officials and Muslim organisations have opposed the proposed lighting, citing its proximity to their place of worship. The dispute involves questions of ownership and the rights of the respective parties.

On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah.

The apex court specified that the ceremony must be conducted by an authorised team and barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.

World.title: Video of bulldozer near sacred Sheshnag lake triggers row in Kashmir - here's what happened
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A video showing a JCB operating near Sheshnag Lake along the

route in

has triggered a political row, with leaders and environmentalists questioning the construction activity in the fragile glacial zone.

The controversy has intensified after political leaders raised concerns over the environmental impact and religious significance of the landscape, while an online petition seeking a halt to construction near Kashmir's alpine lakes gained traction.

The Border Roads Organisation (BRO), however, said post-Amarnath Yatra works were being carried out in compliance with all applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards.



What triggered the row

A video showing an excavator operating near Sheshnag Lake, a high-altitude glacial lake in south Kashmir's Anantnag district, has drawn criticism from political parties, religious leaders and environmentalists, who have demanded that the activity be stopped.

The deployment of heavy machinery near the lake has raised concerns about potential ecological damage to the fragile alpine landscape along the Amarnath cave route.





The controversy has also brought the area's religious significance into focus, with leaders questioning whether construction activity could affect the landscape associated with the annual pilgrimage.

The BRO on Monday said post-Amarnath Yatra works were being carried out in compliance with all applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards.

Political leaders raise environmental, religious concerns

PDP president Mehbooba Mufti expressed alarm over reports of excavation near Sheshnag, saying the use of heavy machinery in the ecologically fragile zone could threaten both the environment and the pilgrimage's religious sanctity.

Mehbooba, accompanied by party MLAs Waheed Para and Syed Muntazir Mehndi, set out towards Sheshnag on Tuesday morning along the Amarnath Yatra route. The PDP leaders attempted to trek from Chandanwari towards Sheshnag but were stopped by police.

The former chief minister said forests, mountains and glaciers, including Sheshnag, play a role in the formation of the naturally occurring ice lingam at the Amarnath cave during the pilgrimage.

"My worst fears were confirmed today when police stopped me from proceeding towards Sheshnag. The questions surrounding construction in this fragile glacial ecosystem are only growing louder. What is being concealed today could become a man made disaster tomorrow. The Amarnath Cave, Yatra and surrounding mountains must be protected as one ecological whole," she said in a post on X.

JKPDP spokesperson Mohit Bhan also criticised the construction activity, pointing to the religious significance of Sheshnag and the need to protect its ecological surroundings.

"We have seen Joshimath, Kedarnath, Mata Vaishno Devi, and the devastation caused by cloudbursts in the Amarnath region. Yet, we refuse to learn. Sacred destinations are being reduced to commercial and picnic spots at the cost of fragile ecosystems. The conversation must go beyond Amarnath and Sheshnag. Shrinking Dal and Wular, rampant encroachments, conversion of agricultural land and felling of mighty Chinars are all part of the same crisis.

Our forefathers protected this shared natural and spiritual inheritance for centuries. We must reclaim that responsibility. Heads must roll, accountability must follow and preservation must take precedence over reckless development," Bhan.

Kashmir's chief cleric, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, also raised concerns over the activity and urged people to oppose what he described as ecological destruction in fragile areas.

"We all have to collectively raise our voice to stop the mindless destruction of our ecology at its most fragile places," he said.

Mirwaiz questioned chief minister Omar Abdullah's silence on the issue and urged authorities to intervene. He also cited retreating glaciers and recent glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal to underline the vulnerability of the Himalayan region.

"With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm.

Kashmir has always warmly welcomed Amarnath Yatra pilgrims, and improving facilities for them has never been an issue. But not at the cost of our fragile ecosystem. Those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such 'developmental projects'," he said on X.

He emphasised that mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection, "not plunder", for present and future generations.

"So this must be immediately stopped," he said.

Congress seeks details of project, approvals

Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra questioned the deployment of a JCB excavator near Sheshnag Lake and sought clarity on the purpose of the work and the permissions granted by various departments.

"I was surprised to see how the JCB reached Sheshnag. From what we could make out in the video, it appeared to be digging soil and dumping it on the left-hand side, towards the lake," PTI quoted Karra as saying.

He said reports suggesting that the agency concerned had obtained no-objection certificates (NOCs) from various departments made it important to establish the purpose of the activity.

"But for which project was it taken there? Which department is involved? Which department granted the NOC, and which other departments gave their approval? It is very important to obtain information about this," he said.

The Congress leader urged the government to clarify its position and make details of the project and approvals public.

Petition seeks halt to construction near alpine lakes

An online petition on Change.org titled "Stop construction around Kashmir's alpine lakes", started by Zarqua Banday, has garnered nearly 1,600 signatures so far. It calls for a halt to construction activity near ecologically fragile alpine lakes and urges authorities to engage with environmental and community groups to develop a sustainable way forward.

The petition argues that road construction in untouched areas could damage fragile ecosystems and increase pollution, habitat destruction and tourist pressure.

"This isn't progress; it's a threat to our environment," it said.

The petition also called for sustainable tourism initiatives, including guided trekking, limited access permits and eco-friendly accommodation, instead of road construction in fragile areas.

It cited the Swiss Alps as an example of regions that have adopted strategies to manage tourism while protecting the environment.

The petition said people in Kashmir are not opposed to development but want it to respect the region's land, traditions and ecological balance.

BJP accuses critics of politicising issue

The Jammu and Kashmir BJP on Tuesday accused critics of selective environmental activism and double standards, saying it would oppose attempts to communalise development, undermine the Amarnath pilgrimage or disturb peace in the Valley.

J&K BJP spokesperson and former MLC Girdhari Lal Raina said the controversy was being used for political purposes.

"What is being projected as an environmental issue increasingly appears to be an attempt to manufacture controversy, disturb the peaceful atmosphere and exploit religious sentiments for narrow political gains," he said.

Without naming any party or individual, Raina accused political parties and leaders of attempting to revive the Amarnath land controversy and communalise the issue.

World.title: ‘26 seats’ to start with: Akhilesh strikes a poetic note on SP-Congress alliance talks
World.content:
chief

on Tuesday wove a poetic verse around the ongoing seat-sharing talks with the

for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, saying the process had begun with an offer of 26 seats and would move forward through mutual understanding.

"Jeetne waali pehli â26 seatonâ se hui hai shuruaat, mil-julkar samajhdaari se aur aage badhegi baat" (The winning start has been made with the first â26 seatsâ; working together wisely, things will move forward), Akhilesh said in the verse shared amid negotiations between the two INDIA bloc allies.

The alliance between the two parties remains intact, and the seat-sharing arrangement is expected to be finalised in the coming meetings, Congress sources said on Tuesday.



The next round of talks is likely to take place on November 27.

Earlier in the day, Akhilesh said the primary objective of an alliance was to win elections and that discussions were under way to assess the winnability of candidates in each constituency.

Speaking to reporters in Lucknow, the SP chief said senior leaders entrusted with the negotiations were actively engaged in the process, but it was too early to disclose details of the proposed arrangement.





"Regarding the ongoing discussions, our party's senior leaders, along with those entrusted by the party to handle these talks, are currently engaged in the process. What exactly is being discussed? How many seats are being agreed upon, and how many could the other party potentially win? These matters are under consideration, so it is difficult to say anything definitive right now. Alliances are formed with the sole objective of winning; the purpose of an alliance is victory," Akhilesh said.

Emphasising the need to counter Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), he said the SP was prepared to make adjustments to secure an electoral victory.

"The Samajwadi Party is committed to making adjustments and accommodations because the battle ahead is significant. When the goal is to win, and we must win, especially against a political 'machine' like the BJP, we have to prepare accordingly and make the right decisions," he said.

Akhilesh also raised questions about the electoral process and the functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI).

"Constitutional bodies have a duty to act fairly, yet questions are being raised about this very body. It is now being suggested that the BJP is planning to add approximately 3 crore votes. Furthermore, regarding the warehouses where EVMs are stored, who are the engineers tasked by the ECI with maintaining these machines? We are told that the machines are being 'serviced,' but no one knows who these engineers actually are," he said.

SP MP Rajeev Rai confirmed that the party had offered 26 seats to the Congress ahead of the second round of negotiations.

"We will hold discussions regarding the number of seats. We have offered them 26 seats," Rai said.

SP Rajya Sabha MP Ram Gopal Yadav also said the proposal had been conveyed to the Congress during Monday's meeting and that discussions would continue.

"Whatever had to be said in the meeting, we said yesterday. We have offered them our 26 seats, and today we are going to hold talks again," he said.

Congress leaders also described the negotiations as positive. AICC in-charge for Uttar Pradesh Rajendra Pal Gautam expressed confidence that the seat-sharing arrangement would be finalised in the next two meetings.

"We are heading in the right direction. In the next two meetings, everything will be done. Discussions have been held on several seats. Discussions have been held on every single seat on the basis of data.

The discussions are heading in a positive direction. Both parties are going ahead with a positive mindset. 403 is a big number; discussions have been held on more than half of them. We will wind this up in the next two meetings.

Our alliance will be a done deal. We will make the announcement soon," Gautam said.

Congress Legislature Party leader in Uttar Pradesh Aradhana Misra 'Mona' also described the first round of talks as positive and said further discussions would be held before the alliance was formally announced.

"We discussed seats in the meeting. It was a positive discussion, and only one round of discussion has been concluded so far. The second round of discussion will be held soon, and if needed, we will come together again. The exercise will continue until we announce the alliance positively," she said.

World.title: ‘If I were Nirav Modi, I would get a red carpet’: Saurav Das attacks Centre over UK travel block
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener

on Tuesday accused the Centre of trying to suppress the youth-led movement by restricting its leaders' travel, curbing protests and censoring social media content, a day after he was stopped from travelling to the UK to attend an event at the University of Oxford.

Addressing a press conference, Saurav alleged that the government was raising questions about discrepancies in his passport after immigration authorities prevented him from travelling to London.

He claimed that the Centre, unable to find grounds to act against CJP leaders through agencies such as the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), was questioning their citizenship, Aadhaar cards and educational qualifications.



"They are now raising questions about discrepancies in my passport. They cannot find anything against any of their so-called leaders and since they cannot use UAPA, ED or CBI against us, they are resorting to such petty tactics. If I were

or Mehul Choksi, a red carpet would have been rolled out for me instead. As you all know, I was supposed to travel to London, but unfortunately, that could not happen because of this cowardly government," he said.





Taking a swipe at the government, Saurav said that had he been fugitive businessmen Nirav Modi, Vijay Mallya or Mehul Choksi, he would have received preferential treatment and been able to leave for London within hours.

"Had I been Nirav Modi, Vijay Mallya, or Mehul Bhai Choksi, what would have happened to me? I would have got a red carpet, I would have been taken to the airport through VIP security, I would have left for London in three-four hours," he said.

Saurav also claimed that Mallya had held a secret meeting with former finance minister Arun Jaitley in Parliament in 2018, during which he disclosed his plans to travel to London before leaving the country.

Oxford visit and planned engagements

Saurav said he and CJP legal head Ratna Singh had been invited to speak at the Oxford Union on December 1. The visit was also expected to include engagements with students at the London School of Economics, Cambridge University, Edinburgh University and Queen Mary University.

"The invitation from the Oxford Union was the primary reason for my visit. Ratna was also invited. Indian students studying there wanted to understand what the CJP movement is all about. I wanted to go there and share my perspective on how such a large-scale movement evolved into a non-violent movement. There is considerable interest among Gen Z communities in several countries around the world to understand this," he said.

Saurav said he had planned to speak about the movement's non-violent character and the principles of Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and B R Ambedkar.

"I would have talked about Gandhiji, Nehruji, Ambedkarji. I would have talked about the principles of Gandhiji, non-violence, peace, peaceful protest," he said.

He questioned why the government was afraid of the movement and said the visit would have provided an opportunity to explain how a large-scale campaign could remain peaceful.

"I want to ask, why is this government so afraid? I would have spoken about the principles and ideals of Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru. It would have been an opportunity for the world to learn how such a massive movement can remain non-violent and draw strength from the principles of peaceful resistance," Das added.

Saurav alleged that the government was also preventing CJP from putting forward its views within the country, both through protests and online platforms.

"We were stopped from going to Jantar Mantar, we were stopped from going to Ramlila Maidan, we were stopped from keeping our point online," he said.

He further alleged that Meta had deleted 60 lakh posts over the past few months and introduced filters that automatically remove content containing certain keywords.

Saurav also referred to the temporary deletion of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's Facebook account, which has since been restored.
