World.title: The OGs reunite: SAD gets 'bada bhai' tag in Punjab, but BJP has bigger ambitions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Two of Punjab's oldest political allies are back together, six years after a bitter parting over the contentious farm laws. The Bharatiya Janata Party (

) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (

) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027

, reviving a partnership that once governed the state for 15 years across three terms.

The reunion, announced on the Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, brings together parties whose relationship was famously described by former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal as "nau-maas da rishta", the bond between the nail and the flesh.

Prime Minister

Narendra Modi

welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first.

"Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," he said in a post on X, adding that the partnership, nurtured by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, LK Advani and Parkash Singh Badal, had "stood the test of time".



Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced the reunion alongside BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, called the Akali Dal the NDA's "oldest ally" and said PM Modi had described the development by saying the "NDA is now complete".

Shah also said SAD would retain its senior-partner status, adding that the "big brother" would get the chief minister's post. "Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats.





Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," the Union minister said at the joint press conference.

The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised.

The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring, including Sukhbir Badal's meeting with PM Modi in August and a shift in SAD's position on the Centre's delimitation proposal.

It also brings together two parties whose electoral fortunes have declined sharply since their separation.

However, Punjab is no longer the state in which the old alliance enjoyed its strongest run. AAP has emerged as the dominant force,

Congress

remains a significant contender, and the BJP and SAD have both undergone changes in their support bases and political strategies.

Why SAD-BJP patched up

The partnership actually predates the BJP. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, shared power with the Akalis in Punjab as far back as 1967 and 1969.

The modern alliance, however, was forged in 1996, when SAD's Moga Declaration pivoted from purely Panthic politics to a broader pitch of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat."

The partnership brought together the Akalis' predominantly rural Sikh support base and the BJP's largely urban Hindu constituency. It also helped both parties build a political coalition in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab.

The hot and cold relationship of SAD and BJP.

The alliance won 93 of 117 assembly seats in 1997, with SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18.

After losing power to Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 and retained power in 2012, winning 67 and 68 seats respectively.

ALSO READ:

But the emergence of AAP, coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, weakened the alliance. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three.

The final rupture came in September 2020, when SAD walked out of the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws.

Sukhbir Badal's wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister on September 17, and the Akali Dal formally ended its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP nine days later.

The laws were repealed in November 2021, but the political damage endured.

The alliance's decline is evident from its electoral record. In 2007, SAD won 48 seats and the BJP 19, taking their combined tally to 67.

They improved to 68 seats in 2012, with SAD winning 56 and the BJP 12. But the numbers fell sharply thereafter. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three. By the 2022 assembly elections, the two parties managed just five seats between them, with SAD winning three and the BJP two.

In 2022, SAD secured 18.38% of the vote and the BJP 6.60%, while AAP swept the election with 92 seats and a 42.01% vote share.

Their separate performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections provided another reason to reconsider the alliance.

The BJP failed to win any of Punjab's 13 seats despite securing 18.56% of the vote. SAD won one seat, Bathinda, with 13.42%.

ALSO READ:

Together, their vote shares added up to nearly 32%, compared with 26.30% for Congress and 26.02% for AAP.

The numbers make a case for pooling their support bases, although the combined vote share does not automatically translate into transferable votes or assembly seats.

For the BJP, the alliance offers access to SAD's traditional rural and Sikh support networks.

For the Akali Dal, it brings back a national ally and an opportunity to rebuild its electoral machinery, which is the BJP's strong suit.

Sukhbir Singh Badal described the reunion as more than an electoral arrangement.

"This is not just a political alliance. There is an emotional bond. As my late father used to say, Akali Dal-BJP is an inseparable, deeply bonded relationship," he said.

Six years later, a very different Punjab

The old partners are back again, but the state the BJP and SAD are returning to is markedly different from the one they left behind in 2020.

The 2027 assembly election will be the alliance's first major state-level electoral test without Parkash Singh Badal, the five-time CM who died in April 2023. A towering figure in the Akali Dal, he was also a key bridge between the SAD and the BJP. Though Sukhbir Badal was already leading the party before his father's death, he now has to rebuild the party's standing without his political stature and influence.

Another factor the alliance must keep in mind is that the farm issue has not disappeared.

The repeal of the three farm laws did not automatically undo the distrust they created. Farmers' demands, including a legal guarantee for minimum support price, remain unresolved, keeping the issue politically alive in an agrarian state like Punjab. The BJP-SAD alliance will have to reckon with that trust deficit, particularly in the rural Malwa belt, which is the largest and most populous region covering major farming districts like Bathinda, Mansa, Sangrur, Patiala, Ludhiana and Muktsar.

This is why the choice of Gurpurab for the reunion announcement is rich in symbolism. PM Modi had announced the repeal of the farm laws on the occasion in November 2021. The two parties have now chosen the same religious occasion to announce their political reconciliation. Whether that symbolism can translate into renewed trust among farmers is a different question.

Another thing that has changed is that the Akali Dal can no longer assume that it commands the entire Panthic vote.

In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, independent candidates Amritpal Singh and Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa won from Khadoor Sahib and Faridkot, respectively. Between them, they also led in 15 assembly segments.

ALSO READ:

This makes the party's return to its traditional Panthic space more difficult. The SAD has tried to reconnect with its core constituency through issues of Sikh identity and historical memory. The controversy surrounding 'Satluj', a film based on activist Jaswant Singh Khalra's work documenting alleged extrajudicial killings in Punjab, offered one such opportunity.

After the film was taken down from an OTT platform, Sukhbir Badal announced screenings across the state, saying young people should know about the events it depicts.

The bigger, bolder BJP

Six years on its own have transformed the BJP from a junior partner that contested just 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats into a more assertive player. Under the old arrangement, the SAD contested 94 assembly seats and the BJP 23, largely in urban constituencies.

For the Lok Sabha elections, the split was 10 seats for the Akalis and three for the BJP.

Its vote share in the 2024 Lok Sabha election rose to 18.56 per cent, up from 9.63 per cent in 2019. The BJP contested all 13 seats in 2024, compared with just three under the old seat-sharing arrangement in 2019. Though it won no seats, the saffron party's vote share was higher than the SAD's 13.42 per cent. In the 2022 assembly election, the BJP had polled 6.60 per cent and won two seats.

The party has also strengthened its ranks through a steady stream of defections. In April 2026, AAP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha led six other MPs into the BJP which included Sandeep Pathak, Ashok Mittal, Harbhajan Singh, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Rajinder Gupta and Swati Maliwal. Six of these seven were Rajya Sabha members from Punjab. The exits dealt a major blow to the AAP's parliamentary strength and brought into the BJP leaders who had been closely associated with the party's Punjab strategy.

Chadha and Pathak, in particular, had played key roles in the AAP's political and electoral planning.

The BJP has since moved to put these former AAP leaders to work against their old party. Chadha and Harbhajan Singh have been named to its Punjab manifesto committee, while Pathak, Mittal, Sahney and other former AAP MPs have been assigned roles in the party's chargesheet committee, which will prepare its case against the Bhagwant Mann government.

Earlier, in March 2024, AAP's then Jalandhar MP Sushil Kumar Rinku and Jalandhar West MLA Sheetal Angural had also joined the BJP. In November 2026, three more AAP legislators, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, crossed over. The BJP has also inducted senior Akali leaders, including Surinder Singh Chauhan and Jaswinderpal Sohal, as well as AAP functionaries from Moga led by spokesperson Navdeep Singh Sangha.

The BJP's recruitment drive has not been limited to the AAP and SAD. Its Punjab ranks also include former Congress leaders such as Sunil Jakhar, Manpreet Singh Badal, Ravneet Singh Bittu and Preneet Kaur.

That changes the terms of the reunion. The BJP returns with a larger vote share, a wider organisational footprint and experienced leaders. The SAD, meanwhile, needs the alliance to recover lost ground and reconnect with rural voters.

Amit Shah has announced that the BJP is okay with the junior-partner label in the alliance. It is, however, unlikely that the BJP will settle for the old seat-sharing formula.

Can the alliance unsettle AAP?

The immediate target of the alliance is the AAP government, which swept to power in 2022 with 92 seats and 42.01 per cent of the vote. Its vote share fell to 26.02 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when it won three seats, but it remains a formidable player.

The SAD-BJP reunion gives the opposition a potentially stronger combination of urban and rural networks. It could also help consolidate voters who want an alternative to the AAP government. The drug problem, in particular, is likely to be a central campaign issue.

At his press conference, Amit Shah listed three priorities for a future NDA government: eliminating drugs, eliminating corruption and strengthening nationalist forces.

He promised that Punjab would be "completely drug-free" by December 31, 2029. He also targeted Congress, recalling Rahul Gandhi's 2017 promise that drugs would be eliminated within one term and accusing the party of doing nothing when it was in power.

The attack gives the alliance a ready-made campaign plank. But it also puts the BJP and SAD on the spot, as both parties have been part of Punjab's political establishment for decades.

The voters, thus, will judge their record as well as their promises.

There is another complication. The Congress remains a strong third front and could split the anti-incumbency vote. Rural Sikh voters who continue to view the BJP through the lens of the farm agitation may also be reluctant to back the reunited partners. The AAP could benefit if opposition votes remain divided.

The BJP-SAD reunion also complicates the Congress's position.

With an established opposition pole, the contest for voters dissatisfied with the AAP government will now intensify. Amit Shah's attack on the Congress over its record on drugs made it clear that the alliance intends to take on both the ruling party and its principal rival.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Congress can still draw on its independent support base, but it will have to navigate a more crowded opposition space, as well as its own internal factional differences.

Six years after a split that left both allies on the margins, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal have chosen pragmatism over past grievances to challenge AAP and Congress. The 2027 election, however, will not be a simple replay of the coalition's past victories. And tough seat-sharing talks are yet to be held.

The OGs may be back together, but winning over a changed Punjab will require more than old chemistry.

World.title: ‘Sitting at the feet of the same BJP’: Bhagwant Mann attacks Sukhbir Badal over alliance
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister

on Tuesday criticised the newly announced alliance between Bharatiya Janata Party (

) and

(SAD) for the 2027 Assembly elections, accusing SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of aligning with the same party he had previously criticised over its handling of farmers' issues.

In a video statement shared by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Mann alleged that the Badal family had initially supported the three farm laws introduced by the Centre in 2020 but changed its stand after the farmers' protest gained momentum and widespread support.

Referring to the resignation of then Union Minister of Food Processing Industries Harsimrat Kaur Badal, Mann claimed the Akali Dal had realised that it would struggle to survive politically in Punjab if it continued to support the laws.



"The BJP and the Akali Dal have formed an alliance. I would like to remind you of what they say to each other, how these people try to make a fool of the public. They feel that people forget things after some time. At first, the entire Badal family kept speaking in favour of these 'black laws', saying, 'That's a very good law, a very good law. It is amazing; if it does amazing work, then with this, the agriculture of Punjab will become very prosperous.





' When the farmers' movement reached its peak and started getting support from all over the world, they realised this would be a mistake and that it would be difficult to survive politically in Punjab," he said.

"So, Harsimrat resigned and started speaking against those laws, claiming, 'The BJP is anti-farmer, the BJP is anti-farmer, we have sacrificed, the BJP is anti-farmer.' But by then, people understood that they were still in talks with each other and were separating from each other just to put on a show for the public," he added.

Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet in September 2020, before the Lok Sabha voted on the farm bills. Days after the Rajya Sabha cleared the final bill, Sukhbir Singh Badal announced the SAD's unanimous decision to withdraw from the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).

Mann also accused the BJP of neglecting Punjab's interests, citing the state's tableau at national events on Republic Day and Independence Day.

"The same BJP says that the tableau that comes out on January 26 or August 15 will not be Punjab's tableau in Delhi. We got this work done by fighting with them," he said.

Targeting

Sukhbir Badal

over his earlier criticism of the BJP, Mann alleged that the SAD president had accused the party of interfering in Sikh religious institutions with the help of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).

"The same BJP about which Sukhbir Badal used to say that Sikh organisations are being taken over by the BJP with the help of the RSS, that the BJP has captured the committee of Hazur Sahib in Maharashtra and the committee of Patna Sahib.

Today, sitting at the feet of that same BJP, you are making a political alliance," he said.

Appealing to people to support the AAP government, Mann said, "Aam Aadmi Party is your own party. There is a party living in your hearts. I will come at your call, wherever you call me. We will come and raise our voice in favour of Punjab."

BJP and SAD revive alliance after six-year break

Mann's remarks came after BJP and SAD announced on Tuesday that they would contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections together, reviving their alliance after a six-year break.

The two parties will jointly contest all 117 Assembly seats, with the SAD taking the lead in the arrangement.

"Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats. Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," Union Home Minister Amit Shah said at a joint press conference attended by BJP president Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal.

"Naturally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will play the role of the elder brother.

The Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will contest together. Both parties will jointly contest all 117 seats, while the Akali Dal will be in the role of the elder brother," Shah added.

The announcement, made on Gurpurab, marked the revival of ties between the two parties, which ended their partnership in 2020 after the SAD withdrew from the NDA over its opposition to the farm laws.

Under their previous seat-sharing arrangement, the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 Assembly seats, while the SAD fielded candidates in the remaining constituencies.

The two parties had jointly governed the state for 10 years before losing the 2017 Assembly elections, when the Congress returned to power under Captain Amarinder Singh.

In the 2022 Assembly elections, the AAP swept to power, while the BJP and SAD, which contested separately, were pushed to the margins.

Meanwhile, the Punjab BJP on Monday announced its 16-member state election committee for the 2027 Assembly polls, with state president Kewal Singh Dhillon heading the panel.

World.title: 1,420 police personnel deployed for first phase panchayat polls in Palnadu
World.content:
The Palnadu district police have deployed more than 1,420 personnel for the first phase of panchayat elections scheduled in seven mandals on November 26, as part of a three-phase polls to be held on November 26, 29 and December 2.

District Superintendent of Police Jagadeesh Adahalli told The Hindu that security arrangements have been made to ensure that voters exercised their franchise freely and without fear. The arrangements also cover the Narasaraopet municipal elections scheduled for November 26, and deployed nearly 150 police personnel for these urban elections.

The SP said forces had been deployed and security at election distribution centres and strong rooms reviewed. Police personnel had been instructed to remain alert and prevent untoward incidents. Candidates, political party leaders and workers were asked to strictly follow the Model Code of Conduct.

The sale of liquor will remain prohibited in Narasaraopet municipality and the seven mandals, covering 72 panchayats, from 5 p.m. on November 24 until the morning of November 27. Action will be taken against those violating the ban.

Lodge owners have been asked to share details of new guests with the police and report suspicious activities. Voters facing threats, inducements or obstruction, and anyone noticing violations or disturbances, should immediately inform the concerned police officials without delay, he said.

World.title: Government fears that its failures will be exposed internationally: Dipke
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) slammed the Central government after its co-founder Saurav Das was stopped at the Delhi airport and denied permission to travel to the U.K.

“Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi, and Mehul Choksi were never stopped from leaving India after committing massive scams, yet a 27-year-old legal journalist like Saurav Das was not allowed to travel when he was only going to attend a university conference (at Oxford) to speak about the CJP, and how Ambedkar and Gandhi’s philosophy shaped our movement,” Mr. Dipke told reporters at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

Mr. Dipke alleged that the government fears that its failures will be exposed internationally if young leaders share ground realities abroad.

U.P. elections

Mr. Dipke also clarified the party’s stand on the upcoming Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh and five other States. “The CJP will neither contest elections directly nor support any political party, but will push for elections to be fought on real youth issues such as education, healthcare, unemployment, semiconductors, renewable energy, technology, and transport, rather than religious polarisation or Mandir-Masjid politics,” he said.

Nagpur rally

Mr. Dipke and co-convener Ashutosh Ranka are expected to address a ‘Save Constitution’ rally in Nagpur on November 26 on the occasion of Constitution Day.

The CJP rally is slated to be held at Samvidhan Chowk. “We will approach all prominent personalities, social activists, representatives of organisations in Nagpur to be a part of the rally. Mr. Dipke and Mr. Ranka will speak on the values enshrined in our Constitution at the programme,” an organiser said.

“The rally will last almost two hours from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. on November 26. Thereafter, the two leaders will address those who gather there,” an organiser from Nagpur told The Hindu. The group has so far approached Satyapal Maharaj, a prominent social educator in the State. “We will firm up the entire schedule by Wednesday,” he said.

Earlier, in a post on X, Mr. Dipke said: “This Constitution Day, let us all come together and pledge to protect our democracy, uphold the values of our Constitution, and follow the path shown to us by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. See you all in Nagpur on November 26! #jaihind #jaibhim.” The announcement comes within days of Mr. Dipke’s visit to Goa where he targeted the BJP accusing the State government of land grab.

During the visit to Nagpur, Mr. Dipke will meet various prominent personalities, social activists, representatives of organisations, and citizens.

“Constitution Day is not merely a day for celebration; it is a day that reminds us of the values, rights, and duties enshrined in the Constitution. Therefore, the Cockroach Janta Party appeals to the citizens of Nagpur, youth, social activists, and those who believe in the Constitution, to participate in large numbers,” the party said in its appeal to the people of Nagpur.

World.title: Africa Cup title given back to Senegal after CAS rules against Morocco
World.content:
More than 10 months on from a chaotic, controversial final, Senegal is Africa's football champion once again.

Also read | CAS verdict on Senegal AFCON title appeal ‘expected end November’

Senegal won back the Africa Cup of Nations title in a legal fight on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned an earlier ruling which handed the trophy to Morocco.

Senegal won the Africa Cup on the field in Morocco in January and then lost it in a legal case in March because its players walked off the field in protest in second-half stoppage time.

CAS has now rejected that earlier ruling, based on referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's decision to let the game resume after the protest.

“Once again and forever, champions of Africa,” the Senegalese football federation posted on social media.

Tournament regulations said a team which refuses to play should be considered to have lost the game, but CAS said those rules were meant only for cases “when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently.”

Ndala “did not err in law” when he resumed the game and had “sole authority” to make that call, CAS said, adding its three judges were unanimous.

“The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension,” CAS said. “However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as arbitrary.' On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.”

Trouble on the field and in the stands

Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time, with chaos on the field and violent clashes in the stands. Even the ball boys were involved in scuffles as they tried to snatch towels that Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy was using to keep his gloves dry.

The result was overturned two months later as a 3-0 default win for Morocco by an appeals panel appointed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

Senegal beat AFCON host nation Morocco after a 15-minute delay in play. At 0-0, Senegal's team walked off the field to protest Morocco being awarded a penalty kick in the last minute of regulation time.

Match referee Ndala of Congo eventually allowed the game to restart, Morocco's penalty by Brahim Diaz was saved, and Senegal won in extra time.

The drama continued through the months of legal tussles. Senegal's players paraded with the trophy ahead of a game in March against Peru, even though Morocco was recognized as the champion at that point. Both teams played at the World Cup believing themselves to be the rightful champion of Africa.

Football laws vs. regulations

Senegal had the laws of the game on its side, and Morocco had the tournament regulations.

The laws of football state that referee decisions are final. CAS backed that position with its own “field of play” doctrine, that on-field calls by a referee generally can't be taken to the sports court.

“By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met — both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,” CAS said.

In the first legal case in March, CAF appeal judges cited AFCON tournament regulations that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorization of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition.”

The CAS judges heard evidence at a one-day hearing last month and the court promised a verdict by the end of November with a full written ruling of its judges setting out reasons for their decision.

CAS verdicts can be challenged at Switzerland's supreme court though only on limited procedural grounds.

The next men's AFCON starts in June co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania. Morocco will aim to end a wait for the title which now stands at 50 years.

Football fans in Senegal celebrate a win

"Senegal won on the pitch, and the court simply confirmed what we all already knew: We are the real champions of Africa,” said Mariama Sidibé, 35, an accountant in the capital, Dakar.

Sidibé said the dispute between Morocco and Senegal should now be left in the past.

“With all of this behind us, we should focus on what unites us now, and who knows, maybe Morocco can have its revenge on the field during the next AFCON this summer,” she said.

“At the end of the day Morocco and Senegal are brothers,” Sidibé added, referring to the countries' long shared close ties built on religion, trade and culture.

Sidi Sylla, a philosophy student at Dakar's main university, said the court's ruling was “not just a win for Senegal but for football in general.”

An historic decision

CAS rulings have stripped many athletes of Olympic medals for doping, but it's rare to overturn the result of a major football competition.

CAS refused to change the results of the 2019 Asian Cup, dismissing an appeal that the star striker on winning team Qatar shouldn't have been eligible for the tournament.

A lengthy legal battle over the same year's African Champions League final also ended with the original winner, a Tunisian club, taking the title after its opponent from Morocco refused to play on.

One notable CAS ruling on a team sport title came at the Winter Olympics in 2022. A doping case involving then-15-year-old Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva ended up with her disqualification, and the Russian team being dropped from gold to bronze in the team event.

World.title: Search intensified for six missing Andhra Pradesh fishermen off Odisha coast
World.content:
Six fishermen from Subbampeta village in Uppada of Kakinada district remain untraced after their fishing boat went missing in the sea off Paradip coast in Odisha. The fishermen ventured into the sea on November 4, 2026.

Even as a search operation has been launched in coordination with the Indian Navy and Coast Guard, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Tuesday instructed the official to intensify the efforts.

The missing fishermen have been identified as Sorada Kondal Rao, Gumpala Prakash, Tirri Narayana, Sorada Chinna, Merugu Narayana and Kandala Ramu. They set sail into the sea on a boat owned by Garikani Simhadri, along with another fishing boat, towards Paradip in Odisha on November 4. According to information provided by family members, the boats had ventured into waters around 200 km from Paradip, Agriculture and Fisheries Minister K. Atchannaidu said on Tuesday.

He said that the government had been coordinating with the Coast Guard and Indian Navy authorities to trace the missing fishermen. He appealed to the family members not to lose hope.

While one of the two boats returned on November 18, the family members of those on board the missing boat lodged a complaint with the Coast Guard’s toll-free number on November 19. The Fisheries Department wrote to the Coast Guard on the same night, seeking an immediate search operations.

Search operations were subsequently launched in coordination with the Coast Guard units at Kakinada and Paradip and the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Chennai.

The families told the officials that the missing boat had 1,500 litres of diesel and food supplies sufficient for 30 days. At a meeting convened by the Kakinada Coast Guard on Tuesday, officials sought detailed information from the families about the boat’s route and its last known location.

Officials are also examining the possibility of the boat drifting off course due to the impact of the cyclone and being carried towards the maritime waters of other countries. Information has been shared with Bangladesh and Myanmar, the Minister said.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu also reviewed the steps being taken to trace the missing boat.

Transponder switched off

The fishermen were carrying mobile phones, but they were switched off. The boat's transponder was also switched off, making it difficult to establish its location. Attempts to trace the vessel using GPS have not yielded any results yet, the officials said.

The Indian Coast Guard has deployed ships and a helicopter for the search operation along the coastal stretch near Paradip. Fisheries Department and Coast Guard officials have also met the families of the missing fishermen and apprised them of the situation.

World.title: SP declares candidates for five seats in U.P. Assembly polls
World.content:
The Samajwadi Party (SP) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announced five candidates for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls.

The party named Ashu Malik as candidate for the Saharanpur assembly seat, Nahid Hasan for Kairana, Mahboob Ali for Amroha , Jyoti Lodhi for Lalitpur and Umar Ali Khan for the Behat assembly seat.

In a related development, SP president Akhilesh Yadav urged Congress to understand public expectations and realities and engage in serious discussions to ensure victory for their alliance in most seats, describing the U.P. assembly election as a historic opportunity for secular parties to defeat the communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies and save the country from falling into the wrong hands and being ruined.

“This time is a historic opportunity when both of us secular parties can together defeat the communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies forever and save the country from falling into wrong hands and getting ruined. We want you and I to understand public expectations and realities and engage in serious discussions to ensure victory for our “alliance” in most seats. In all the seats we contest, our winning numbers should exceed the number of seats we fail to win. Only victory will make the division respectable, because winning seats brings respect,” he wrote on X.

Mr. Yadav asked Congress to mark all potential seats and send them to the SP.

“We will then discuss together which seat and which candidate is in a position to win. Based on our assessment and mathematical equation for victory, we may also inform the Congress about several winnable seats that they, for some reason, haven’t even considered,” he said.

“Our effort is that when big leaders meet, on all the seats, there should be discussion on the candidate of the ‘INDIA Alliance’ and not the candidate of Congress or the SP, and the thing which will give positive results would be that we present our candidate as the ‘PDA candidate’,” he added.

The SP chief claimed ground surveys have made it clear that the message has reached every city, neighborhood, street, and village that aggrieved and humiliated people from every community and every section of society across the state have rallied against the BJP, believing that the PDA will defeat the NDA and bring about change.

“The truth is, we don’t want seat sharing to be based on a “me-or-you” approach. We don’t want it to be a division, we want to call it ‘seat adjustment’. In seats with difficult equations, we will discuss at least two candidates together, choose the one with the most potential, and work together to ensure their victory. We don’t want alliance candidates to be imposed on each other, but rather, they should be decided by consensus,” he added.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh extends Employees Health Scheme facilities to retired transport staff
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Public Transport Department (APPTD) has advised its unit officers to step up awareness and facilitate enrolment of retired employees in the Employees Health Scheme (EHS), following the government’s permission to extend medical benefits to the staff who retired on or after January 1, 2020.

In a circular issued on Monday, the officials said the government had permitted the Chief Executive Officer of Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust to extend EHS facilities to retired APPTD employees on payment of the prescribed one-time subscription. The scheme also covers their spouses.

They said 10,249 employees had retired or ceased service between January 1, 2020, and October 2026, of whom 7,844 had enrolled in EHS so far.

Retired employees enrolled in the scheme are entitled to medical facilities at EHS-empanelled hospitals and APSRTC dispensaries. The department had also issued instructions earlier this year extending outpatient (OP) facilities at APSRTC dispensaries and hospitals. These include consultation, treatment, diagnostic investigations and supply of medicines for ailments covered under EHS.

As retired employees have been showing interest in joining the scheme, unit officers have been asked to conduct awareness programmes at every depot on the second Tuesday and Wednesday of each month to explain its benefits and facilitate enrolment.

Officers have also been instructed to collect the details of retired employees who have not yet enrolled, through a Google Form, and facilitate the generation of login credentials from Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust so that they can access the scheme’s benefits.

World.title: Rain likely across Andhra Pradesh for next three days
World.content:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has forecast that Andhra Pradesh may receive light to moderate showers for the next three days until November 27.

According to the IMD, there is a trough extending from the south-west Bay of Bengal to the west-central Bay of Bengal, which may bring cloudy conditions and rainfall across the State. Thunderstorms are also likely.

Many weather stations recorded moderate showers on Tuesday, November 24, as well. According to the real-time rainfall information from the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES), Kondapuram in SPSR Nellore district recorded 39.2 mm between 8.30 a.m. and 3 p.m. on Tuesday.

During this period, other stations that recorded rainfall include: Kothapatnam of Prakasam district: 34.4 mm, Kavali of SPSR Nellore district: 34.2 mm, Marella in Prakasam district: 33.5 mm, Tripuranthakam of Markapuram district: 27.9 mm, among others.

According to the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority, scattered light to moderate rainfall is likely in the districts of Parvathipuram-Manyam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Markapuram, Prakasam, Sri Sathya Sai, YSR Kadapa, Annamayya, Chittoor and Tirupati districts on Wednesday, November 25. Other districts may also receive scattered light rainfall.

The APSDMA has warned people against standing under trees during thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds.

World.title: Bi-weekly special trains between Tirupati and Vizag extended till January 29, 2027
World.content:
The Indian Railways will continue the bi-weekly special train services between Tirupati and Visakhapatnam until January 29, 2027.

The decision has been taken to clear the extra rush of passengers during the festival season, said South Coast Railway (SCoR) public relations officer Nusrat M. Mandrupkar.

Train No.08509 Tirupati-Visakhapatnam Special, which runs on Sundays and Thursdays, will be extended from November 29, 2026 to January 28, 2027.

Train No.08510 Visakhapatnam-Tirupati Special, which runs on Mondays and Fridays, will be extended from November 30 to January 29, 2027.

En route, these special trains will stop at Renigunta, Kadapa, Yerraguntla, Tadipatri, Gooty, Guntakal, Dhone, Betamcharla, Nandyal, Diguvametta, Markapur Road, Donakonda, Narsaraopet, Guntur, Vijayawada, Eluru, Rajahmundry and Samalkot stations, Ms. Nusrat said in a release on Tuesday.

World.title: PM Shehbaz assures KP governor of continued support to eliminate terrorism
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday assured KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi of all possible cooperation on behalf of the federal government for the complete eradication of terrorism, durable peace and the welfare of the public in the province.

The premier made these remarks as he met with Kundi in Islamabad on Tuesday, according to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

During the meeting, he said that the sacrifices of the security forces and KP police in the war against terrorism in the province would not go in vain.

The federal government would continue to “fully support the implementation of the decisions taken at the apex committee meeting to completely eliminate terrorism”, he was quoted as saying.

He reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to providing full support for the development of KP and the welfare of its people, saying that all possible resources would be mobilised to provide them with healthcare, education and other basic facilities, according to the PMO.

The premier directed that special attention be given to improving social development indicators in KP, including healthcare and education.

He said that attention would also be given to promoting sports facilities in the province and providing young people with opportunities for constructive activities, the PMO added.

Meanwhile, Governor Kundi briefed the prime minister on the ongoing efforts by himself and the KP Advisory Council to improve law and order in the province.

Separately, Kundi also met with President Asif Ali Zardari, a statement by the President’s Office said, where he briefed the president on the situation following Oct 11, particularly the security situation.

The meetings come weeks after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament amid protests by the opposition.

On Oct 22, PM Shehbaz also chaired a meeting of the federal apex committee in Peshawar. He had vowed to take tough decisions, while reaffirming the Centre’s commitment to bringing peace to terrorism-hit districts in the province.

Last week, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir also reaffirmed the security forces “unwavering resolve” to decisively eliminate terrorism and preserve peace and stability of KP in close coordination with law enforcement agencies.

World.title: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week
World.content:
Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper was struck for the second time in days on Tuesday, injuring 11 people, as the coalition fighting Houthis denounced a “terrorist attack”.

The building, which was also attacked last Thursday, is one of several high-profile targets hit since hostilities with the Houthis restarted in July.

Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence reported Tuesday’s injuries and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).

The image showed some damage to the building about halfway up the facade, similar to the impact from a strike on the same tower on Nov 19, which caused damage but no injuries.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the image was taken or the extent of the further damage from the latest strike.

Saudi Civil Defence said the 11 people injured included two Saudi citizens, four Egyptian nationals, three Nepalese nationals and two Indian nationals.

“Relevant authorities responded to the incident immediately, implementing all established protocols and measures for handling such situations, and taking the necessary steps to ensure the safety of lives and property,” the Arabic statement said.

“One of the towers in the financial centre was targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack,” coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a social media post, without naming the building.

Standing 385 metres high, the PIF tower is the most prominent landmark of King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD), a showcase for Saudi Arabia’s economic ambitions.

A witness told AFP that a vehicle fitted with a speaker had warned pedestrians in the area to take cover on Tuesday. No warning was sent to mobile phones about any threats to the capital.

Afterwards, police cars blocked some entrances to the gleaming financial district. With imposing skyscrapers, luxury shops and green spaces, the district also hosts the headquarters of the Saudi stock exchange along with multinationals such as Goldman Sachs.

An attack on the PIF is symbolic as the fund is driving efforts to diversify the oil-reliant Saudi economy — a project that has been complicated by the Middle East war and Houthi strikes.

A tower belonging to state oil giant Aramco in KAFD was hit earlier this month, while Riyadh’s international airport was repeatedly struck in October, with one attack killing 14 people.

The Houthis, who control much of western Yemen including the capital Sanaa, have been firing at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen’s frozen civil war reignited in July in a knock-on from the US-Iran war.

The attacks have caused the cancellation of most international flights to Riyadh, and forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including soccer’s AFC Asian Cup.

Such cowardly attacks undermine peace efforts: Pakistan

Pakistan strongly condemned the “terrorist attack carried out today by the Houthi militia”, the Foreign Office said.

In a statement, FO said Islamabad denounced “such cowardly attacks, which endanger civilians and civilian infrastructure, heighten regional tensions and undermine efforts to restore peace and stability”.

“Pakistan stands in full solidarity with Saudi Arabia in the face of these attacks. The Kingdom has every right to defend its territory and protect its citizens and residents,” FO affirmed.

It expressed Pakistan’s deep sympathies with those injured and their families and wished them swift and full recovery. FO also commended the Saudi authorities for their “prompt response” and the steps taken to protect lives and property.

Islamabad has condemned Houthi attacks repeatedly, including on international platforms, and termed them a grave violation of the kingdom’s sovereignty.

Pakistan and Riyadh have signed two defence pacts aimed at collective deterrence, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement that also includes Turkiye.

Under the Makkah Defence Alliance, Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish leaders met in Riyadh in October and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.

Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said later that month.

‘26 killed in Yemen attack’

On the ground in Yemen, the war has caused a major humanitarian crisis, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced from their homes since July.

The Houthis have seized swathes of territory, forcing forces aligned with the internationally recognised government to stage a major retreat this month.

The Saudi-led military coalition has been striking Houthi targets in the impoverished country.

On Tuesday, local officials said a coalition airstrike on buses and trucks killed 26 people in Lahj province. On the other hand, government forces blamed the Houthis for the attack.

As the conflict shows no sign of slowing, Britain sanctioned the Houthis and four of its top officials “for deliberately attempting to undermine stability” on Tuesday.

The measures include an asset freeze against the group and an asset freeze and travel ban on four figures, including security and intelligence head Abdul Hakim Hashem Ali al-Khaiwani, and interior affairs official Abdulkarim Amir al-Din Hussein al-Houthi.

The Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen in early 2015, after the Houthis had captured the capital Sanaa and sent the internationally recognised government fleeing to Aden.

The war left hundreds of thousands dead and triggered a humanitarian catastrophe before an uneasy ceasefire went into effect in 2022.

World.title: Govt reduces diesel price by Rs4 per litre, petrol by Re1 per litre
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre and that of diesel by Rs4 per litre, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs318 per litre and diesel at Rs353 per litre on Nov 25 (Wednesday).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Fazl decries ‘state siege’, claims prevented from attending Lahore event
World.content:
LAHORE: Police began removing barriers around Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s place of stay in Lahore on Tuesday evening, with the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief claiming he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

In a post at 10:40am, JUI-F said Fazl reached Lahore on Monday night and was scheduled to address lawyers today at a seminar at the invitation of the Lahore High Court Bar Association (LHCBA). However, due to police deployment, he was restricted from leaving his accommodation, JUI-F said.

JUI-F spokesperson Hafiz Ghazanfar Aziz said police began removing the hurdles by 7pm and informed Fazl that he was free to leave. However, the senior politician decided to stay in the city for the night.

Aziz condemned the alleged government action, calling it an attack on civil liberties and constitutional rights.

A city police officer, who spoke on condition of anonymity, also confirmed that police began “removing the barriers” by evening.

Meanwhile, a plea challenging the alleged “siege” of Fazl’s place of stay was filed in the Lahore High Court (LHC). On the other hand, the district administration also placed a three-day ban on public gatherings and “unlawful assemblies”.

In an earlier video message, the JUI-F chief alleged that he was under a “state siege” and that roadblocks and checkpoints across Lahore were preventing him from attending a multi-party seminar organised by the LHCBA.

Fazl thanked the bar association, its president and members for inviting him to address the seminar, but regretted that “state-imposed restrictions” had prevented him from attending in person.

He said the entire city had been “choked” by roadblocks and checkpoints, adding that peaceful citizens were being stopped from entering an environment of “intellectual discussion”.

“God willing, these sieges will break, these obstacles will be removed. Oppression never achieves permanence, but patience has always enjoyed permanence throughout history,” he said.

Fazl said his party had always worked for peace and had put its workers’ lives at risk for the country. He added that JUI-F did not need “a certificate of patriotism” from the rulers or any state institution.

“Neither from the rulers nor from any state institution have we come to obtain a certificate of loyalty to the homeland. In fact, I believe that perhaps we should be the ones issuing this certificate to people now. Their loyalties are questionable, whereas our loyalties are above all suspicion,” he said.

Claiming arrests of party workers and leaders in different areas, the JUI-F chief said his party would go ahead with its planned public conference in Sargodha on Nov 26.

He alleged that businesses were being shut down, shops and flour mills sealed, and party office-bearers arrested in Bhakkar, Mianwali, Khushab, Sargodha and its tehsils.

The JUI-F chief urged the public to make the gathering successful and demonstrate their commitment to freedom, constitutional supremacy, the rule of law and democracy.

“We are fighting the case of the public. We are fighting the case of Pakistan. We are fighting the case of this state,” he said.

Fazl alleged that the state had intensified its actions against JUI-F after the party exposed its role in matters concerning mineral resources in tribal areas.

He said his party was fighting for the rights of people across all provinces, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, Sindh and Punjab, as well as Gwadar.

“These are the property of the people, not the property of the federation, nor the property of any single powerful institution, and we will not allow it to be looted by anyone,” he said.

Fazl said his party would remain steadfast in its position and take the matter to its “logical conclusion”. He reiterated his gratitude to the LHCBA and regretted that restrictions had prevented him from addressing its members directly.

Opposition leaders Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI MNA Asad Qaiser, and veteran lawyer Ali Ahmed Kurd were among the participants of the LHCBA gathering, videos showed.

Plea filed in LHC against alleged ‘siege’

The plea against the alleged “siege” of Fazl’s accommodation was filed before the LHC by JUI-F lawyer Advocate Abrar Hussain.

It has yet to be fixed.

In his petition, the lawyer alleged that around 3,000 police personnel had been deployed outside Fazl’s residence, effectively confining him to his house.

The petitioner said he had sought a copy of the legal order authorising the detention or confinement of Fazl by police officials, but authorities did not share any such document.

He further alleged that police had also denied him permission to meet the JUI-F chief.

The petitioner requested the court to direct the police to lift the “siege” of Fazl’s residence.

In a statement, the party’s spokesperson warned that arrests of JUI-F workers in different cities on Monday, followed by the alleged deployment of a heavy police contingent outside the party chief’s residence, would have political consequences for the government.

He said arrests, roadblocks, the sealing of businesses and the registration of FIRs could not deter the party from its struggle. The JUI-F, he added, would continue its efforts for the supremacy of the Constitution and the protection of people’s rights.

Section 144 imposed in Lahore

Separately, Section 144 was imposed in Lahore for three days, from Nov 24 to 26, according to an order issued by the deputy commissioner, a copy of which is available with Dawn.

The order cited reports from law enforcement and intelligence agencies about a “serious and imminent threat” to public peace, security and the safety of life and property across Punjab, including Lahore, from militant and terrorist organisations and hostile intelligence agencies.

It said assemblies, rallies, gatherings, sit-ins, processions, demonstrations and public meetings could become targets for terrorist attacks, adding that the possibility of an untoward incident could not be ruled out.

The order also expressed apprehension that certain elements could engage in activities likely to lead to unlawful gatherings, disturb public order and pose security risks, potentially resulting in the loss of life and property or damage to critical infrastructure.

Under the restrictions, a complete ban has been imposed on the assembly of five or more people, processions and gatherings in any public place, street, road, highway, motorway or open space. The order also prohibits inciting people to participate in unlawful assemblies.

However, the restrictions will not apply to marriage ceremonies, funeral prayers, burial gatherings, prayers in mosques and churches, official duties of government and semi-government organisations, and courts of law, the order stated.

Fazl-govt rift

Tuesday’s developments came amid tensions between Fazl and the federal government, which have been ongoing since mid-October.

Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks against each other.

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

JUI-F spokesman Aslam Ghouri had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that the Maulana’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.

World.title: Huang’s return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop
World.content:
Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday as caution returned after Jensen Huang’s extraordinary return to AI giant Nvidia days after he was forced to resign, with investors bracing for further volatility in a key sector driving economic growth worldwide.

A day after Huang’s reinstatement as CEO drove Nvidia shares up more than 30 per cent, adding more than $900 billion to the firm’s market value, the euphoria dissipated as its stock lost almost 9pc mid-session.

Fellow tech behemoth and AI giant Anthropic also slumped, giving up around 12pc to $77.19, below its $83 price for last week’s IPO.

Monday aside, AI stocks had already sold off sharply throughout November on worries about profitability and the vast sums pumped into the sector.

Overall, the tech-heavy Nasdaq shed 2.3pc and the broader-based S&P 500 lost 1.1pc, while the Dow was just into the green around 1700 GMT (10pm PKT).

Europe’s main stock markets, which feature far fewer tech companies than their Asian and US rivals, finished a handful of percentage points lower after jumping on Monday in line with Wall Street.

Away from the tech sector, French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi revealed it would buy the US biopharma group Insmed, a specialist in respiratory treatments, for $41bn as it races to bulk up its development pipeline of new drugs.

Sanofi’s share price closed up almost 10pc following the news.

Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago over extramarital affairs, reportedly with an alleged Chinese spy as well as a senior Nvidia executive before US President Donald Trump noisily declared he should be brought back.

“Jensen’s return takes away one of the biggest unknowns hanging over the AI trade,” said Charu Chanana, an investment strategist at Saxo Markets.

“He is not just Nvidia’s CEO; he is arguably the biggest salesman for the entire AI ecosystem. His relationships with customers, suppliers and capital providers are difficult to replicate,” she said.

But “Jensen Huang alone cannot support the AI trade in the long term,” said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB.

“Nvidia’s stock price decline on Tuesday is to be expected after such a large rally in the previous session,” she added.

Analysts were in broad agreement that Huang’s return did not mean an end to probes or the uncertainty that has clouded the AI trade for six months.

The company remains under scrutiny from investigators including at the FBI and on Capitol Hill for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia’s top-line chips.

Monday’s Wall Street surge had propelled Asian markets earlier on Tuesday, with Taipei surging 9pc higher as chip titans TSMC and MediaTek added nearly 10pc each.

Seoul piled on more than 6pc thanks to strong gains in fellow chip giants SK Hynix and Samsung, and Tokyo rose nearly 4pc, led by a 12.5pc jump for semiconductor tester Advantest.

World.title: Pakistan Customs seizes nearly 1kg of 'Multan-bound' marijuana in Karachi
World.content:
The Collectorate of Customs (CoC) (airports) in Karachi foiled a narcotics smuggling attempt and seized 900 grams of marijuana during routine scanning at the International Mail Office (IMO), Pakistan Customs said on Tuesday.

During routine scanning, Customs staff intercepted a “suspicious parcel” originating from Canada’s Ontario and destined for Multan, the statement said.

“The parcel was declared as ‘Books (Gift)’. However, physical examination by Preventive Officer Muhammad Shah Jahan revealed boxes of chocolates and cereals, within which the 900 grams of marijuana was concealed,” the press release said.

The seized marijuana was valued at approximately Rs. 27.25 million, Pakistan Customs said.

The consignment was shifted to the Directorate of Enforcement and Compliance (DEC) headquarters at Jinnah International Airport for further necessary proceedings.

A first information report (FIR) has been registered in the case and further legal proceedings were underway, Pakistan Customs said.

“Reflecting continued vigilance, Pakistan Customs remains committed to curbing narcotics smuggling and safeguarding public welfare.”

World.title: Rohail Nazir's fifty books Asia Cup Rising Stars semi-finals spot for Pakistan Shaheens
World.content:
An unbeaten half-century by Rohail Nazir, followed by a devastating bowling display, helped Pakistan Shaheens defeat Nepal by 96 runs in their final Group ‘B’ match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars at the University of Doha for Science and Technology on Tuesday.

The defending champions remained unbeaten in the tournament, winning all three of their group matches to qualify for the semi-finals, where they will face Bangladesh A on Nov 27.

Batting first, Pakistan Shaheens were in trouble at 66-6 in 16.5 overs before wicket-keeper-batter Rohail steadied the innings with an unbeaten 64 off 83 balls, hitting four fours and three sixes.

After Hasan Nawaz fell for 28 off 59 balls, leaving the Shaheens at 88-7, Rohail added 70 runs for the eighth wicket with Ahmed Daniyal, who scored 16 off 35 balls, to help his side reach 168 before being bowled out in 42 overs.

For Nepal, Rashid Khan claimed five wickets for 39 runs, while Abhishesh Gautam took two.

Nepal’s chase got off to a disastrous start as Muhammad Imran and Mohammad Hasnain reduced them to 15-4 inside six overs. Hasnain struck twice in successive deliveries to dismiss Ishan Pandey and Lokesh Bam without scoring.

Left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqim then claimed three wickets as Nepal slumped to 59-9. Mayan Yadav offered some resistance with a top score of 41 off 50 balls but was trapped leg-before by Maaz Sadaqat as Nepal were dismissed for 72 in 17.3 overs.

Hasnain and Sufyan took three wickets each for 21 and 17 runs respectively, while Imran claimed two for 29.

Rohail was named player of the match for his match-winning innings.

World.title: Govt selects consortium of 3 foreign banks for $500m finance facility backed by MIGA
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The government on Tuesday selected a consortium of three foreign banks to arrange a $500 million trade finance facility, backed by the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), a member of the World Bank Group.

“Following a competitive selection process and receipt of bids from nine international financial institutions, the Finance Division, Government of Pakistan, has selected the following banks as financing partners for the facility,” the Ministry of Finance said in a statement.

The banks included Commerzbank, JP Morgan and Standard Chartered Bank. It added that this facility opened new avenues for international financing.

According to the ministry, the decision was taken in a virtual meeting held by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb with the senior leadership of a consortium of international banks and representatives of the agency.

The banks were selected on the basis of the most competitive financing terms offered to the government, it said.

“The one-year facility, renewable on a rolling 1+1+1 basis, will support the financing of essential imports and trade-related expenditures,” the statement said.

It noted that the transaction marked the government’s first-ever credit enhancement transaction with MIGA under its Trade Finance programme, while also representing the first-ever participation of Commerzbank and JP Morgan in commercial lending to the government.

“The strong response and participation from international financial institutions reflect growing confidence in Pakistan’s improving economic outlook and progress towards sustainable growth,” the ministry said, expressing the government’s appreciation for the interest shown by all participating institutions and its gratitude “for their time, effort and engagement throughout the process”.

It said the transaction marked an important step towards “mobilising private international capital through multilateral risk-mitigation instruments, diversifying external financing sources and exploring innovative financing structures, while maintaining prudent debt management and fiscal responsibility”.

The ministry said the government would work closely with MIGA and the selected banks to advance the transaction towards its timely execution, looking forward to building strong and lasting relationships.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.
